title: Genesis 1:1
text:
The beginning; of the creation here spoken of. 
 
  Created; brought into being out of nothing. 
 
  The heaven and the earth; the matter out of which these were afterwards formed. 
 
The existence, wisdom, and greatness of God are shown by the things which he has made, even his eternal power and godhead; so that those who see these things and yet do not adore him, are without excuse.  Romans 1:20

title: Genesis 1:2
text:
Without form; tha materials existed, but the different kinds had not been separated or put into shape. 
 
  Void; empty, and destitute of the vegetation and living creatures which were afterwards brought forth.  How long the earth remained so, God has not revealed, and we do not know. 
 
  The deep; the abyss of waters. 
 
  Moved; in the original, brooded or hovered over the mass of matter, and thus prepared it for being brought into an orderly form, and for bringing forth, at the command of God, various productions.

title: Genesis 1:3
text: Light exists independently of the sun, as in electricity, lightning, and fire.  God caused the light to shine out of darkness, and he can shine into dark hearts, and give them the light of the knowledge of his glory in the face of Jesus Christ.   II Corinthians 4:6

title: Genesis 1:6
text: Firmament; in the original, expanse; namely, that above and around the earth, which we call sky.

title: Genesis 1:9
text: Waters--dry land; the earth had before been covered with water; but now the water and the dry land were separated.

title: Genesis 1:10
text: In separating and combining the elements, assigning to each its appropriate place, and upholding it there, no less really than in its creation, God showed his infinite power, wisdom, and goodness.  He spake, and it was done; he commanded, and it stood fast.  Psalms 33:9 Hebrews 1:3

title: Genesis 1:11
text: Yielding seed; to perpetuate by natural growth the same kind.

title: Genesis 1:12
text: In the continuance of the great law which God at first gave, that each seed should produce its kind in all future time, we have evidence that he sees and governs throughout the vegetable creation--is of one mind, and none can turn him.   Job 23:13 Isaiah 46:10

title: Genesis 1:14
text:
vv. 14-19 
 
  Lights; light and heat had been made before, on the first day,  Genesis 1:3-5 ; but now there were two great bodies in the heavens to occasion, through their motions and those of the earth, day and night, summer and winter, seed-time, and harvest.

title: Genesis 1:18
text: The sun, moon, and stars are bright manifestations of the wisdom, power, and goodness of God.  We can see and enjoy them without being able to understand their nature, or how they produce their effects.  So we can believe truths, and enjoy the benefits of faith, without comprehending how those truths exist, are related, or operate so usefully on us.

title: Genesis 1:20
text:
Life; vegetable life had been given before,  Genesis 1:11 Genesis 1:12 ; but now a higher kind of life, that of animals, was given. 
 
  Fowl that may fly; better, let fowl fly.  The fowl, as well as the beasts, were formed out of the ground.   Genesis 2:19 .

title: Genesis 1:21
text: Whales; the original word denotes the large sea animals generally-- sea-monsters.

title: Genesis 1:24
text: Cattle-creeping thing-beast of the earth; the usual Hebrew division of land animals.  The beast of the earth denotes wild beasts, and the creeping thing all small animals that move with a low or gliding motion, as moles, serpents, etc.

title: Genesis 1:26
text:
Us; such are the nature and manifestations of God, that he can properly speak of himself as I or we, me or us; thus our Saviour said, We will come unto him, and make our abode with him,   John 14:23 . 
 
  Our image-our likeness; like his Creator, a rational spirit, exercising dominion.

title: Genesis 1:28
text: The fear of man manifested by fishes, fowls, and beasts, testifies to his dignity as the representative of his Maker; and by yielding to him to whom God gave dominion, they acknowledge God's authority, and thus honor him.  They also suffer in consequence of man's sin.  Genesis 6:7 Romans 8:20

title: Genesis 1:29
text:
vv. 29-30 
 
  Every herb bearing seed-every green herb; God gives to man for his food the fruits and seed-bearing plants, such as wheat, pulse, etc.; leaving to the cattle the green herbage.

title: Genesis 1:31
text:
Very good; each part is separately pronounced good, but the whole is very good, because it is only in the whole that each part finds its perfection. 
 
All that God does is very good; like its Author, perfect.  Nothing could be better; and in our treating all things according to his will there is great reward.

title: Genesis 2:1
text: Thus; as described in the previous chapter.

title: Genesis 2:2
text: Rested; not in the sense of weariness, or ease from fatigue; God is never weary.  Isaiah 40:28 .  But he ceased from the work of the six days.  He rested, as men should, after six days of labor; and as the friends of God, who rightly understand their duty, will.  Having made man in his own image, he now sets him an example.

title: Genesis 2:3
text:
The seventh day; that which succeeds the six working days; and which was made to be a day of rest from secular employments and of devotion to religious duties. 
 
  Sanctified it; set it apart from other days for sacred employments. 
 
As God made one day in seven for rest and spiritual duties, set it apart to be devoted not to secular but to sacred employments, and enforced the observance of it by his own example and his command, it is manifestly his will that men should regard it; and no man in this respect does his will who does not remember the Sabbath-day to keep it holy.

title: Genesis 2:4
text:
"These are the generations;" this expression is always prefixed to the account to which it belongs.   Genesis 5:1 Genesis 10:1 Genesis 11:10 Genesis 25:12 Genesis 25:19   Genesis 36:1 Genesis 37:1   Here it introduces a second further account of the creation, containing important particulars which could not be brought into the preceding narrative without interrupting its orderly plan. 
 
  Lord; in the original, Jehovah.  This is the first time this word is used in the Bible.  It is the peculiar name of Him, who is, and was, and is to come, the Almighty; and implies eternal, independent, unchanging self-existence, and infinite perfection. 
 
When the word Lord in the Bible is printed in small capitals, it is in the Hebrew, JEHOVAH.

title: Genesis 2:5
text: Every plant-before it was in the earth-every herb-before it grew; many prefer to render the original, "And no plant of the field was yet in the earth, and no herb of the field yet grew," the sacred writer again commencing with the time when the earth was void.

title: Genesis 2:7
text:
Formed man;  Genesis 1:1 Hebrews 1:1-13:25  was not born as men now are, and did not grow up gradually; but as other things were formed by the power of God at once, he was created full-grown and perfect. 
 
As the body of man was at first formed from the dust, and all our bodies must soon return to dust, our chief concern should be for the soul; that it may be fitted, when it leaves the body, to enter into the presence and enjoy the favor of God.

title: Genesis 2:8
text: Eden; a country east or north-east of Palestine, through which flowed the rivers Tigris and Euphrates.

title: Genesis 2:9
text:
The tree of life; whose fruit would be to man, if obedient, a pledge of endless life. 
 
  Tree of knowledge; by man's treatment of which his character would be known; and concerning which he knew by express revelation the will of God: by obeying that will, he would know good and good only; and by disobeying, he would know evil, and transmit it to his posterity.

title: Genesis 2:10
text: Was parted-four heads; was divided into four head streams.  But whether we are to reckon downward from Eden, so that the garden lay at their common source, or upward, so that it lay below their junction, is not agreed.

title: Genesis 2:13
text: Ethiopia; in the Hebrew, Cush; not the Ethipia in Africa, but a country in Asia, inhabited by descendants of Cush the son of Ham, and father of Nimrod.   Genesis 10:6 Genesis 10:8

title: Genesis 2:14
text:
Hiddekel; the river Tigris, which empties into the Euphrates. 
 
  Euphrates; a river which rises in America and flows south into the Persian Gulf.

title: Genesis 2:15
text:
Dress; cultivate 
 
Diligence in business during the six working days, as well as rest from it on the Sabbath, was needful to man in a state of innocence.  He was made for employment; and no man can indulge in idleness or sloth, without committing sin.

title: Genesis 2:16
text: Of every tree; except the tree of knowledge,  Genesis 2:17 .

title: Genesis 2:17
text:
Thou shalt not eat of it; this was a test of his obedience to the known will of God. 
 
  Surely die; in the original, dying thou shalt die.  He would lose the moral image and the favor of God; become mortal and exposed to endless sinfulness and misery.

title: Genesis 2:18
text:
Alone; without a human companion. 
 
  Meet for him; suited to his nature, condition, and wants. 
 
As God has told us that it is not good for man to live unmarried, those who contend that it is best for ministers of the gospel to live unmarried, set up their wisdom in opposition to his, deprive themselves of many blessings, and set an evil example to their fellow-men.

title: Genesis 2:23
text:
Woman--man; in Hebrew, man is Ish; woman, Isha, the feminine of man. 
 
The manner in which, and the object for which woman was made, show that the husband and wife should love each other with tender affection; cultivate union of views, interest, and effort; and mutually seek each other's highest good.

title: Genesis 2:24
text:
Therefore; on account of her likeness to man, her suitableness to be his companion, the appointment of God with regard to it, and the mutual affection which he would cause to subsist between them. 
 
  One flesh; united in bonds more tender and strong than those which unite relatives by birth. 
 
Marriage, according to the will of God, is a union for life of one man with one woman, and with one only; and the fact that it is a divine institution, shows that men should enter into it for the glory of God in the promotion of their own happiness and usefulness.

title: Genesis 2:25
text: Not ashamed; shame is the fruit of sin, and as they had never sinned, they felt none of its evil.  How long they continued in this state, God has not told us; and we do not know.

title: Genesis 3:1
text:
Subtle; cunning, deceitful. 
 
  He; the serpent, or Satan speaking by him. 
 
The great means of safety to man is continued hearty belief in the truth of God's declarations.  Hence Satan tries to prevent this, that by their own voluntary transgressions, he may destroy them.

title: Genesis 3:4
text:
Ye shall not--die; this is the first lie recorded in the Bible. Satan was its author, and he is justly called the father of lies.  John 8:44  
 
Satan tries to make men disbelieve God's declarations, in order to lead them to break his commands.  Liars resemble Satan, do his work, and will partake of his torment.   Revelation of John 21:8

title: Genesis 3:5
text: Be as gods; be greatly exalted in knowledge, and able to choose for yourselves between good and evil.

title: Genesis 3:6
text:
To make one wise; the tempter occasion from the name of the tree, to deceive her into the idea that it would make her wise in such a way as greatly to advance her dignity and blessedness. 
 
  She took of the fruit; showing that she believed Satan rather than God.

title: Genesis 3:7
text:
Were opened; but in an opposite sense from that of the tempter. They were opened to see their shame and ruin, and to understand from their own sad experience the difference between good and evil.  Compare  Genesis 3:22 . 
 
  Knew that they were naked; experienced shame from their nakedness as the fruit of sin.

title: Genesis 3:8
text: Hid themselves; through conscious guilt, and fearful expectation of coming evil.

title: Genesis 3:9
text: Sin makes men ashamed of themselves, afraid of God, and desirous to escape his notice.  But their efforts to hide themselves or their sins are vain, and only show the reality of their guilt and the dreadfulness of their condition.

title: Genesis 3:11
text: Who told thee; how didst thou become ashamed and fearful?  This was asked, not for the information of God, but for the conviction of Adam.

title: Genesis 3:12
text: She gave me; this was true, but it did not excuse him.

title: Genesis 3:13
text:
Beguiled; deceived. 
 
Impenitent men try to cast the blame of their sins on others; while those who are penitent, take it to themselves.   Luke 15:21

title: Genesis 3:14
text:
The serpent; the instrument through which Satan acted. 
 
  Cursed; he would be greatly degraded, and detested.

title: Genesis 3:15
text:
It; the seed of the woman, or, as it might be rendered, He, referring especially to Christ, who in due time would come to destroy the works of the devil. 1Jo 3.8 
 
  Bruise thy head; overcome him and destroy his power.  Bruise his heel; inflict upon him temporary evil.

title: Genesis 3:16
text:
And thy conception; in thy conception. 
 
  Thy desire--to thy husband; he should control her, and she subject to him.

title: Genesis 3:17
text: Duty, safety, and interest sometimes require us to refuse compliance with the wishes of our dearest friends; and if we do not, we shall bring upon ourselves a dreadful curse.

title: Genesis 3:18
text: The herb of the field; for which he must laboriously toil, instead of living any longer in paradise.

title: Genesis 3:19
text: The evil of sin surpasses all finite conception.  Every instance of death is an evidence of its power, and of the truth of God.  When the word hath gone out of his mouth, it standeth for ever.  All who disbelieve his known declarations, demonstrated in the universal mortality of men, are without excuse.

title: Genesis 3:20
text: Eve; meaning life.

title: Genesis 3:21
text:
Skins; supposed to be of animals offered in sacrifice to God, pointing forward to the great atoning sacrifice of Christ, the promised Conqueror of Satan.  Throgh faith in Christ, God would forgive men, sanctify, and save them. 
 
When our first parents had vainly endeavored to hide their shame by a covering of their own invention, God, in his great mercy, provided for them a suitable covering.  This truly shadows forth the righteousness which God gives through faith in Christ, to all who humbly ask him for it, with a hearty acknowledgement of the worthlessness of their own righteousness.

title: Genesis 3:22
text: One of us;  Genesis 1:1  Man had vainly attempted to elevate and bless himself, by taking his own way, in compliance with Satan's temptation, and in opposition to the known will of God; thus he knew good and evil, by losing the one and suffering the other.

title: Genesis 3:24
text:
Cherubim; this was some visible appearance of celestial beings, but its exact nature is unknown. 
 
There is nothing in the nature of holiness which is a security against apostasy and ruin.  Those that are perfectly holy may commit sin; and thus change their character, condition, and prospects for eternity.

title: Genesis 4:1
text:
Cain; meaning possession. 
 
  A man; man-child, a son. 
 
  From the Lord; that is, by intercession with him, and with his aid. Some suppose she thought this son to be the promised Seed, who should bruise the serpent's head.

title: Genesis 4:2
text: Abel; signifying vanity.

title: Genesis 4:3
text: In process of time; probably at the end of some stated time appointed to worship God.

title: Genesis 4:4
text:
Had respect; received it with favor, and showed that he accepted it; because it pointed forward to the atoning blood of Christ, and showed faith in what God had revealed concerning him.  Genesis 3:15 Genesis 3:21 Hebrews 11:4  
 
In the declaration that the seed of the woman should bruise the serpent's head, and in the appointment of sacrifices,  Genesis 3:15 Genesis 3:21 , God revealed the certainty of a coming Saviour, and laid a foundation for faith, by the exercise of which men might be justified, and for Christ's sake be accepted as righteous.   Hebrews 11:4

title: Genesis 4:5
text:
Had not respect; he did not accept it.  It was not an expression of faith in a coming Saviour, and was not offered with a right spirit. 
 
  His countenance fell; he looked sad, angry, and sullen. 
 
Faith in what God has revealed with regard to the Redeemer, and the way of life through him, is, to those who know this revelation, essential to acceptable worship.  He that rejects the Son rejects also the Father, and will be rejected by him.   John 15:23 I John 2:23

title: Genesis 4:7
text:
Sin lieth at the door; according to some, crouched at thy door, like a beast of prey, ready to destroy thee; according to others, a sin-offering (such as I require) lieth at the door, by offering which in a right spirit, thou mayest gain my favor. 
 
  Thou shalt rule over him; Cain, being the eldest son according to his birthright would have preeminence over Abel.

title: Genesis 4:9
text:
My brother's keeper; one whose business it is to watch over and take care of him. 
 
Sins have a close connection, and the commission of one leads to the commission of others.  He who will commit murder will also tell lies.

title: Genesis 4:10
text: Blood crieth; calleth for the punishment of him who shed it.

title: Genesis 4:11
text: From the earth; or ground, which would not yield him its increase as before, and would thus testify against his sin.

title: Genesis 4:12
text: A fugitive--a vagabond; driven from God's presence and the home of Adam.   Genesis 4:16 .

title: Genesis 4:14
text:
Face of the earth; the land where he had dwelt. 
 
  From thy face; from the place where God manifested his special presence, he would be expelled. 
 
  Shall slay me; he knew they would think that he deserved to die for killing his brother, and was afraid they would treat him accordingly. 
 
A murderer feels that he deserves to die; and when he is put to death, often acknowledges that it is just.

title: Genesis 4:15
text:
Seven-fold; he shall be more severly punished. 
 
  Set a mark upon Cain; more literally, appointed to Cain a sign, that is, some miraculous token.  He was to live a vagabond, as a monument of the guilt of murder and of the wrath of God against it.

title: Genesis 4:16
text: Land of Nod; that is, of vagrancy.

title: Genesis 4:17
text: His wife; it is supposed that Cain was married before he murdered Abel.

title: Genesis 4:19
text: Two wives; this is the first instance mentioned of a violation of the law of marriage, by taking more than one wife.  It shows that men had become very corrupt, and this course tended to make them worse.

title: Genesis 4:20
text: The father; the inventor of a business, or he who makes great improvements in it, is, in Hebrew, called the father of those who pursue it.

title: Genesis 4:22
text: Instructor--and iron; or, forger of every instrument of brass and iron.

title: Genesis 4:24
text: Lamech seventy and seven; God had said,   Genesis 4:15 , that should any one kill Cain, his death sould be avenged seven-fold; and Lamech says his would be avenged seventy and seven; implying that in his own estimation he was much less guilty than Cain; and that he who should kill him, would be punished much more severely than he who should kill Cain.

title: Genesis 4:25
text: Seth; meaning appointed or substituted in place of Abel.

title: Genesis 4:26
text:
To call upon the name of the Lord; they separated themselves from the wicked, maintained the public worship of God, and were thus recognized as his visible people.  It is generally thought that they were "the sons of God," mentioned in  Genesis 6:2 . 
 
If men would possess the character and receive the reward of God's people, they must separate themselves from his enemies, publicly maintain his worship, and show themselves to be his friends.  Mark 8:38 John 14:21 I Corinthians 7:19 II Corinthians 6:17

title: Genesis 5:1
text: Book of the generations; history of Adam and his posterity.

title: Genesis 5:2
text: Their name Adam; that is, man.

title: Genesis 5:3
text: In his own likeness; a human being, and depraved; who, without the renewing grace of God, would never be holy, but would live and die in sin.

title: Genesis 5:24
text:
Walked with God; was cordially reconciled to him,  Amos 3:3 ; sought his guidance, believed his declarations, obeyed his commands, and enjoyed his presence. 
 
  Was not; was not found on the earth; nor did he die, but God took him to heaven.   Hebrews 11:5 . 
 
To walk with God is the highest duty, the greatest honor, excellence, and blessedness of man.   Jude 1:14 Jude 1:15 Hebrews 11:5-6

title: Genesis 5:27
text: He died; in the year after the flood.

title: Genesis 5:29
text:
Noah; signifying rest; expressive of the hope and expectation that he would be a great blessing. 
 
Parents often hope for great comfort from their children; and if children are pious, especially if they become preachers of righteousness, and are instrumental in the salvation of men, parents have reason to rejoice with great joy.

title: Genesis 5:31
text: He died; five years before the flood.

title: Genesis 5:32
text: Japheth;  he is generally thought to have been the elder; see note to  Genesis 10:21 ; but Shem is mentioned first, because from him would descend the Messiah.

title: Genesis 6:2
text:
Sons of God; his visible worshippers, who had remained in the home of Adam. 
 
  Of men; the openly wicked, who seem to have belonged to Cain's descendants.  Genesis 4:16  
 
  All which they chose; being governed in this matter by their own wills, not by the will of God. 
 
Intimate connections with the wicked are sources of great moral corruption and danger.

title: Genesis 6:3
text:
Strive with man; to bring him to repentance and salvation. 
 
  Is flesh; corrupt,  John 3:6  
 
  A hundred and twenty years; so long would God wait before he would destroy the world.

title: Genesis 6:4
text:
Giants; men of great stature and wickedness. 
 
  Men of renown; famous for their deeds of rapine.

title: Genesis 6:6
text: Repented the Lord--grieved him; he would change his conduct towards men, as men change their conduct when sorry for what they have done; and instead of continuing them on the earth and granting them his favors, as he had done, he would destroy them.

title: Genesis 6:7
text:
The fear of man manifested by fishes, fowls, and beasts, testifies to his dignity as the representative of his Maker and by yielding to him to whom God gave dominion, they acknowledge God's authority, and thus honor him.  They also suffer in consequence of man's sin.  Genesis 6:7 Romans 8:20  
 
When God, instead of preserving and blessing men, turns against and destroys them, he is said in the Bible to repent, because he changes his conduct as men do when they repent.  Not that he alters his purposes, or does what he did not always intend to do.  In this sense he is of one mind, and none can turn him,  Job 23:13 ; he is not a man that he should lie, nor the son of man that he should repent.  Numbers 23:19   There is no contradiction in these texts; they refer to different things, and express different truths.  In studying the Bible, we should not regard simply the sound of the words, but become acquainted with and believe their meaning.  In no other way can we receive benefit from them.

title: Genesis 6:8
text: Grace; favor, as being a righteous man.

title: Genesis 6:9
text:
Perfect; not in the sense of being sinless; but in the sense of being sincere, upright, and truly devoted to God. 
 
The cause of the difference between a good man and the openly wicked is, not their natural disposition, but divine grace; and the fruits of this grace are piety towards God, integrity, uprightness, and benevolence towards men.

title: Genesis 6:12
text: The corruption of men proceeds from themselves; they are the authors of all their wickedness, and the cause of their own ruin.  Proverbs 1:31 Hosea 13:9 James 1:14

title: Genesis 6:14
text: Gopher; a species of resinous wood; perhaps the cypress.

title: Genesis 6:15
text:
Length; about four hundred and fifty feet. 
 
  Breadth; seventy-five feet. 
 
  Height; forty-five feet: proportions according to which the best ships are now built.

title: Genesis 6:16
text: And in a cubit shalt thou finish it above; literally, unto a cubit shalt thou finish it above; that is, thou shalt make it to the height of a cubit.  Some understand these words of the roof of the ark, which was to have a cubit's slope from the central line outwards.  But they more naturally refer to the windows.  The horizontal width of the window is not given; this may have greatly exceeded its height.

title: Genesis 6:18
text: My covenant; his engagement for the preservation of Noah and his family, when the rest of the world should be destroyed.

title: Genesis 6:22
text: That faith in God which he accepts, and which is the means of justification and salvation, leads those who exercise it to obey his commands.

title: Genesis 7:1
text: It is not necessary for a man to be wicked because others around him are wicked.  Any one may, if he will, be righteous, even in the midst of abounding iniquity.  And every one whom God sees to be righteous through faith, will be saved when the wicked are destroyed.

title: Genesis 7:2
text: Clean beast; suitable for sacrifice.

title: Genesis 7:5
text: If men would be saved, they must not only believe God's declarations, but also make it their great object to obey all his commands.

title: Genesis 7:10
text: After seven days; on the seventh day it began to rain.

title: Genesis 7:11
text:
Second month; the year began late in september; and the second month, called Marchesvan answered to the last part of October and the first part of November. 
 
  Fountains of the great deep--windows of heaven; the waters rushed up from the sea, and poured down from the heavens.

title: Genesis 7:15
text: God has power not only over men, but also over beasts, and all the works of his hands.  He can influence, direct, and control them, as seemeth him good.

title: Genesis 7:16
text: Those who believe God's declarations and obey his commands, will receive his effectual protection and care.

title: Genesis 7:20
text:
Fifteen cubits; about twenty-two and a half feet. 
 
  Upward; above the highest land.

title: Genesis 7:21
text: Men who know the declarations of God but do not believe them, will be convinced of their truth by their fulfilment; and when he undertakes to punish, there is no possibility of escape.

title: Genesis 7:24
text: A hundred and fifty days; so long, it is supposed, the waters did not sensibly abate.

title: Genesis 8:1
text:
Remembered; showed that he remembered. 
 
  Assuaged; began to abate. 
 
However great or long-continued the trials of God's poeple, he never forgets them; nor does he continue those trials any longer than will promote his glory and their highest good.  Let them place impicit confidence in him; in due time all his promises will be fully accomplished.

title: Genesis 8:3
text: Hundred and fifty days; from the time it began to rain.

title: Genesis 8:4
text:
Seventy month; called Nisan, and answering to the last part of March and the first part of April. 
 
  Mountains of Ararat; in Armenia.

title: Genesis 8:5
text: Tenth month; called Thammuz, and answering to the last part of June and the first part of July.

title: Genesis 8:6
text: Forty days; after the mountains were first seen.

title: Genesis 8:7
text: A raven; which, being an unclean bird, could feed on dead bodies.

title: Genesis 8:9
text: Found no rest; though the tops of some mountains could be seen, these were not the regions which the dove would visit.

title: Genesis 8:12
text: In the days of Noah, as at the creation and in the days of Adam, time was divided into weeks or periods of seven days; marked, not by the revolutions of heavenly bodies, as were months and years, but by the return of the Sabbath, a day of rest from secular, and of devotion to sacred duties.  This division of time was carried into all parts of the world, and has been observed by the people of God in all ages.

title: Genesis 8:13
text: The first month; called Tisri, and answering to the last part of September and the first part of October. This was the first month of the civil year.  Afterwards, in the days of Moses the ecclesiastical year of the Jews began in the month of Abib or Nisan, answering to the last part of March and the first part of April.

title: Genesis 8:14
text: The seven and twentieth day; reckoning the day he entered and the day he left, this was twelve months and eleven days from the time the fountains of the great deep were broken up, and the windows of heaven opened.   Genesis 7:11   Theirs were lunar months, measured by the changes of the moon.  Six of these consisted of thirty days each and six of twenty-nine.  Twelve months and eleven days would therefore make a solar year, or three hundred and sixty-five days.

title: Genesis 8:18
text: As soon as trials have accomplished God's wise and benevolent ends, he delights to deliver his people from them, and to fill their hearts with joy.

title: Genesis 8:20
text:
Altar; an elevated place on which to offer sacrifices. 
 
  Burnt-offerings; offerings that were consumed by fire; expressive of the conviction of the offerers, that they, as sinners, deserved to be consumed; also of their gratitude for sparing mercy, their need of pardoning grace, and their hope of obtaining it, through the sacrifice of Christ as a propitiation for the sins of the world.  Ephesians 5:2 Hebrews 9:14 I John 2:2

title: Genesis 8:21
text:
A sweet savor; God was pleased with, and accepted the offering, as a suitable expression of a penitent, believing, and grateful heart. 
 
  Said in his heart; determined, and made know his determination. 
 
  Not again curse the ground; by bringing upon it a flood. 
 
  For; though men would continue to be naturally as wicked after the flood as before, yet God would not again interrupt the regular course of the seasons, and of day and night, to the end of time. 
 
Whatever destruction God brings upon the wicked, and however extensively iT may be known, without the grace of God those who survive will continue to be wicked; neither judgments nor mercies will lead them to love and obey God.

title: Genesis 8:22
text: The regular return of day and night, summer and winter, seed-time and harvest, is a constant memorial of the truth of Jehovah; that when the word hath gone out of his mouth it standeth for ever.  Numbers 23:19 Matthew 24:35

title: Genesis 9:1
text: With the increase of the human family by the marriage of one man with one woman, God is well pleased, that all parts of the earth may be inhabited, cultivated, and filled with his praise.

title: Genesis 9:2
text: Into your hand; they shall be subject to you, to be used for your benefit.

title: Genesis 9:3
text:
Every moving thing; that is good to eat. 
 
The fear of man in beasts, birds, and fishes, is evidence of the truth and goodness of God.  Without his permission we should have no right to use them for food; and all wanton destruction of them, or putting them to pain, is sinful.

title: Genesis 9:4
text: The blood--shall ye not eat; it must not be eaten, as it was to typify the blood which was to be offered to God as an atonement for the sins of men.

title: Genesis 9:5
text:
At the hand of every beast will I require it; this was to impress upon them the sacredness of human life, and thus prevent one man from killing another.  Exodus 21:28-29  
 
  Brother; he who slays a man slays his brother, since the whole human family are brethren of one blood.

title: Genesis 9:6
text:
His blood be shed; the murderer of man should by man be put to death.  This was designed to be another safeguard of human life.  The murderer was to die, to prevent others from committing murder. 
 
  In the image of God; a rational, accountable, moral, and immortal being; to exercise by God's appointment a portion of his authority, and with a right to life, till God, or some one in obedience to or in accordance with his will, should take it away. 
 
God is the rightful disposer of human life, and as he directs that the murderer shall by man be put to death, it is morally wrong for government not to do it.  It is a violation of duty to God and to men.

title: Genesis 9:9
text: Establish my covenant; confirm a solemn promise or engagement.

title: Genesis 9:13
text:
My bow; the rainbow. 
 
  A token; a visible assurance of the certain fulfilment of what God promised, and bringing it to remembrance.

title: Genesis 9:15
text:
I will remember my covenant; the rainbow was to be a means of leading men in all ages to remember God's covenant, and to feel that he remembers it, and that what he has promised he will accomplish. 
 
Whenever we see the rainbow we have evidence of the truth of God's declarations, and that he remembers them; and we should feel that not one jot or tittle of what he has said will fail, but that all will be fulfilled.

title: Genesis 9:19
text: Overspread; repeopled with inhabitants.

title: Genesis 9:20
text: A husbandman; a cultivator of the earth.

title: Genesis 9:21
text: Wine is an intoxicating liquor.  Those who, at home or abroad, on ordinary or on festive occasions, drink it, are in danger of becoming drunken; nor is piety towards God, nor benevolence to men, nor a long course of successful resistance of temptation, a sure safeguard against it.  All, therefore, who think they stand, should take heed lest they fall; praying, "Lead us not into temptation," and showing the sincerity of their prayers by their conduct.

title: Genesis 9:25
text:
Canaan; God mercifully restricted the curse to Canaan the son of Ham, and father of the Canaanites, whom, as a just punishment for their sins, God in after-ages directed the Israelites to destroy.  Exodus 34:10-14 Deuteronomy 7:17-24  
 
  Servant of servants; the meanest of servants.

title: Genesis 9:27
text:
Enlarge Japheth; greatly extend the territory of his descendants. 
 
  Dwell in the tents of Shem; partake of the blessings enjoyed by him.  The Jews came from Shem.  The chief civilized and Christian nations of modern Gentiles are from Japheth.

title: Genesis 10:1
text: Now these are the generations; this chapter contains the oldest and most important genealogical record in the world.  The reader will notice that the names of the descendants of Noah's sons represent generally not simply individuals, but nations, or families of nations sprung from them.

title: Genesis 10:2
text:
Gomer; probably the Cimmerians north of the Black sea, around which and north of it his sons settled,  Genesis 10:3 . 
 
  Magog; a powerful people of the north.  Ezekiel 38:15 Ezekiel 39:2  
 
  Madai; the Medes east of Assyria and south of the Caspian sea. 
 
  Javan; the Ionians on the western coast of Asia Minor, and then the Greeks generally. 
 
  Tubal, and Meshech; probably inhabiting the region between the Caspian and Black seas, and further north.

title: Genesis 10:3
text: Togarmah; probably the Armenians, or a people in that vicinity.

title: Genesis 10:4
text:
Elishah; the Greeks. 
 
  Kittim; the same as Chittim, and the isles of Chittim.  The word is plural, and signifies the coasts and islands west of Palestine, and then, in a general sense, Europe and the coasts of Asia Minor.  The same is signified by "the isles of the Gentiles,"  Genesis 10:5 . 
 
The sons of Japheth occupied Europe, Asia Minor, the countries around the Black sea and the Caspian, and the vast region to the north and east of them.

title: Genesis 10:6
text:
Cush; from whom came the Ethiopians, south of Egypt. 
 
  Mizraim; from whom came the Egyptians.  Mizraim is the Hebrew word for Egypt.

title: Genesis 10:7
text:
Seba; a people of Ethiopia, the same as the Sabeans, mentioned in  Isaiah 45:14 , along with Egypt and Ethiopia.  It must not be confounded with the Sabeans of  Job 1:15 , where a different word is used in the Hebrew. 
 
  Havilah; different from the Havilah mentioned in  Genesis 10:29 . 
 
  Sheba, and Dedan; to be distinguished from the Sheba and Dedan named,  Genesis 25:3 , as descendants of Abraham. There was also a third Sheba, descended from Shem,  Genesis 10:28 .

title: Genesis 10:8
text:
vv 8-9 
 
  Mighty one in the earth--mighty hunter; distinguished for his bold and successful exploits, in overcoming and controlling beasts and men.

title: Genesis 10:10
text:
Babel; Babylon on the Euphrates. 
 
  The land of Shinar; the plain country lying around Babylon.  It was six or seven hundred miles east of Canaan.

title: Genesis 10:11
text:
Asshur; from him came the name Assyria.  He was a son of Shem,  Genesis 10:22 , and is mentioned here by way of anticipation.  Some prefer: "He [Nimrod] went forth to Asshur," that is, Assyria. 
 
  Nineveh; a city on the river Tigris, about three hundred miles north of Babylon.

title: Genesis 10:13
text:
Ludim; that is, children of Lud, im being the Hebrew plural. Another Lud is mentioned  Genesis 10:22 , the descendant of Shem. 
 
  Pathrusim; the people of Pathros, that is, Upper Egypt.

title: Genesis 10:14
text: Philistim; the Philistines, who occupied the south-western angle of Palestine. From  Deuteronomy 2:23  and  Amos 9:7 , we learn that they came out of Caphtor.  We may suppose that from the Casluhim came first the Caphtorim, and from these the Philistim. According to the ancients, the Casluhim and Caphtorim were Egyptian colonies, the former inhabiting Colchis, at the eastern extremity of the Black sea; the latter Cappadocia, in the eastern part of Asia Minor.  Some understand by Caphtor the modern island of Crete.

title: Genesis 10:15
text:
Zidon; from whom came the Zidonians. 
 
  Heth; the father of the Hittites.

title: Genesis 10:19
text:
Zidon; the chief city of the Zidonians, in the northwest corner of Palestine on the Mediterranean sea. 
 
  As thou comest to Gerar, unto Gaza; that is, extending from Zidon to Gaza, as one goes south to Gerar.  Gaza was the southern city of the Philistines, and Gerar was near it. 
 
  As thou goest unto Sodom--unto Lasha; extending from Zidon south- east to Lasha, as one goes towards Sodom, etc. Lasha seems to have been east of the Dead sea.  Sodom and the three cities named with it lay in the vale of Siddim, which is now covered by the Dead sea. 
 
The posterity of Ham occupied Egypt and Africa generally, the whole eastern coast of the Mediterranean, the great plain around the lower Euphrates and its branches, and some parts of Asia Minor and of Arabia.

title: Genesis 10:21
text:
Eber; see note  Genesis 10:24 . 
 
  The elder; these words, as they stand in the original, may refer to either Shem or Japheth.  From the fact that in the genealogical tables Japheth is named first, as also from  Genesis 5:32  compared with  Genesis 11:10 , it is inferred with probability that Japheth was the elder brother.

title: Genesis 10:22
text:
Elam; inhabiting the country now called Persia. 
 
  Asshur; see note  Genesis 10:11 . 
 
  Lud; according to Josephus, the Lydians in Asia Minor. 
 
  Aram; a general name for ancient Syria, lying north and north-east of Palestine, and in the wider sense, including Mesopotamia.

title: Genesis 10:23
text: Uz; several persons of this name are mentioned in Scripture,  Genesis 22:21 Genesis 36:28 ; and from which of them the land of Uz in Arabia was peopled, is not known.  Probably Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash all occupied parts of Syria.

title: Genesis 10:24
text: Eber; or Heber in Mesopotamia beyond the Euphrates.  He was the ancestor of Abraham, and many suppose that from him is derived the word Hebrew.

title: Genesis 10:25
text:
Peleg; meaning division. 
 
  The earth divided; among the different tribes of men.  Genesis 11:8

title: Genesis 10:26
text:
Joktan; his children seem all to have settled in Arabia, or further east. 
 
  Hazarmaveth; the same as Hadramant in south-eastern Arabia.

title: Genesis 10:28
text: Sheba; the Sabeans in the southern part of Arabia Felix.

title: Genesis 10:29
text:
Ophir; probably in India. 
 
  Havilah; on the Persian gulf. 
 
The posterity of Shem occupied Arabia, Syria, and the region east, in a more southern line than that of the posterity of Japheth. 
 
Many changes were afterwards made among the descendants of Noah's three sons, by colonization and conquest.

title: Genesis 10:32
text: As all nations had one common origin and sprung from one family, they should all love each other as brethren, and seek to promote each other's good; doing in all things to others as they ought to wish that others should do to them.

title: Genesis 11:1
text: One language--one speech; these words denote union in counsel and in language.

title: Genesis 11:3
text:
Go to; come now. 
 
  Slime--for mortar; bitumen; a pitchy substance which they used for cement.

title: Genesis 11:4
text:
A name; a tower of renown, which may serve as a centre of unity. 
 
It is natural for men to seek to be distinguished, and as natural to seek it in a wrong way and for a wrong end.  In doing this they will be disappointed.  Would they be truly great, and permanently honored, which they may and ought to desire, they must seek these blessings, not in the indulgence of selfish gratification, but in learning and doing the will of God.

title: Genesis 11:6
text: Nothing will be restrained; if permitted to go on, they will accomplish their designs.

title: Genesis 11:7
text: Confound their language; by an influence from God their speech was confounded, and their counsels divided, so that they separated themselves into different famlies speaking different languages.

title: Genesis 11:9
text:
Babel; meaning confusion. 
 
The effects of the confusion of tongues are seen down to the present day, in the variety of languages which are spoken, and in the difficulty thus occasioned of holding conversation and communicating freely the knowledge which multitudes need, and without which they are exposed to perish.

title: Genesis 11:10
text: Shem; the progenitor of Abraham, whose history Moses, the writer of this book, is about to give.

title: Genesis 11:26
text:
Lived seventy years; and after that, 
 
  Begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran; but not, it is supposed, in this order.  Haran was the first-born, and Abram was the youngest.  He is mentioned first as Shem was,  Genesis 5:32 , because from him was to spring the Messiah. See  Genesis 5:1-32  and  Matthew 1:1-25 .

title: Genesis 11:28
text: Ur of the Chaldees; a place it is supposed between the Tigris and the Euphrates, about four hundred miles north-east of Canaan.  This is the first time the Chaldees are mentioned in Scripture.  They lived in the north part of Mesopotamia, now Koordistan.  Afterwards they went south into the land of Shinar, which was afterwards called Chaldea and Babylonia.  Genesis 10:10

title: Genesis 11:29
text: Sarai--Milcah; these are both supposed to have been daughters of Haran, the elder brother of Abram and Nahor.  If so, these two brothers married their nieces; but it seems that Haran and Abraham, though both sons of Terah, had not the same mother.   Genesis 20:12

title: Genesis 11:31
text:
Into; towards. 
 
  Canaan; a country on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean sea. 
 
  Haran; a place in Mesopotamia between the rivers Euphrates and Chebar.  It is called in the New Testament, Charran.   Acts 7:4  
 
The statements of the Old Testament are in various ways confirmed by the New, and thus they mutually support and illustrate each other; while both throughout have special reference to, and in numerous ways proclaim the dignity and show forth the glory of Jesus Christ.

title: Genesis 12:1
text:
Abram; this is composed of two Hebrew words: 
 
  Ab, signifying father, and ram, meaning high or distinguished.

title: Genesis 12:2
text: Be a blessing; to all families of the earth  Genesis 12:3  by being the progenitor of Jesus Christ.

title: Genesis 12:3
text:
Be blessed; in his seed, which is Christ.   Galatians 3:8-16  
 
Though God calls his people to make great sacrifices for his sake, he promises them blessings greater than those they relinquish; and in believing and obeying him, they will find abundant reward.

title: Genesis 12:6
text:
Sichem; called also Shechem; and in the New Testament, Sychar.  John 4:5   It lay between mount Ebal on the north, and Gerizim on the south.  It is now called Nabulus or Nablus, and is about forty miles north of Jerusalem. 
 
  Plain; the original word means oak.

title: Genesis 12:8
text:
Bethel; the meaning of this word is house of God.  This name was afterwards given to this place by Jacob.   Genesis 28:19   The city was before called Luz, and is about thirty miles south of Shechem. 
 
  Hai; called Ai,  Joshua 8:1 ; a few miles east of Bethel. 
 
When called to remove from one place to another, it is a great comfort to take with us our friends.  Wherever we are we should worship God, and commit ourselves and our friends to his merciful guidance and care.

title: Genesis 12:10
text: Though obedience to God will not, in this world, secure us from trials, it will prepare us to meet them, make them blessings, and fit us, when we leave this world, to be freed from all trials and receive unmingled and everlasting joys.

title: Genesis 12:12
text: The best of men are far from being faultless; they do many things in which it is neither wise, nor safe, nor right for us to imitate them; and whenever we trust to human expedients instead of trusting in God, we may expect to be punished for our folly.

title: Genesis 12:13
text:
My sister; see note to  Genesis 20:12 . 
 
  That it may be well with me; that I may be well treated for thy sake.  See  Genesis 12:16 . 
 
  My soul shall live; my life shall be spared.

title: Genesis 12:15
text: Great beauty is a source of great danger, and often the means of great evil to its possessor.

title: Genesis 12:16
text: He had sheep--camels; Abraham had them as presents from Pharaoh.

title: Genesis 12:17
text: Plagued Pharaoh; and also in some way revealed to him the cause of these plagues. Compare  Genesis 20:3 .

title: Genesis 12:19
text: Might have taken her to me my wife; he had purposed an honorable marriage with her, but had not accomplished it. Compare  Genesis 20:4 .

title: Genesis 12:20
text: The Lord watches over his people for good, and takes much better care of them than they do of themselves.

title: Genesis 13:1
text: The south; the south part of Canaan.

title: Genesis 13:4
text: Habitual communion with God is essential to a life of faith; and necessary in order rightly to use the blessings, meet the trials, and discharge the duties of life.

title: Genesis 13:6
text:
Not able to bear them; the pasturage was not sufficient for their flocks. 
 
Increasing riches may part old and tried friends.

title: Genesis 13:7
text:
Dwelled then in the land; this made their quarrels the more improper and perilous. 
 
Contentions among the friends of God, the members of their families, or persons in their employment, are exceedingly injurious to his cause; they tend to prejudice men against religion, and to prevent their salvation.

title: Genesis 13:8
text: Brethren; near relatives, and professors of the same religion.

title: Genesis 13:9
text: A wise and good man will be kind, accommodating, and peaceful; will seek to avoid strife, especially with his relatives; and will often relinquish his rights rather than contend for them.

title: Genesis 13:10
text:
Jordan; rising near mount Lebanon, and running south into the Dead sea.  The plain of Jordan was the region bordering on the river. 
 
  Sodom--Gomorrah; cities in the south of Canaan, the site of which is now occupied by the Dead sea. 
 
  Garden of the Lord; the scenery of paradise may harbor a population ripening for hell. 
 
  As thou comest unto Zoar; the meaning is, "all the plain of Jordan," as far as to Zoar, "was well watered."  Zoar was a small place near Sodom and Gomorrah.   Genesis 19:22

title: Genesis 13:13
text: When men, in selecting their place of abode, regard the opportunities for making money more than they do the means of intellectual and moral improvement, they commit sin, and will have reason to be grateful if they escape ruin.

title: Genesis 13:15
text:
To thee will I give it; not to him personally, but to his descendants.   Acts 7:5  
 
  For ever; for a perpetual inheritance, should they continue to obey him. 
 
God requires faith in promises, the fulfilment of which is future and distant.

title: Genesis 13:16
text: As the dust of the earth; very numerous.

title: Genesis 13:18
text:
Plain; oaks of Mamre,  Genesis 12:6 . 
 
  Hebron; a city about twenty miles south of Jerusalem, called also Kirjath-Arba, or the city of Arba, a famous giant who lived there.  Joshua 14:15  
 
Men who, from regard to God, make sacrifices for peace, will be kept from many evils into which others will fall.  They will receive much good themselves, and be instrumental in communicating much to others.

title: Genesis 14:1
text:
Shinar;  Genesis 10:1 
  Ellasar; apparently lying between Shinar and Elam. 
 
  Elam; Persia. 
 
  Nations; several small nations, whose situation is unknown.

title: Genesis 14:2
text: King of Sodom; the word king is used in the Bible for the ruler of a city or small district; and for the chief of a clan or tribe, as well as for the ruler of a nation.

title: Genesis 14:3
text:
Joined together; assembled as allies. 
 
  Vale of Siddim; the southern part of the valley of the Jordan, in which were the cities previously mentioned, (see note)  Genesis 14:1 , and which is now covered by the Dead sea.

title: Genesis 14:4
text:
Served Chedorlaomer; by paying him tribute. 
 
  Rebelled; refused longer to pay tribute.

title: Genesis 14:5
text: Ashteroth--Ham--Shaveh Kiriathaim; places east of the Jordan.

title: Genesis 14:6
text:
Mount Seir; south of the Dead sea. 
 
  El-paran; west of mount Seir.

title: Genesis 14:7
text:
Kadesh; Kadesh-barnea, in the desert south of Judah. 
 
  Hazezon-tamar; En-gedi, on the west shore of the Dead sea.  II Chronicles 20:2

title: Genesis 14:10
text:
Slime-pits; places where bitumen, and adhesive and inflammable substance, oozed out of the ground, or where bitumen had been dug out to be used for mortar.   Genesis 11:3  
 
  Fell there; were entangled among them and overcome, and many perished.

title: Genesis 14:11
text: Ever since the apostasy, there have been men who acted as if might gave right; who, if they could, would rob others; and, to obtain their property, put them to death: sins as odious and hateful when committed by rulers and nations, as when committed by private individuals.

title: Genesis 14:12
text: When men, for worldly purposes, choose to dwell in places distinguished for wickedness, they expose themselves to share in the calamities which that wickedness brings upon the people.

title: Genesis 14:13
text:
The Hebrew; a name given to Abram, as some suppose, because he descended from Eber, or Heber; and as others think, because he came from beyond the river Euphrates; the word signifying one who has passed over. 
 
  Plain of Mamre;  Genesis 12:1 
  Confederate with Abram, united with him in opposing his enemies.

title: Genesis 14:14
text:
Brother; here used for nephew.  Genesis 12:13  
 
  Dan; perhaps Dan-jaan, mentioned  II Samuel 4:6 , and different from the Dan in the northern limit of Palestine, which did not receive this name till long after the death of Moses.   Judges 18:29

title: Genesis 14:15
text:
Left hand; to the north. 
 
  Damascus; the capital of ancient Syria; on a plain east of Anti- Lebanon.

title: Genesis 14:16
text: When men have been robbed of what justly belongs to them, those who are right-minded will abhor the crime, and be disposed, when they can, to take right and effectual measures that what has been taken away may be restored.

title: Genesis 14:17
text: Shaveh--dale; a valley near Jerusalem.

title: Genesis 14:18
text:
Melchizedek; a name meaning King of righteousness. 
 
  Salem; meaning in Hebrew, peace,  Hebrews 7:2 ; supposed to have been the place afterwards called Jerusalem.

title: Genesis 14:20
text:
He gave him tithes; Abram gave to Melchizedek a tenth part.  Hebrews 7:1-17  This was done as an expression of gratitude to God, whose priest Melchizedek was. 
 
Though God often suffers wicked men to take possession of what does not belong to them, such possession gives them no just title to it; and when, in his providence, he restores it, his goodness should be acknowledged, and the praise given to him.

title: Genesis 14:21
text: Persons and--goods; which Abram had taken from the enemy.

title: Genesis 14:22
text: Lifted up my hand; taken an oath, or made a solemn promise.

title: Genesis 14:23
text: Good men, who do right, will be careful to avoid the reality and the appearance of covetousness, and of every thing selfish, niggardly, and mean.

title: Genesis 14:24
text: Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre: the confederates of Abram, mentioned  Genesis 14:13 .

title: Genesis 15:1
text: Those who are protected by God have no reason to fear, and those who receive his gracious reward will not want any good thing.

title: Genesis 15:2
text:
Give me; he asks for something higher than the mere increase of his outward estate. 
 
  Steward of my house; or, as many prefer, possessor of my house, that is, heir.

title: Genesis 15:3
text: Born in my house; a house-servant.

title: Genesis 15:6
text:
Counted it to him for righteousness; accepted him as righteous, through faith, or the exercise of that confidence in God which led him to follow his directions.   Romans 4:4 Romans 4:21 Romans 4:22 Galatians 3:6-9 Galatians 3:29 James 2:21-24  
 
That confidence in God which leads men to believe and obey him is counted to them for righteousness and those who exercise it will, for Christ's sake, be justified, sanctified, and saved.  Romans 4:3 James 2:21-24

title: Genesis 15:7
text:
Ur of the Chaldees;  Genesis 11:31 
  Give thee this land; not him personally, but his posterity.  Acts 7:5

title: Genesis 15:8
text: Whereby shall I know; by what token or visible sign.

title: Genesis 15:10
text: One against another; the carcass was divided length-wise, and each half placed opposite the other, with a space wide enough for those who in this way made a covenant, to pass between them in token of its ratification.

title: Genesis 15:11
text: Fowls; ravenous birds, accustomed to feed upon flesh.

title: Genesis 15:12
text: Great darkness; emblematical of the affliction which would come upon his posterity in Egypt.

title: Genesis 15:13
text:
Four hundred years; the departure of the Israelites from Egypt took place four hundred and thirty years from the time the promise was first made to Abraham; about half of which his posterity spent in Canaan, and the rest in Egypt.   Genesis 12:1-3 Exodus 12:40-41 Galatians 3:17 Galatians 4:29   In the present prophecy, uttered some years after the first promise, the round number four hundred is appropriately employed. 
 
God graciously communicates to his people as much knowledge of the future as will best fit them for the discharge of their duty; and what would not be useful to them he kindly withholds.

title: Genesis 15:14
text:
Judge; visit with judgments, in punishment of their sins. 
 
  Substance; riches.  Psalms 105:37

title: Genesis 15:16
text:
In the fourth generation; after four hundred years from the time above mentioned; or the fourth generation from the time they went into Egypt, Moses and Caleb being the fourth generation from Levi and Judah. 
 
  Amorites; the Israelites, after they should leave Egypt.  Deuteronomy 20:17 Joshua 3:10 Joshua 10:5-14 Joshua 24:15

title: Genesis 15:17
text: A smoking furnace, and a burning lamp; symbols of the divine presence.

title: Genesis 15:18
text:
River of Egypt; supposed to be a stream which emptied into the Mediterranean between Gaza and the eastern branch of the Nile.  Numbers 34:5 Joshua 13:3 I Chronicles 13:5 .  Its present mane is El-Arish. 
 
  Euphrates;  Genesis 2:1 
 
When God in his providence has given to a people a good land, and they abuse his mercies, break his laws, and live in rebellion against him, he may justly take it from them and give it to others.

title: Genesis 15:19
text:
vv. 19-21 
 
  Kenites--Jebusites; tribes that dwelt in Canaan.  Genesis 9:25-27

title: Genesis 16:2
text:
May obtain children by her; her present purpose was to reckon Hagar's offspring as her own. 
 
Abraham was not perfect.  In all things he came short, and in many things offended.  It is not wise, safe, or right for us to imitate any mere man in all things.  There is but one perfect example.

title: Genesis 16:3
text: To be his wife; a subordinate wife, or concubine, according to the custom of those times.  This was a violation of the great law of marriage, and was followed by great domestic troubles.   Matthew 19:5-9

title: Genesis 16:5
text: My wrong be upon thee; thou art the cause of this evil, and thou oughtest to prevent it.

title: Genesis 16:6
text: Such is human nature, that irresponsible power is very likely to be abused; and nothing but the grace of God will teach masters and mistresses so to treat servants as to fulfil the great law of love.  Matthew 7:12

title: Genesis 16:7
text:
The Angel of the Lord; supposed to be the Messenger of the covenant, the Messiah.   Malachi 3:1 Luke 1:76  
 
  Shur; a city on the borders of Egypt and Palestine.  The adjacent desert is called the wilderness of Shur.  She was on the way to her native home.

title: Genesis 16:9
text: Return to thy mistress; she would be more exposed to hardship, suffering, and death in going forward, than in going back.

title: Genesis 16:11
text:
Ishmael; a Hebrew name, meaning God will hear; it was given as a memento that God had heard and granted her relief, and an encouragement to her and others to call upon him.   Psalms 50:15  
 
The Lord tenderly sympathizes in the afflictions of servants as well as of masters.  His ears are always open to the cries of those who heartily call upon him, and he is ready to help them.

title: Genesis 16:12
text:
He will be a wild man; his posterity would be rude, unsubdued, and opposed to the restraints of city life; as the Arabs in their native country always have been. 
 
  His hand--against every man; they would be robbers and plunderers of such as should fall in their way. 
 
  Dwell in the presence; though opposed to all nations, they would never be exterminated or dispossessed; and they have continued to inhabit Arabia down to the present day.

title: Genesis 16:14
text: Kadesh and Bered; places about forty miles south of Hebron.

title: Genesis 16:15
text: Mementos of divine kindness are highly proper, and may be very useful. They remind us of the unmerited goodness of God, tend to awaken new gratitude, and lead to increasing devotion to his service.

title: Genesis 17:1
text:
Perfect; sincere, upright, wholly and perseveringly devoted to the service and glory of God.

text: Those who are most guilty themselves are often most ready to denounce vengeance on others.

title: Genesis 39:4
text: Grace; favor.

title: Genesis 39:5
text: The Lord will not forsake any who put their trust in him; and fidelity in the discharge of duty in lower situations is the best preparation for, and the surest way of advancement to those that are higher.

title: Genesis 39:6
text:
He knew not aught; he did not take the care of any thing himself, but left all to Joseph. 
 
  Goodly--well-favored; beautiful in person.

title: Genesis 39:8
text: Wotteth; knoweth.

title: Genesis 39:9
text: The fear of the Lord is the surest pledge of fidelity, the best safeguard against temptation, and the most powerful means of promoting all the great interests of men.

title: Genesis 39:15
text: Tempters to sin will turn accusers, and when they have power, will become persecutors and tormentors.

title: Genesis 39:20
text: In the prison;  Genesis 41:14 Psalms 105:1

title: Genesis 39:21
text: No evils which men can inflict can shut out the presence and favor of God from those who trust in him; and a servant in a dungeon may be more happy than a king on his throne.  Though he may suffer for righteousness' sake, in due time he will be delivered, and his sorrow turned into joy.

title: Genesis 39:22
text: He was the doer; he gave directions, and things were done accordingly.

title: Genesis 40:1
text:
Butler; a cup-bearer; one who presented to the king his wine. 
 
  Baker; the one who furnished the king his bread, or had the direction of others who did it.

title: Genesis 40:3
text:
Ward; prison. 
 
The present condition of men is no certain indication of their character.  In the same dungeon may be very different men, and from very different causes--men who are serving different masters, and preparing to dwell for ever in different places.

title: Genesis 40:4
text:
Charged Joseph; gave him the care of them. 
 
  Served them; supplied their wants.

title: Genesis 40:5
text: According to the interpretation; that is, the dreams were truly prophetic, and had each an interpretation, as was afterwards explained by Joseph.

title: Genesis 40:8
text: Those who receive their blessings as the gift of God, and gratefully acknowledge him, will sympathize in the distresses of others, and be disposed, as far as may be consistent, to relieve them.

title: Genesis 40:12
text:
Three branches are three days; not literally, but they represent or mean three days.  So the three baskets,  Genesis 40:18 .  Compare also  Matthew 26:26 . 
 
To insist on a literal interpretation where the meaning is evidently figurative, is a gross perversion of Scripture.

title: Genesis 40:13
text: Lift up thy head; take thee out of prison.

title: Genesis 40:15
text:
Stolen; his brethren, in selling him, took what was not theirs, and appropriated it to their own use.  This, Joseph called stealing. 
 
The selling of a brother into bondage is not only palpable dishonesty, but aggravated theft.   Exodus 21:16

title: Genesis 40:16
text: Good; favorable.

title: Genesis 40:23
text: In prosperity men are apt to overlook and forget those who have aided them in adversity, and thus to show that their hearts are deceitful and desperately wicked.   Jeremiah 17:9

title: Genesis 41:1
text: The river; the Nile, upon the annual overflow of which the fertility of Egypt depends.

title: Genesis 41:2
text:
Kine; cows. 
 
  Well-favored; good looking.  So ill-favored means bad looking. Both the fat and the lean cows came out of the river, signifying that from it come both plenty and want in Egypt.

title: Genesis 41:5
text: Ears of corn; heads of wheat.  The so called Egyptian wheat bears several heads on one stalk.

title: Genesis 41:7
text: All future things are known to God, and as far as he sees best he makes them known to men.  Before men had the Bible, God often communicated information to them in dreams and visions.  But now we are not to expect information in those ways, but to give heed to the Bible, which is able to make us wise unto salvation, and furnish us thoroughly for every good work.

title: Genesis 41:8
text: Magicians; the sacred scribes of Egypt, whose office was to explain signs, interpret dreams, and reveal hidden things.

title: Genesis 41:9
text: My faults; against Pharaoh, rather than against Joseph.

title: Genesis 41:13
text: He restored; Pharaoh restored.  The chief butler speaks of his maonarch in the third person.

title: Genesis 41:14
text: God never overlooks the trials of his people, or suffers them to continue a moment too long.  When the right time comes he delivers them, often suddenly, in ways, by means, and for purposes which they never expected.

title: Genesis 41:16
text:
It is not in me; he could not of himself interpret the dream, it must be by divine aid. 
 
  An answer of peace; one that would remove his fears and promote his good.

title: Genesis 41:25
text:
Is one; both dreams mean the same thing. 
 
Those who in all their ways acknowledge God, will find that he directs their paths; and those things which they thought to be against them, they will see were ordered in such a way as to promote their highest good.

title: Genesis 41:26
text: Are seven years; represent them.   Genesis 40:12 Genesis 40:18

title: Genesis 41:28
text: This is the thing which I have spoken; this is the thing which I said before.  See  Genesis 41:25 .

title: Genesis 41:33
text: The fact that men are dependent on God does not supersede the necessity, on their part, of wisdom and discretion; and those who have most of these qualities, will be most likely to be successful.

title: Genesis 41:34
text: Of the land; the produce of the land.

title: Genesis 41:36
text: The land perish not; the inhabitants of it.

title: Genesis 41:39
text: Those who know most of God and his ways will be the most wise and discreet.  They can be most safely trusted, and in great and difficult services may be expected to do the most good.

title: Genesis 41:42
text: Put it upon Joseph's hand; in token of his being clothed with authority.

title: Genesis 41:43
text: The second chariot; the chariot assigned to the man that stood next in rank to the king, and doubtless second to the king's chariot in splendor.

title: Genesis 41:44
text:
Lift up his hand or foot; a proverbial expression, denoting that all the people should be under Joseph's control. 
 
He who shows the most kindness, patience, compassion, and benevolence in a dungeon, may be expected to show the most humility, meekness, equanimity, and loveliness on a throne.

title: Genesis 41:45
text:
Zaphnath-paaneah; supposed to mean, saviour of the world. 
 
  Priest; a priest at that time, in Egypt, was a civil as well as an ecclesiastical ruler; and by this marriage Joseph became connected with one of the great men of the kingdom. 
 
  On; called by the Greeks Heliopolis, or the city of the sun.  It was on the east of the Nile, in the land of Goshen, and not far from the modern Cairo.

title: Genesis 41:47
text: By handfuls; in great abundance.

title: Genesis 41:48
text: Laid up the food; that which was not wanted for present use.

title: Genesis 41:51
text: Manasseh; that is, one causing forgetfulness.

title: Genesis 41:52
text:
Ephraim; fruitful. 
 
God can, in this world, cause his people to forget their sorrows, or so to remember them as to heighten their joys, and make them feel that their sharpest trials were not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall follow.

title: Genesis 41:55
text: Egypt was famished; the people had consumed all their food, and were in want.

title: Genesis 42:1
text: Look upon one another; in perplexity and despair.

title: Genesis 42:2
text: In seasons of danger and distress nothing is gained by despondency. The question should be, What shall we do? and having ascertained, we should, without delay, and in dependence on God, attempt to do it.  He helps those who, in the right way, attempt to help themselves.

title: Genesis 42:6
text:
That sold; directed as to the selling. 
 
  Bowed down;

title: Genesis 42:7
text: Made himself strange; acted as one that did not know them.

title: Genesis 42:9
text:
The dreams;  Genesis 37:5-9 
  The nakedness of the land; its defenceless points, where and how a successful attack might be made upon it. 
 
The efforts of men to thwart the plans of God are the means of fulfilling them; yet they are as wicked in opposing him, as if he did not make what they do the occasion of promoting his cause.

title: Genesis 42:14
text: That is it that I spake unto you;what I said to you before,  Genesis 42:9 , is the truth.  Compare above,  Genesis 41:28 .

title: Genesis 42:15
text: By the life of Pharaoh; as surely as Pharaoh lives.

title: Genesis 42:16
text: Men are often strongly tempted to do evil that good may come, but it is never right; and the success of a plan is no sure evidence of the righteousness of the means used in prosecuting it.

title: Genesis 42:17
text:
Ward; prison. 
 
  Three days; this gave them time to reflect upon their past conduct, their treatment of Joseph and Jacob, and upon their present condition and prospects.  This was what Joseph intended, and he no doubt prayed that it might be for their good.

title: Genesis 42:20
text: Be verified; be proved to be true.

title: Genesis 42:21
text:
Guilty concerning our brother; conscience condemned them for their treatment of Joseph, more than twenty years before. 
 
  Therefore is this distress; they viewed it as a punishment of their sins.

title: Genesis 42:28
text:
They were afraid; lest they should be charged with having stolen the money, and by treated as thieves. 
 
  God hath done; in his providence caused to come upon us as a punishment for our sin. 
 
When men have done what they know to be wicked, and evils come upon them, conscience links the two together, and views the one as a punishment for the other.

title: Genesis 42:37
text: Slay my two sons; that is, you may slay them, if I bring not Benjamin back again; a rash expression, but it showed Reuben's earnestness and sincerity.

title: Genesis 42:38
text: His brother; that is, Joseph; his own brother by Rachel.

title: Genesis 43:5
text: As to the future doing of things which are left to our discretion, it is ordinarily not best to say positively what we will or will not do, but to feel our dependence on God; and when the time to act comes, decide as truth and duty may then require.

title: Genesis 43:7
text:
According to the tenor of these words; suited our answers honestly to these questions of his. 
 
When things seem to go against us, we are apt to overlook the controlling hand of God, and regard only the instruments; but in blaming them, we often find fault with him.

title: Genesis 43:11
text:
Balm; balsam, like that of Gilead. 
 
  Honey; probably here honey of grapes, made by boiling down new wine to a third or half. 
 
  Myrrh; here probably a fragrant gum called ladanum. 
 
  Nuts; the original word means pistacia-nuts. 
 
When a man has promised to do what is wrong, instead of feeling that he is bound to fulfil his promise, his duty is to acknowledge his sin in making it, repent, and do what is right.  There is always a law higher than any mere human promise, namely, the law of God.  If a man does wrong because he has promised or sworn to do it, he adds sin to sin, and ripens for an aggravated condemnation.  Matthew 14:9-10

title: Genesis 43:12
text: Double money; that which they brought back, and enough more to buy the corn which they needed.

title: Genesis 43:14
text: If I be bereaved--I am bereaved; an expression of desponding resignation.

title: Genesis 43:18
text: A guilty conscience, when awakened, naturally forebodes evil, producing a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation; and unless men find the way of deliverance, it wil make them wretched.

title: Genesis 43:22
text: Property that has come into our hands by oversight or mistake, as well as that which we have wrongfully obtained, should be carefully and promptly returned to its rightful owners.

title: Genesis 43:23
text:
God--hath given you treasure; not without human agency; but he had so ordered things in his providence that they had their money. 
 
  I had your money; it was paid to me, and I acknowledge the receipt of it; of course you need not fear.  He had himself, at the command of Joseph, without their knowledge, put it into their sacks.

title: Genesis 43:24
text: Washed their feet; according to the custom of travellers in those days.   Genesis 18:4

title: Genesis 43:25
text: The present; that which they had brought from the land of Canaan.

title: Genesis 43:26
text:
Bowed themselves;  Genesis 37:7 
 
When events, long before made known, are accomplished by the voluntary actions of free moral agents, it shows that such actions were beforehand certain; though that certainty does not lessen men's freedom, nor diminish their praise or blameworthiness in performing those actions.   Acts 2:23

title: Genesis 43:30
text: Family ties are tender and lasting; and delightful, after long absence, is the meeting of affectionate family friends.  As their forcible and violent separation causes the intensest anguish, so their kind, providential restoration gives inexpressible joy.

title: Genesis 43:31
text: Refrained; from weeping, and appeared as usual.

title: Genesis 43:32
text: For that is an abomination; the Egyptians kept themselves separate from all strangers, and had a particular aversion to men whose occupation was that of shepherds.   Genesis 46:34

title: Genesis 43:33
text:
They sat before him; they were seated according to their different ages. 
 
  Marvelled; that he who seated them should know, in each case, which was oldest.

title: Genesis 43:34
text: Messes; portions of food.

title: Genesis 44:5
text: Whereby--he divineth; in this, as in using an interpreter and swearing by the life of Pharaoh, Joseph conducts himself towards his brethren as an Egyptian.  We are not to understand that he actually practised divination.  The practice of divining by cups was common among the Egyptians.

title: Genesis 44:9
text: Hasty decisions, and strong, confident assertions are often wrong, and bring those who make them into great perplexity and distress.  Proverbs 29:11

title: Genesis 44:14
text: Fell before him; in token of submission.   Genesis 37:7 Genesis 37:10

title: Genesis 44:16
text:
The iniquity of thy servants; he might not mean by this to confess that they had stolen the cup, but that God in his providence was righteously punishing them for their sins, and that they meant to accept whatever he should lay upon them. 
 
Hearty acknowledgment of the justice of God in our trials, and humble submission to his will, indicate a preparation for approaching deliverance.

title: Genesis 44:18
text:
Even as Pharaoh; having full power to do as he should choose. 
 
It is never wise or right, in a world of mercy and grace, to despair, or cease to use appropriate means; however dark to human appearance may be the prospect, or feeble the means used, God can give speedy and triumphant success.

title: Genesis 44:32
text: The most touching and efficacious eloquence is often a simple narration of facts.  God's ways are great, and a true recital of them is suited to produce great effects.  His ways, like himself, are perfect, and a knowledge of them is suited to make men perfect, and lead them, in their measure, to imitate him.

title: Genesis 44:33
text: Let thy servant abide instead of the lad; the feelings of the ten brethren towards their father and towards Benjamin, the trial of which seems to have been a chief object of Joseph's demeanor towards his brethren, were fully proved by this last self-sacrificing offer of Judah.

title: Genesis 44:34
text: An affectionate and tender regard for one's father, a readiness to sacrifice, and if need be suffer, to prevent evils from coming upon him, and to prolong his life, promote his comfort, and cheer him in old age, is peculiarly pleasing to God, and is often followed by some of his richest blessings.

title: Genesis 45:1
text: Then Joseph; in all his preceding conduct towards his brethren, which had the appearance of harshness, Joseph had acted by a divine illumination; not for the gratification of his own private feelings, but for the accomplishment of the divine purposes, which included the humiliation of his brethren, and the trial of their feelings towards their father and Benjamin.  Now the way was fully prepared for making himself known to his brethren.

title: Genesis 45:5
text:
Be not grieved; indulge not excessive anguish, nor sink into despair, for God is to be seen and acknowledged in all these things. 
 
A wise and good man will sometimes act towards those whom he loves in a way which he knows will give them pain, not because he takes pleasure in distressing them, but for the purpose of doing them good; and he will remove their sorrow as soon as he sees that he can do it consistently with their highest benefit.

title: Genesis 45:6
text: Earing; and old English word for ploughing, or tilling.

title: Genesis 45:8
text:
Not you; that is, not you merely, or principally.  You were instruments in fulfilling the infinitely wise and gracious purposes of God. 
 
God is not to be overlooked in any of the actions of men, but is to be acknowledged and adored as over all, perfect and blessed for evermore. However wicked those actions, or great the evils they occasion, he intends so to counteract and overrule them as to accomplish unspeakable good.

title: Genesis 45:9
text:
God hath made me lord; men had been the means, but God had been the cause, and to him belonged the glory. 
 
Whatever good we receive, and in whatever way, God is its author, and to him we should give the praise.

title: Genesis 45:10
text: Goshen; the north-east part of Egypt, nearest to the land of Canaan.

title: Genesis 45:20
text: Stuff; furniture; such things as could not be easily carried.

title: Genesis 45:22
text: It is sometimes right and best to bestow more of undeserved favors upon one than upon another; and a truly penitent, grateful, and benevolent heart will not repine at seeing this: it wil not blame the giver nor envy the receiver, but will admire the one and rejoice with the other.

title: Genesis 45:24
text:
Fall not out; not get into any dispute as to who was most guilty in selling Joseph, or deceiving his father, or about any thing else. 
 
Criminations and contests among brethren are exceedingly injurious, and the truly wise and benevolent earnestly desire to prevent them.

title: Genesis 45:26
text: Fainted; in the original, was cold; that is remained unmoved.

title: Genesis 45:28
text: When the friends of God see the ends he had in view, the ways he took to accomplish them, the results which have followed and are to follow, it will be enough--enough for life, enough in death, and enough for eternity.

title: Genesis 46:1
text: In undertaking a journey, or entering upon any new plan, we should feel our dependence upon God, seek his blessing, and commit ourselves to hsi guidance and care.

title: Genesis 46:4
text:
Bring thee up again; that is, thy posterity.   Genesis 50:21  In view of this fact, both Jacob and Joseph,  Genesis 50:25 , commanded that their bodies should be buried in the land of Canaan. 
 
  Put his hand upon thine eyes; Joseph should be with his father, and close his eyes when he should die. 
 
With the blessing of God we need not fear to undertake any service, make any sacrifice, or endure any trial to which he may call us.

title: Genesis 46:27
text: Threescore and ten; seventy; namely, the sixty-six mentioned  Genesis 46:26 , with Jacob, Joseph, and his two sons.  The Greek version of the Seventy here adds from  Numbers 26:28-37 , and  I Chronicles 7:14-23 , five grandsons of Joseph, computation seems to have been followed by Stephen.   Acts 7:14

title: Genesis 46:30
text:
Let me die;  Luke 2:29-24:53 
 
Men may receive such blessings as to desire no more on earth, and be willing at any time to leave it, and enter into heaven.   Philippians 1:23

title: Genesis 46:34
text: A wise regard for our friends will ordinarily lead us to wish them to continue in the employment in which they have been educated and with which they are acquainted, as promising greater happiness to themselves and greater usefulness to others.

title: Genesis 47:4
text:
