Sore; very grievous. 
 
Notwithstanding our dependence on God for all the blessings we enjoy and hope for, it is as needful to use all suitable means to obtain these blessings, as it would be if success depended solely on our efforts.  Compare  Acts 27:22-25 Acts 27:30-32 Acts 27:44 .

title: Genesis 47:9
text:
Pilgrimage; journey through this world. 
 
The longest life is but a journey through this world to another; and as character is the chief thing, our great concern should be that it may be such as shall render us most useful and fit us for heaven.

title: Genesis 47:11
text: Rameses; the capital of Goshen, about half way from the Nile to the Red sea.

title: Genesis 47:20
text: Men will cheerfully give up their property to save the life of the body; and yet, for the sake of property, they will sacrifice the life of their souls.   I Timothy 6:9-10 James 5:3

title: Genesis 47:21
text: Removed them to cities; where the food was stored, for the greater convenience of supplying them.

title: Genesis 47:22
text: Priests; the priests of Egypt were a very powerful and influential body, and enjoyed many privileges above the common people.

title: Genesis 47:23
text: Sow the land; as the seven years of famine were now drawing to a close.

title: Genesis 47:25
text: To be ungrateful to one who has saved our life, would be base; how much more so not to be grateful to Him who, by suffering and death for us, has opened a way to save the undying soul.

title: Genesis 47:26
text: The fifth part; this is supposed to have been the tax which they paid for the use of the land and the support of the government.

title: Genesis 47:30
text:
Their burying-place;  Genesis 23:20 Genesis 25:1  This Jacob did, not merely because he wished to be buried by the side of his fathers, but also as an expression of his faith in the promise of God that his posterity should inherit that land. 
 
The pious at death wish to have such disposal made of their bodies as shall be most useful to survivors, and, if consistent, to have them laid with the bodies of pious ancestors; that at the trump of the archangel they may rise and ascend together, and complete in body and soul, be ever with the Lord.   I Corinthians 15:51-55 I Thessalonians 4:16-17

title: Genesis 47:31
text: The bed's head; in  Hebrews 11:21 , the Septuagint, or Greek translation, is followed: worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff.

title: Genesis 48:3
text:
Luz;  Genesis 28:13 Genesis 28:1 
 
In sickness it is well gratefully to recount the past goodness of God to us and our families, and earnestly to recommend him and his salvation to all around us.

title: Genesis 48:5
text: They shall be mine; adopted as children and made heads of distinct tribes, like the other sons of Israel.

title: Genesis 48:6
text: After the name of their brethren; they should not be heads of distinct tribes, but should be reckoned as belonging to the tribe of Ephraim or of Manasseh.

title: Genesis 48:7
text: Rachel died;  Genesis 35:9 Genesis 35:16 Genesis 35:1

title: Genesis 48:8
text: Beheld; he could discern that they were present, though he could not distinguish them.

title: Genesis 48:11
text: God is often better to us than our fears, and does more for us than we, in our ignorance and weakness, had dared to hope.  This should lead us to trust in him at all times, and in well-doing, patiently wait for his salvation.

title: Genesis 48:12
text: Bowed himself; in token of reverence for his father, from whom he was now to receive, in the persons of his sons, the paternal blessing.

title: Genesis 48:14
text: Wittingly; knowingly, designedly.

title: Genesis 48:15
text: However much we may have of this world, and however many may minister to our wants, our daily bread comes from God, and he is the giver of all the common as well as special mercies of life.

title: Genesis 48:16
text:
The Angel;  Genesis 17:1 Genesis 28:15 Genesis 31:11 Genesis 31:13 Genesis 31:1 
  My name--and the name of my fathers; let them be called not Egyptians, but Israelites, descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and heirs of the promises made to them.

title: Genesis 48:18
text: Not so; he thought his father had made a mistake.

title: Genesis 48:19
text: Be greater; have a more numerous and powerful posterity.

title: Genesis 48:21
text: Strong confidence in the promises of God, and good hope through grace that when absent from the body we shall be present with the Lord, and that he will be the God of our children and children's children to coming generations, gives peace and joy in death.

title: Genesis 48:22
text:
One portion; the Hebrew word rendered portion is shechem, which signifies shoulder, and also, as here, tract of land.  Thus Jacob points out this tract as the inheritance of Joseph.  Compare  John 4:5 .  Accordingly Joseph was buried here, Jos 24.32, and the whole adjacent country fell to the tribes of Ephrim and Manasseh. At the same time the words, "one portion above thy brethren," seem to intimate the double inheritance which Joseph should have in the land of Canaan through his two sons.   I Chronicles 5:2  
 
  With my sword and with my bow; by warlike force.  There is an allusion here to the destruction of Shechem by Jacob's sons, which though disapproved by him, was yet, in the providence of God, designed to foreshadow the future conquest of Canaan by his children, to which these prophetic words look forward.

title: Genesis 49:2
text: We should desire not only to be useful in life, but in death to inculcate such truth, communicate such instruction, and set such an example as shall be most useful to coming generations.

title: Genesis 49:3
text: Excellency of dignity, and--of power; as the first-born, the blessings of the birthright belonged to Reuben, but on account of his sin it was taken from him.

title: Genesis 49:4
text:
Unstable as water; easily overcome by temptation, and rushing headlong into iniquity. 
 
  Shalt not excel; neither he nor his posterity would ever be distinguished.  Genesis 35:22

title: Genesis 49:5
text:
Are brethren; not merely descended form the same parents, but alike in cruelty of disposition. 
 
  Instruments of cruelty; he refers to their destruction of the Shechemites,  Genesis 34:25-29 .

title: Genesis 49:6
text: Come not thou; in this verse Jacob expresses his deep abhorrence of their crimes.

title: Genesis 49:7
text:
I will divide them; this was a prophecy from God, that their posterity would be scattered among the other tribes.  The Simeonites never attained to distinction among the tribes of Israel.  They had their portion within the inheritance of Judah,  Joshua 19:1 ; and seem to have been gradually absorbed and lost in that powerful tribe.  The Levites, as is well known, received no separate inheritance among the other tribes, but were distributed in cities throughout the land. 
 
We may feel the effects of our sins long after they have been committed.  Even if they have been repented of and forgiven, we and our posterity may suffer evils in consequence of them to the end of time.

title: Genesis 49:8
text:
Thy brethren shall praise; there is an allusion here to the meaning of the word Judah, that is, praise.   Genesis 29:35   His descendants would be highly distinguished and honored by all the other tribes. 
 
  In the neck; they would overcome their enemies.

title: Genesis 49:9
text: A lion; as the lion is the king of the forest, and terrible to other beasts, so the tribe of Judah would govern the other tribes, and be a terror to their foes.

title: Genesis 49:10
text:
The septre; an emblem of power and authority. 
 
  Shiloh; the Messiah, Prince of peace, sent as a Saviour.  Isaiah 7:14 Isaiah 9:6-7 Isaiah 11:1-10 Jeremiah 23:5-6 Daniel 9:25-27 Matthew 1:21-23 . 
 
  To him; to Shiloh. 
 
  The gathering of the people; or, the obedience of the people.  See  Deuteronomy 18:18-19 .  They shall accept him as their King, and he shall reign over them. 
 
The fact that the sceptre has long ago departed from the tribe of Judah, who have ceased to govern Israel, shows that the Messiah has come, and that the expectation of a future Messiah is vain.

title: Genesis 49:12
text: Red with wine--white with milk; his posterity would have a very fruitful country, and an abundance of the good things of life.

title: Genesis 49:13
text:
The haven of the sea; or, the shore of the sea.  The possessions of Zebulun extended from the sea of Chinnereth, afterwards called the sea of Galilee, on the east, to the Mediterranean on the west. 
 
  Zidon; or Sidon, a very ancient city on the Mediterranean, north of the more modern city of Tyre.

title: Genesis 49:14
text:
vv. 14-15 
 
  Issachar; the territory of Issachar lay south of Zebulun, and included the noble and fertile plain of Esdraelon. 
 
  Strong ass--bowed his shoulder to bear; his posterity would be distinguished for their ability and readiness to labor, for their quiet, patient, and industrious habits, and their preferring to live at home rather than engage in wars or public afairs.

title: Genesis 49:16
text: Judge his people; in allusion to the meaning of the word Dan, that is, one who judges.  From the tribe of Dan came Samson.  Judges 15:7-20 Judges 16:27-31

title: Genesis 49:17
text: A serpent--and adder; they would overcome their enemies by subtlety, stratagem, and surprise, rather than by courage and open force.   Judges 18:27

title: Genesis 49:18
text: The fulfilment of the prophecies uttered by Jacob on his death-bed shows that he spoke as directed by the Holy Ghost.  But however highly favored a good man may be on earth, however numerous his blessings or those of his posterity, nothing will fully satisfy him but the salvation of God.

title: Genesis 49:19
text: Gad; the possessions of the tribe of Gad lay on the east of the Jordan, and were peculiarly exposed to the assaults of hostile troops. See  Deuteronomy 33:20 Judges 10:8 Jeremiah 49:1 I Chronicles 5:18-22 I Chronicles 12:8 .

title: Genesis 49:20
text: Fat--royal dainties; the inheritance of his posterity would yield in abundance, not merely the necessaries, but also the luxuries of life.

title: Genesis 49:21
text:
A hind let loose; a female deer roaming at large, distinguished for beauty and fleetness.  But some render, Naphtali is a slender deer, slender being used in the sense of graceful. 
 
  Goodly words; words graceful and pleasant. He is thus marked as excelling in the gift of speech.  Of this the Song of Deborah and Barak,  Judges 5:1-31 , is an example.

title: Genesis 49:22
text: A fruitful bough; he would have a very numerous posterity.

title: Genesis 49:24
text: From thence; some refer these words to Joseph, but they belong rather to God.  We may render the whole passage thus: From thence [even from] the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel; from the God of thy father, who helps thee; and from the Almighty, who blesses thee, [shall be] blessings of heaven above, etc.

title: Genesis 49:25
text:
Blessings of heaven above; the sunshine, and fertilizing rain and dews. 
 
  Blessings of the deep; the fertlizing springs and streams. 
 
  Blessings of the breasts and of the womb; fruitfulness in his posterity, and in their flocks and herds.

title: Genesis 49:26
text:
Have prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors; have exceeded the blessings which my ancestors pronounced on their children.  The spirit of prophecy has made to me a fuller revelation of the good things reserved for thee. 
 
  Unto the utmost bound--everlasting hills; so long as they shall endure.  But many prefer to render, "Unto the precious things of the everlasting hills;" that is, my blessing extends so far as to include all these, and as long as they endure.  Compare  Deuteronomy 33:15 . 
 
The measures which men take in opposing God, are made the means of fulfilling his designs; and those which are adopted to prevent the exaltation and glory of his people, are made the occasion of promoting them.

title: Genesis 49:27
text: Raven as a wolf; his posterity would be warlike, fierce, and cruel.  Judges 19:22-27 Judges 20:14-25 .

title: Genesis 49:28
text: Blessed them; foretold the blessings God would bestow upon them, and what would take place in future times with regard to their posterity.

title: Genesis 49:29
text: In the cave;  Genesis 47:30 Genesis 23:19 Genesis 25:9 Genesis 35:27 Genesis 35:1

title: Genesis 49:33
text: Men who have finished the work God gave them to do, and are through grace gathered in peace--their bodies to the grave and their souls to the assembly of just men made perfect--are unspeakably blessed. Re 14.13

title: Genesis 50:1
text: Divine grace does not destroy or lessen natural affection, but regulates, purifies, and exalts it.

title: Genesis 50:2
text: Embalm; prepare the body with spices, drugs, and gums, in order to preserve it.

title: Genesis 50:3
text:
Forty days; the time it took to embalm the body. 
 
  Threescore and ten; seventy; the forty days in which they were embalming him, and thirty besides. 
 
The removal of the righteous, especially those who have had great influence, is not only a private, but a public loss, and may well occasion public grief.

title: Genesis 50:4
text: House of Pharaoh; his chief servants or princes.

title: Genesis 50:5
text: I have digged; it was common for men to prepare their burial-place long before their death, and Jacob is supposed to have prepared his in the cave of Machpelah, before he left Canaan.

title: Genesis 50:7
text: All the servants of Pharaoh; the elders; his principal men; a great company.   Genesis 50:9

title: Genesis 50:10
text: Beyond Jordan; on the west side; Moses having written this on the east of Jordan.

title: Genesis 50:11
text: Abel-mizraim; mourning of the Egyptians.

title: Genesis 50:13
text: Decent and affectionate respect should be paid to the mortal remains of departed friends, and their dying requests, so far as may be consistent, should be faithfully complied with.

title: Genesis 50:17
text: The trepass of thy brethren; in selling Joseph into Egypt.  Genesis 37:28

title: Genesis 50:18
text:
Fell down;  Genesis 37:7 Genesis 37:1 Ge 37.7,10. 
 
A guilty conscience naturally forebodes evil; and duty, as well as interest, requires that suitable measures should be taken to escape it.  Leviticus 26:36 Leviticus 26:40-45 Proverbs 28:1

title: Genesis 50:19
text: Am I in the place of God? it was not his business to punish them; that belonged to God.   Romans 12:19 Hebrews 10:30

title: Genesis 50:20
text:
Ye thought evil; in intending that Joseph should live and die a slave, and that his father should think that he had been torn in pieces. 
 
  God meant it unto good; that he should be greatly exalted, and be the means of saving his father, his brethren, and multitudes of others from death, and of illustrating to all future generations the wonderful providence of a wonder-working God. 
 
The object of God in suffering men to commit wickedness is very different from their object in committing it.  Whenever they intentionally do wrong, their object is evil, and they are evil.  His design in suffering it to be committed is good, and he is good.

title: Genesis 50:24
text: He sware;  Genesis 15:14 Genesis 46:4 Genesis 48:1

title: Genesis 50:25
text: Living faith in God gives good hope, through grace, that when the soul is absent from the body it will be present with the Lord; that in due time the body will be raised, immortal and glorious, to be united with the soul, and both be perfect in his likeness for ever.

title: Exodus 1:5
text: Seventy souls; including Jacob himself, Joseph, and his two sons.  Genesis 46:27

title: Exodus 1:6
text: No excellence of character, and no degree of authority, influence, or usefulness among men can keep off death.  It becomes all, therefore, to prepare for it, by setting their affections on things above, and laying up treasure, not on earth, but in heaven.

title: Exodus 1:8
text: Knew not Joseph; was ignorant of his eminent services.  Probably he belonged to a new dynasty.

title: Exodus 1:10
text:
Deal wisely; cunningly, in such a manner as to diminish their number and power. 
 
Tyrants often pretend that their unrighteous decrees are needful to the welfare of the state.  Were this true it would not excuse them, for the end does not justify the means.  But it is not true; the permanent good of individuals or communities is never promoted by doing wrong.

title: Exodus 1:11
text:
Burdens; exactions of labor and money. 
 
  Treasure-cities; fortified places for the keeping of military or other stores. 
 
  Pithom and Raamses; cities in the north-east part of Egypt, in or near Goshen.   Genesis 45:10 Genesis 47:11  
 
The providences of God often alarm men; and to prevent evils, real or imaginary, and obtain good, they frame and execute wicked devices.

title: Exodus 1:13
text: With rigor; with great cruelty.

title: Exodus 1:16
text: See them upon the stools; the Hebrew may be rendered, "ye shall look upon the stones."  The reference is supposed by some to be to a basin of stone, with a stone lid, used to wash the new-born infant.

title: Exodus 1:20
text: God dealt well with the midwives; blessed them because they would not obey the command of Pharaoh.

title: Exodus 1:21
text: Made them houses; increased and prospered their families.

title: Exodus 2:1
text: There went; had gone.  Amram the father of Moses had been married a number of years, and had at least two children, Miriam and Aaron, when Moses was born.   Exodus 2:4 Exodus 6:20 Exodus 7:7

title: Exodus 2:2
text: Goodly child; beautiful, well-favored.   Acts 7:20

title: Exodus 2:3
text:
Slime and--pitch; to keep out the water. 
 
  River's brink; the border of the river Nile.

title: Exodus 2:10
text:
Became her son; was adopted as her son. 
 
  Moses; orginally an Egyptian word, meaning saved from the water; but, by a slight change, made to signify in Hebrew drawn out.

title: Exodus 2:11
text: Was grown; had arrived to years of maturity.  He was forty years old; was "learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians," and was "mighty in words and in deeds."  Acts 7:22-23

title: Exodus 2:12
text: Slew the Egyptian; Moses may have received from God an intimation that he should deliver Israel,  Acts 7:25 ; but his present atempt was unauthorized and premature.

title: Exodus 2:14
text: With the first-fruits of our time, talents, property, and all that we possess, God is well pleased; and our own highest interests, as well as his glory, will be promoted by our devoting them to him.

title: Exodus 2:15
text:
Midian; a country south and south-east of Canaan, and near the Red sea. 
 
The efforts of men to perpetuate oppression may prepare the way for the deliverance of the oppressed.

title: Exodus 2:16
text: Priest of Midian; the Hebrew word for priest signifies also prince.  Genesis 41:45

title: Exodus 2:18
text: Reuel; probably the same as Jethro; or, as some think, the father of Jethro.   Exodus 3:1 Numbers 10:29

title: Exodus 2:22
text:
Gershom; meaning, a stranger there. 
 
God has a work for each one of his people; and he bestows upon them such mercies, and leads them through such trials as are best suited to fit them to perform it.

title: Exodus 2:24
text:
His covenant;  Genesis 15:14 Genesis 46:1 
 
The measures which men adopt to thwart the purposes of God or the good of his people, are often made the means of fulfilling them.

title: Exodus 2:25
text: Had respect; viewed them with compassion, and with the purpose to deliver them.

title: Exodus 3:1
text:
Jethro;  Exodus 2:1 
  Horeb; a mountain in Arabia between the two arms of the Red sea.

title: Exodus 3:2
text:
Angel of the Lord;  Exodus 3:4 Exodus 3:6 Genesis 16:7-14 Genesis 22:8-12 Genesis 24:1 
  Flame of fire--bush; the manner of the vision was a striking symbol of the condition of Israel, burned in the furnace of persecutions, but not consumed.

title: Exodus 3:5
text:
Holy ground; to be treated with peculiar reverence, because of the manifestation of Jehovah there. 
 
The place where God manifests himself has a peculiar sanctity; and if we should approach him acceptably, it must be with reverence and godly fear. 
 
The comfort of our thanksgivings to God, the peace we have through faith in Christ, and the joy of communion with him and his people, we should ever remember are mercies which come to us through the Saviour's blood.   Ephesians 2:13-22

title: Exodus 3:6
text: Look upon God;  John 1:18 John 14:1

title: Exodus 3:9
text: Jehovah is a just, and also a kind, compassionate, and merciful God. He tenderly sympathizes with all the distressed, especially such as wrongfully suffer; and in due time he will deliver the oppressed, and punish the oppressor.

title: Exodus 3:11
text:
Who am I? expressing a sense of his insufficiency. 
 
The kindness and condescension of God, in communing with his people, and permitting them to feast with him on the riches of his grace, are unspeakably great.

title: Exodus 3:12
text:
This shall be a token; the fulfilment of this prediction would be to Moses and Israel a sign that God had sent him. 
 
However unworthy men may be, and however insufficient in themselves for services to which God calls them, if he grant them his presence they may fearlessly go forward, expecting to be crowned with success.  Psalms 71:16 Philippians 4:13

title: Exodus 3:14
text: I am that I am; either, I am he who I am; or, I am that which I am.  In either case, the words denote the self-existent, eternal, and incomprehensible nature of Jehovah.  As the only original Being, he is the ground of all created being. Compare  John 8:58 Hebrews 13:8 Revelation of John 1:8

title: Exodus 3:15
text: The eternal, unchanging perfections of Jehovah are a proper ground for implicit confidence in him, and prompt, persevering obedience to all his commands.

title: Exodus 3:16
text: Elders of Israel; their head men.

title: Exodus 3:18
text: Met with us; appeared to us and given us directions.

title: Exodus 3:19
text: No, not by a mighty hand; not though I deal with him by a mighty hand.  He would withstand all God's mighty judgments, till the last great plague.

title: Exodus 3:20
text: Neither the power of God, nor the truth of his promises, nor the certainty that they will be accomplished, renders the use of means unnecessary, or furnishes any ground to expect his blessing in the neglect of them.

title: Exodus 3:21
text: Give this people favor; lead the Egyptians to furnish them the things they should ask for, and which they had doubtless earned.  Exodus 12:35-36

title: Exodus 3:22
text:
Borrow; the word rendered borrow, means also, to request or demand, not expecting to make a return.   Joshua 15:18 I Samuel 8:10 Psalms 2:8  
 
  Jewels; the word rendered jewels means also furniture, utensils, and goods of various descriptions.   Genesis 24:53 Genesis 27:3 Deuteronomy 22:5   I Kings 6:7 II Chronicles 34:12  
 
  Spoil the Egyptians; carry away the rich treasures which they shall give you.  Exodus 12:36 Genesis 15:14

title: Exodus 4:1
text: It is often exceedingly difficult to induce even the best of men in all things heartily to believe God; and were it not for his boundless compassion and grace, instead of being saved by faith, they would perish through unbelief.

title: Exodus 4:2
text: A rod; a sheperd's crook or staff.

title: Exodus 4:5
text: That they may believe; this was the object of the miracle, to lead the people to believe what Moses should say, and that God had truly sent him.

title: Exodus 4:6
text: Leprous as snow; white with leprosy, a loathsome disease, universally regarded as incurable, except by the immediate power of God.  The twofold miracle of a sudden production and sudden cure of this disease would be to the Hebrews a most convincing proof of God's presence.

title: Exodus 4:8
text:
Believe the voice; its testimony to the fact that God had sent Moses to deliver his people from bondage. 
 
God in his mercy furnishes his people with all needful aid for the services to which he calls them; so that in reliance on him they may safely follow his directions, expecting that he will give them success.

title: Exodus 4:10
text: Not eloquent; not of ready utterance, or persuasive power of speech.

title: Exodus 4:13
text:
Send, I pray; by some one else, not by me. 
 
Men are very apt to start objections against doing what they dislike, and to desire that others may perform the labors and bear the trials of difficult services, rather than themselves.

title: Exodus 4:14
text:
Against Moses; on account of his great and unreasonable reluctance to do what God commanded. 
 
God is angry with men when they are afraid or ashamed to obey him, or seek to excuse themselves from doing their duty.

title: Exodus 4:15
text: Put words in his mouth; tell him what to say.

title: Exodus 4:16
text: Instead of God; make known to him the will of God, and direct him what to do.

title: Exodus 4:18
text: In doing the will of God we should endeavor not needlessly to exasperate men, and should use all suitable means to secure their approbation and aid.

title: Exodus 4:20
text:
His sons; Gershom and Eliezer,  Exodus 18:3-4 . 
 
  Returned; set out to return. 
 
  The rod of God;  Exodus 4:2 Exodus 4:1

title: Exodus 4:21
text:
Put in thy hand; directed, and would enable him to perform. 
 
  Will harden his heart; by making known to him his duty and the reasons for doing it, and yet suffering him to take his own way, and thus obstinately and wickedly refuse to obey God's most wise, just, and reasonable commands.

title: Exodus 4:22
text: My son--my first-born; greatly beloved, and greatly favored.

title: Exodus 4:23
text: Slay thy son;  Exodus 12:29-30:1

title: Exodus 4:24
text:
Inn; the place where they stopped for the night. 
 
  Kill him; threatened Moses with death, should he still continue to neglect to circumcise his son.  As he was called to be the leader of Israel, it was preeminently important that he should be an example of obedience to all God's ordinances.  He seems to have culpably delayed this rite out of regard to Zipporah's wishes. 
 
Those who are called to guide others in the path of duty should be careful to walk in it themselves, and in all things to set an example which others may safely follow.

title: Exodus 4:25
text:
Sharp stone; sharp flints were then used for knives. 
 
  A bloody husband; in the original, a bridegroom of blood; that is, a bridegroom to whom I was espoused under the necessity of performing upon my offspring the bloody rite of circumcision.

title: Exodus 4:26
text: He let him go; the Lord ceased to threaten him with death for neglecting his duty.

title: Exodus 4:27
text: In the mount; at mount Horeb.   Exodus 3:1 Exodus 4:14

title: Exodus 4:28
text: Signs; miracles which God had commanded him to perform.

title: Exodus 4:31
text:
Visited the children of Israel; appeared for them in mercy, and was about to deliver them from bondage. 
 
God is often better to his people than their fears, and always better than their deserts.  Difficulties in the way of duty, which may seem insuperable, when they engage in it disappear or are readily overcome. The yoke which appeared to be so galling is easy, and the burden which seemed so heavy is light.   Matthew 11:29-30

title: Exodus 5:2
text: The commands of God are reasonable and binding on all who know them. If men do not obey them, it is because they have no disposition to obey.

title: Exodus 5:3
text:
The desert; the desert of Shur, lying between Egypt and Canaan. 
 
  Fall upon us with pestilence; punish us with death for neglecting to obey his command.

title: Exodus 5:4
text: Let the people; hinder their working.

title: Exodus 5:6
text:
Taskmasters; Egyptians appointed to exact of the Israelites the required labor. 
 
  Officers; Israelites appointed to execute the directions of the taskmasters.   Exodus 5:14-16

title: Exodus 5:7
text: Straw; to be mixed with the clay, to make the bricks more firm and durable.  They were not burned, but dried in the sun.

title: Exodus 5:8
text:
The tale of the bricks; the full amount which was required. 
 
Wicked men often imagine that the friends of Jehovah have no real regard for him; that their professions are mere pretence, and that if they were not hypocritical, selfish, and idle, they would not wish to spend time in worshipping him.

title: Exodus 5:9
text: Vain words; false pretences, about being required by God to go and worship.

title: Exodus 5:21
text:
Judge; judge you for the evil you have brought upon us, in occasioning an increase of our burdens. 
 
  Made our savor to be abhorred; made us odious to Pharaoh and his people, and thus disposed them to deal more cruelly with us. 
 
  Put a sword in their hand; giving them a pretext for killing us.

title: Exodus 5:22
text: Returned unto the Lord; expressed to him his feelings, which were as unreasonable towards Jehovah as those of the Israelitish officers were towards him; and much more inexcusable, as he had been expressly forewarned that Pharaoh would for a time resist his efforts.  Exodus 3:19-20

title: Exodus 5:23
text: Good men in pursuing a good object in the right way, if not immediately successful, are liable to become discouraged, and to complain not merely of men, but also of God.

title: Exodus 6:1
text:
Strong hand; under the judgments of God, Pharaoh would not only consent, but be very urgent to have them go. 
 
When men despair of help from themselves and from creatures, and look to God, he shows both his readiness and his power to do for them what they need.

title: Exodus 6:2
text: I am the LORD; in the Hebrew, I am Jehovah.  This is the first time that the declaration, I am Jehovah, occurs in the Bible in this naked form.  Its meaning is, that the name is a pledge that he who bears it will fulfil all his promises.  The word Jehovah signifies HE IS, and, like the equvalent name, I AM, it denotes the self-existence, independence, immutability, and infinite fulness of the divine Being.

title: Exodus 6:3
text:
God Almighty; see  Genesis 17:1 Genesis 35:1 
  By my name JEHOVAH was I not known to them.  It had been known from the beginning that God's name was Jehovah,  Genesis 4:2 .  We have reason to believe that God himself, who named man Adam, also named himself Jehovah.  But in his revelations to the patriarchs, God had not appropriated this name to himself in a peculiar way, as he now did.  He had said to them, I am God Almighty; I am Jehovah, the God of Abraham, etc.; but not simply, I am Jehovah.  The name of God comprehends the sum of all his attributes.  To manifest God's name to men, is to manifest his true character.   John 17:6   When it is said that God keeps believers through his name, the meaning is, that he keeps them through those divine attributes which his name comprehends.  John 17:11   When God says, I am Jehovah, he means that the fulness of divine perfections which that name includes, is a sure pledge that he will redeem all his promises to his covenant people.

title: Exodus 6:8
text:
I did swear;  Genesis 15:18 Genesis 26:3 Genesis 28:13 Genesis 35:1 
 
Those attributes of God which are implied in the names that he appropriates to himself in his word, are made known to men in his providence.  Both by what he says and by what he does, he shows that he is Jehovah.

title: Exodus 6:12
text:
Uncircumcised lips; not eloquent.  Exodus 4:10  
 
Even the best of men are strongly tempted to walk by sight, not by faith; and if appearances are against them, are liable to be discouraged, though all the perfections of Jehovah are pledged in their behalf.

title: Exodus 6:14
text:
vv. 14-27 
 
The special design of this table is to show the descent of Moses and Aaron.  It therefore proceeds no further than Levi, the third son of Jacob, and gives full details respecting his descendants.

title: Exodus 6:29
text: The utter insufficiency of men, and their entire dependence on God, instead of being a reason why they should not in all things obey him, are a reason why they should obey him; and in doing his will they will find his grace to be sufficient for them, and his strength made perfect in their weakness.  II Corinthians 12:9 2Co 12.9;l Heb 11.34|

title: Exodus 7:1
text: I have made thee a god to Pharaoh--thy prophet; as God communicates to men his will through prophets, so Aaron should make known to Pharaoh the messages which Moses, acting in God's name, should direct him to deliver.

title: Exodus 7:3
text: Harden Pharaoh's heart; as a punishment for his sins, he was given up to hardness of heart and blindness of mind, so that God's dealings with him served only to increase his obduracy and wickedness.

title: Exodus 7:4
text: That I may lay my hand upon Egypt; this was not Pharaoh's object in refusing to obey God, but it was God's object in suffering him to do it.

title: Exodus 7:5
text:
The Egyptians shall know; that Jehovah is almighty, and able to do his pleasure. 
 
The Lord takes occasion, even from the obstinacy and wickedness of men, to manifest his character and show forth his glory, to the terror of his enemies and the joy of his friends.

title: Exodus 7:11
text:
The sorcerers--the magicians; men who pretended to supernatural power, and were accustomed to practise deceits upon their fellow-men.  II Timothy 3:8   Pharaoh wished to see whether his own magicians could perform like wonders. 
 
  With their enchantments; certain mysterious forms of words by which they pretended to work wonders.

title: Exodus 7:12
text: And they became serpents; this was probably done by sleight of hand.

title: Exodus 7:13
text:
He hardened Pharaoh's heart; this in the original is the same as in  Exodus 7:22 , where it is rendered, Pharaoh's heart was hardened. 
 
Things which, in the course of divine providence, take place through the wickedness of men, are sometimes, in the Bible, ascribed to God. This shows his all-controlling agency, though he cannot be tempted, neither does he at any time tempt men to commit sin.   James 1:13-14

title: Exodus 7:19
text: Streams--rivers; the various branches of the Nile, and the canals leading from it.

title: Exodus 7:22
text:
Did so with their enchantments; imitated in appearance the miracle of Moses.  As Pharaoh did not love the truth, God suffered the magicians to deceive him to a certain point by their enchantments.  II Thessalonians 2:11   Thus his heart was hardened, and he persisted in his obduracy. 
 
When men dislike to obey God, and seek excuses for their neglect, they can generally find them; and when they wish to harden themselves against him, he often suffers them to do it, even to their ruin.

title: Exodus 8:6
text: God can make even the meanest of his creatures instruments of punishment to those who rebel against him; and none are so exalted that they can resist him and prosper.  Though for a time he waits upon them, not willing that they should perish, yet "he that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy."

title: Exodus 8:7
text: And brought up frogs; see  Exodus 7:1

title: Exodus 8:9
text: Glory over me; or, according to many, Appoint me a time.

title: Exodus 8:13
text: Villages; yards, or grounds about the houses of the Egyptians.

title: Exodus 8:15
text:
He hardened his heart; by refusing to obey God.  Here the hardening of his heart is ascribed to Pharaoh, and yet the process was probably the same as when it was ascribed to God.   Exodus 7:13  
 
In one sense it was ascribed to God, and in another to Pharaoh. 
 
Those misgivings, confessions, resolutions, and promises which are extorted only by the endurance of present or the fear of future evils, are not to be depended on.  When those evils or fears are removed, their apparent good effects will be like the morning cloud or early dew, which quickly pass away.   Hosea 6:4

title: Exodus 8:16
text: Lice; the word translated lice is by many supposed to mean gnats.

title: Exodus 8:18
text: The magicians did so; smote the earth to bring forth lice.  Some suppose that as they had no previous warning of this plague, and no time to prepare their deceptions, they could not imitate this miracle even in appearance; and to hide their shame, confessed that it was the effect of divine power.

title: Exodus 8:21
text: Swarms of flies; the word in the original, translated swarms of flies, means, according to some, a mixed multitude of noisome insects; according to others, a particular kind of insect.

title: Exodus 8:22
text:
Sever; separate. 
 
However great the calamities which God brings upon his enemies, he is ever able and willing to protect his people and deliver them from temptations, while he reserves the wicked to the day of judgment to be punished.  And though now they may often seem to be in many respects alike, yet hereafter all men will return and discern between him that serveth God and him that serveth him not.   Malachi 3:18 II Peter 2:9

title: Exodus 8:24
text: Corrupted; destroyed, devoured.   Psalms 78:45   This word is most naturally understood of the destruction of the products and wealth of the land.  For this reason some suppose that it here denotes a species of beetle, common in Egypt, that devours whatever comes in its way.

title: Exodus 8:26
text:
Meet; suitable, fit, proper. 
 
  Sacrifice the abomination; various animals were worshipped by the Egyptians, and should they see the Israelites sacrifice them they would be greatly offended.

title: Exodus 8:32
text: Pharaoh hardened his heart;  Exodus 8:15

title: Exodus 9:3
text: Murrain; a pestilence among cattle.

title: Exodus 9:6
text:
All the cattle; great numbers of all kinds, as appears from a comparison with  Exodus 9:19 . 
 
The brute creation often suffer through the wickedness of man, and are visited with calamities as a punishment of his sins.

title: Exodus 9:9
text: It shall become small dust; the meaning of these words is, that in connection with this sign a fine irritating dust, produced by the power of Jehovah, filled the land, producing painful sores in man and beast. The handful of ashes from the furnace is called this dust because it represents it symbolically.

title: Exodus 9:10
text: Blains; violent and painful inflammation.

title: Exodus 9:11
text: Whatever power the wicked claim, or whatever influence theymay be able to exert over their fellow-men, they are entirely dependent upon God; and if they continue in rebellion against him, nothing can shield them from his indignation.

title: Exodus 9:12
text: The Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh;  Exodus 4:21 Exodus 7:3 Exodus 8:1

title: Exodus 9:16
text:
Raised thee up; caused thee to stand; continued thee in life, notwithstanding all thy wickedness. 
 
  My name may be declared; my character, as manifested in my wonderful works, may be made known to all people. 
 
All men are under sacred obligations to honor God.  If they will not, by obeying his commands, he will glorify his justice in their punishment, and ultimately in their ruin.

title: Exodus 9:21
text: Men who believe God, will use the means which are needful to escape the evils he threatens; while those who disbelieve, by neglecting the means of escape, will bring those evils upon them.

title: Exodus 9:23
text: Fire; lightening.

title: Exodus 9:27
text: However much the wicked may try to justify themselves and condemn Jehovah for bringing evils upon them, they will ultimately all confess that he is right and they are wrong; and will feel that they are the cause of their own ruin.

title: Exodus 9:29
text: The earth is the Lord's; he is its rightful owner and universal governor.

title: Exodus 9:31
text: Was bolled; the bolls of flax are the round seed-cups at the summit of the stalks.  Many prefer to render, the flax was in flower.

title: Exodus 9:32
text: Rye; the Hebrew word means spelt-- Isaiah 28:25  and  Ezekiel 4:9  --a species of beardless wheat common in Egypt.

title: Exodus 9:34
text: The long-suffering and patience of God, his kindness in removing evils and in bestowing new mercies, are often abused to the increase of transgression, and a preparation for more aggravated woe.

title: Exodus 10:2
text: The glory of God in the manifestation of his true character, is one great design of all his dispensations towards the children of men.

title: Exodus 10:4
text: Locusts; a species of insect resembling our grasshopper, but much larger.  They fly with the wind in immense swarms that darken the air, and where they alight they cover the face of the ground, and devour every green thing.

title: Exodus 10:7
text: The wickedness and obstinacy of rulers are often the means of great calamities to the people.  And when, instead of being what they ought to be, ministers of God for good, they become ministers of evil, it is right for the people by suitable means to seek a change for the better.

title: Exodus 10:10
text:
Be so with you, as I will let you go; may he deal with you just so as I shall let you go.  He means, I will not let you go; and if your God grants your requests in the same way that I do, you will fare hard. 
 
  Look to it; for evil is before you; that is, according to our version, by persisting in your demand you will bring upon yourselves destruction.  Compare  Exodus 10:28 .  But many prefer to render, Consider that your designs are evil.

title: Exodus 10:11
text: When men become convinced that they must yield to God or perish, their yielding is often partial, or in pretence merely; and when they find that their submission must be sincere, and that they must in all things follow the will of God, they sometimes become vexed and determine that they will not regard him.

title: Exodus 10:13
text: East wind; locusts come to Palestine and Egypt from their breeding places in the Arabian desert on the east.

title: Exodus 10:17
text:
This death only; this deadly plague, implying that he would not give occasion to Jehovah to send another. 
 
Increasing sin brings increasing misery; and men often earnestly seek deliverance, not from the love and practice of iniquity, but from its consequences.

title: Exodus 10:19
text: The Red sea; which lies east of Egypt.  It is common for locusts to perish in this way.

title: Exodus 10:21
text: Even darkness which may be felt; rather, so that one shall grope in darkness.

title: Exodus 10:28
text: However great the miseries which the sins of men bring upon them, if left without the grace of God to pursue their own chosen way, they will grow worse and worse till they perish.

title: Exodus 11:1
text:
The Lord said; or, the Lord had said, as the Hebrew may be rendered.  Compare  Genesis 12:1 .  Thus the first three verses of  Exodus 11:1  will form a sort of parenthesis,  Exodus 11:4  being immediately connected with the last verse of the preceding chapter,  Exodus 10:29 . 
 
  Thrust you out; be exceedingly earnest to have them all immediately depart.  Exodus 11:8 .

title: Exodus 11:2
text:
Borrow; ask, solicit, or demand.   Exodus 3:22 . 
 
  Jewels; the Hebrew word here used means also vessels, utensils, garments, and weapons.   Exodus 3:22 .

title: Exodus 11:3
text:
Gave the people favor; inclined the Egyptians willingly to give the Israelites what they asked, so as to hasten their departure.  This however, did not take place till after Moses had left Pharaoh, and brought upon him the judgment he had denounced. 
 
All hearts are in the hands of the Lord, and he can turn them as the rivers of waters are turned.  When he sees best, he can influence his enemies to favor his people, and gladly to bestow upon them whatever they desire.

title: Exodus 11:5
text:
Behind the mill; their grain was ground in a small hand-mill of two stones, by female servants who sat behind the mill and turned the upper stone.  The maid-servant suffers for the sin of Pharaoh.  In respect to Israel, she may be innocent; but in respect to God, she and her first-born both belong to a fallen and guilty race, and God may deal with them as he sees good. 
 
As God is the giver and preserver of life, he has a perfect right, at such times and by such means as he sees best, to take it away.

title: Exodus 11:7
text: Not a dog move his tongue; a proverbial expression denoting entire peace and safety.

title: Exodus 11:8
text: When God undertakes to deliver his people he will accomplish it; and what men do to prevent this he will overrule to render their deliverance in due time more complete, triumphant, and glorious.

title: Exodus 11:9
text: The Lord said; had said.  He had foretold this, and all things had occurred according to his predictions.   Exodus 3:19 Exodus 4:21 Exodus 7:3 Exodus 7:4   Exodus 10:1 .

title: Exodus 12:1
text: Spake; this command seems to have been given previously to the ninth plague, which lasted three days. The first thirteen verses contain particular directions for the observance of the first passover; the next seven,  Exodus 12:14-20 , general directions for its observance in all coming generations.

title: Exodus 12:2
text:
This month; the month Abib or Nisan, answering to the last part of March and the first part of April. 
 
  The beginning; of their ecclesiastical year.  It had been the seventh month; and Tishri, answering to the last part of September and the first part of October, had been the first month, and so in the civil concerns it still continued to be.

title: Exodus 12:3
text:
Lamb; the word in the original means either a sheep or a goat.  It was to be one year old.   Exodus 12:5 . 
 
The directions of God to his ancient people were suited to impress upon them the evil of sin, the necessity of an atonement, and the efficacy of that precious blood which was to be shed for many for the remission of sins.   Matthew 26:28

title: Exodus 12:4
text: According to the number; about the number that would at a meal consume a lamb.

title: Exodus 12:5
text:
Without blemish; perfect, sound, healthy. 
 
  Of the first year; literally a son of a year, that is, a year old.

title: Exodus 12:6
text: In the evening; literally between the two evenings.  The first evening began about the middle of the afternoon, when the daily evening sacrifice was offered; the second at sunset.

title: Exodus 12:7
text: Upper door-post; the lintel or beam that goes across over the door.

title: Exodus 12:8
text:
Fire; as the paschal lamb was a type of Christ,  I Corinthians 5:7 , the fire may be regarded as an emblem of the wrath of God which he endured in our stead. 
 
  Unleavened bread; bread not raised with yeast, leaven, or any fermenting substance.  As leaven works in secret and unseen, it is the emblem of hypocrisy and deceit.  They were on these occasions to abstain from it, to impress on their minds the importance of worshipping God sincerely, in spirit and in truth.   I Corinthians 5:6-8  
 
  Bitter herbs; as a memorial of their bitter servitude in Egypt. But as this was a type of the worse bondage of sin, these bitter herbs may be taken to represent the bitter fruits of sin, and the necessity of repentance in order to salvation. 
 
It was not enough for the deliverance of Israel that the paschal lamb should be slain and its blood struck upon the door-posts, but they must eat of the lamb, and thus a union be formed between it and them.  So the blood of Christ will save none but such as are by faith united to him.   John 6:53 I Corinthians 6:17

title: Exodus 12:9
text:
Sodden; boiled. 
 
  Purtenance; head, legs, heart, liver, lungs, and kidney.  The lamb after being dressed was to be roasted whole.

title: Exodus 12:10
text: That which remaineth; which they did not eat.

title: Exodus 12:11
text:
Loins girded; they wore loose flowing garments, which, when they were about to travel, were fastened close by a girdle, strap, or belt around the body.  This girdle was to be thus fastened, that they might be prepared to start immediately on their journey towards Canaan. 
 
  The Lord's passover; that, out of regard to which the Lord, when he should slay the Egyptians, would pass over, spare, and not destroy the Israelites.  The blood of this lamb, sprinkled by God's command on the doorposts, typified the blood of the Lamb of God, Jesus Christ, out of regard to which God passes over, spares, and saves those who obey him. Hence Christ is said to be "our Passover."   I Corinthians 5:7   By eating of the lamb the Israelites were taught the necessity of union by faith to Jesus Christ, as well as of reliance on his blood for salvation.  John 6:48-58

title: Exodus 12:12
text: The gods of Egypt; according to some, by their visible destruction, as afterwards in the case of Dagon,  I Samuel 5:3-4 ; or, as others prefer, the gods (marg. princes) of Egypt may refer to the first-born of the ruling priests and princes, and of various animals worshipped there.  See  Numbers 33:4 .

title: Exodus 12:13
text:
A token; an evidence that they had complied with the Lord's directions, and were under his protection. 
 
  The plague; that which destroyed the first-born of Egypt.  Exodus 12:23  
 
It is through the blood of Christ, typified by the blood of the paschal lamb, that God pardons men, and saves them from that destruction which as sinners they deserve.  1Co 5.7

title: Exodus 12:14
text: A memorial; a means of keeping in remembrance their preservation and deliverance when the Egyptians were destroyed.   Exodus 12:27

title: Exodus 12:15
text:
Seven days; from the evening of the fourteenth to the evening of the twenty-first day of the month.   Exodus 12:18  
 
  Cut off from Israel; see note to  Genesis 17:14 .

title: Exodus 12:16
text:
Convocation; an assembling together for public worship. 
 
  No manner of work; except of necessity and mercy.  Compare  Matthew 12:11 .

title: Exodus 12:17
text: For ever; to the end of the Jewish state.

title: Exodus 12:21
text: The passover; the lamb that was to be slain on that occasion.

title: Exodus 12:22
text: Hyssop; a low shrub, or herb, common in eastern countries.

title: Exodus 12:24
text: The ordinances which God appoints as memorials of his goodness should be carefully observed by his people, not in outward form merely, but in spirit and in truth, with repentance for sin, faith in the Redeemer, and gratitude for his infinite mercy.

title: Exodus 12:27
text: The ordinances of God, when understood, are adapted to impress divine truth, especially upon the minds of children and youth.  The meaning of them should therefore be carefully explained by parents and teachers, that all may apprehend it, and receive the benefit which it is suited to impart.

title: Exodus 12:32
text: Bless me; seek of God a blessing for me.

title: Exodus 12:33
text:
We be all dead; we shall be, if we retain the Israelites any longer. 
 
God can so order events in his providence, that oppressors will be anxious to get rid of those whom they oppress; and all will at length see that, under his righteous government, the condition of the oppressor is more dreadful than that of the oppressed.

title: Exodus 12:34
text: Kneading-troughs; vessels containing their dough.

title: Exodus 12:35
text: Borrowed; asked, requested.   Exodus 3:21-22 Exodus 11:2-3

title: Exodus 12:36
text:
Lent unto them; granted them what they desired, in order to hasten their departure. 
 
  Spoiled the Egyptians; by carrying away much of their substance.  Genesis 15:14

title: Exodus 12:37
text:
Rameses; a city which the Israelites had built, and where they were now assembled.   Exodus 1:11  
 
  Succoth; a place of encampment between Rameses and Suez. 
 
  Six hundred thousand--men; this shows that the whole number of souls was probably over two millions.   Psalms 105:37

title: Exodus 12:40
text: Four hundred and thirty years; from the time the promise was made to Abraham.   Genesis 15:13   About half this time was spent in Canaan, and the rest in Egypt.   Galatians 3:17

title: Exodus 12:41
text: If the oppressed believe and obey God, their deliverance from the power of their oppressors will not be delayed any longer than is needful to make such deliverance most for the glory of God, and the final good of all who trust in him.

title: Exodus 12:43
text: Stranger; a foreigner who had not embraced the Jewish religion, and was not circumcised.   Exodus 12:45 Exodus 12:48

title: Exodus 12:46
text: Neither--break a bone; for the symbolical and prophetic meaning of this see  John 19:33 John 19:36

title: Exodus 13:2
text:
Sanctify; set apart for God, to be devoted peculiarly to his service.   Exodus 13:12  
 
  All the first-born; as a memorial of the preservation of the first-born of man and beast among the Israelites when the first-born among the Egyptians were destroyed, all the first-born males of man and beast were devoted to the Lord.  The male children were to be in all cases redeemed; the first-born of unclean beasts to be redeemed or slain; the first-born of clean beasts were to be offered in sacrifice, and when certain specified parts had been burned, the remainder belonged to the priests.  The particular details are given in the Levitical law.

title: Exodus 13:4
text: Abib; meaning, green corn.  This was the seventh month, called also Nisan.   Exodus 12:2

title: Exodus 13:7
text: In the Bible the same or similar instructions are often repeated, that the truth may become familiar, and make a strong, abiding impression on the heart.

title: Exodus 13:9
text: A sign; a means of keeping their deliverance in remembrance, and making God's commands familiar to their minds.   Exodus 13:16 Proverbs 3:3  The Jews interpreted these directions literally, writing certain precepts of the law on parchment, and wearing them as evidences or ornaments of piety.   Matthew 23:5

title: Exodus 13:10
text: In his season; on the fourteenth day of Abib annually.

title: Exodus 13:13
text:
Every firstling of an ass--and all the first-born of man--shalt thou redeem;  Numbers 3:46-51  
  Shalt break his neck; that they might not appropriate it unredeemed to their own use, this precept was added.

title: Exodus 13:14
text:
What is this? why are the first-born thus devoted to God and redeemed?  What is the meaning of it? 
 
The ordinances of God are designed to increase the knowledge, perpetuate the remembrance, and extend the efficacy of his truth; and the proper understanding of these ordinances is suited to benefit all, especially the young.

title: Exodus 13:15
text: Would hardly; refused.

title: Exodus 13:17
text: Through the--land of the Philistines; the direct way from Egypt to Canaan.

title: Exodus 13:18
text:
Red sea; which separates Egypt from Arabia.  It is about 1,400 miles long, and upon an average about 150 miles wide.  It extends from the straits of Babelmandel on the south, which unite it with the Indian ocean, to the isthmus of Suez on the north, which separates it from the Mediterranean sea.  At the north end it divides into two arms or gulfs, between which is the wilderness in which the children of Israel spent forty years.  The western arm, called the gulf of Suez, is about 190 miles long and on an average 21 miles wide.  It was near the head of this gulf, that the Hebrews passed and the Egyptians were drowned.  Exodus 14:21-30   The eastern arm, called the gulf of Akabah, and anciently the Aelaintic gulf or gulf of Elath, is about 100 miles long, and on an average about 15 miles wide.  On this gulf was Eziongeber, a port from which Solomon sent his ships to Ophir for gold.  I Kings 9:26  From Rameses to the Red sea was about forty or fifty miles. 
 
  Harnessed; armed, equipped, and in order. 
 
The way through this world in which God leads his people is often very different from what they expect or desire, and very different from what any finite mind at the time would think to be best. 
 
"But though they go far wandering round, 'Tis the right way to Canaan's ground."

title: Exodus 13:19
text: The bones of Joseph;  Genesis 50:25

title: Exodus 13:20
text:
Etham; a place near Suez, at the head of the western branch of the Red sea. 
 
  The wilderness; of Etham.

title: Exodus 13:21
text: Pillar of a cloud; a cloud in the form of a pillar, to shield them from the sun and guide them in the daytime, and to give them light by night.

title: Exodus 13:22
text:
Took not away the pillar; it continued with them through the wilderness, as the emblem of the divine presence.  Exodus 14:24 Exodus 33:9-14  
 
God is the guide and protector of his people.  To follow him is perfectly safe.  And after he has, by the wisest means and in the best way, prepared them for heaven, he will receive them there.

title: Exodus 14:2
text:
That they turn; to the south, and go down on the west side of the west arm of the Red sea, instead of passing northward round the head of the sea, as they might have done. 
 
  Pi-hahiroth--Migdol and--Baal-zephon; places south of Etham, where they would be shut in between the mountains and the sea; so that should Pharaoh follow them with his army, they would, without a miracle, have no way of escape.

title: Exodus 14:4
text:
Harden Pharaoh's heart;  Exodus 4:21 Ex 4.21 
 
  I will be honored; in the destruction of Pharaoh and his host. 
 
If men would not have their hearts hardened, they must not continue knowingly to disobey God.  If they thus disobey, all the blame will rest upon themselves.

title: Exodus 14:5
text: Turned against the people; against permitting them to escape.

title: Exodus 14:8
text: With a high hand; by a high hand; that is, by the hand of Jehovah, lifted up with might for their deliverance.

title: Exodus 14:9
text: When suffering the consequences of sin and fearing destruction, men often appear to be penitent and disposed to reform; but if when they are relieved and their fears pass away, they rush again into sin, they not unfrequently become more hardened, reckless, and wicked than ever, till, given up of God, they sink into ruin.

title: Exodus 14:15
text: It is the duty of men not merely to pray, but to act; and unless they go forward in the way of duty, their prayers will not avail.  God helps those who do what he requires to help themselves.

title: Exodus 14:18
text: The dispensations of Providence, as well as the publication of divine truth, are to some, by being improved, a savor of life unto life; to others, by being abused, a savor of death unto death; and God is honored in the salvation of the one and the destruction of the other.

title: Exodus 14:19
text: Angel of God; the Angel of the covenant, who was afterwards made flesh and dwelt among men.   Deuteronomy 1:32-33 Psalms 99:6-7 Isaiah 63:8-16   John 1:14 I Corinthians 10:9   Compare  Exodus 14:24-25 .  He was now present in the cloud; and when he removed, the cloud removed with him.

title: Exodus 14:20
text:
To them; the Egyptians. 
 
  These; the Israelites. 
 
Many things are very plain, and give great light and comfort to those who obey God, which appear exceedingly dark and perplexing to those who knowingly disobey him.

title: Exodus 14:24
text:
The morning-watch; the night was divided into three watches of four hours each.  The morning-watch  was the last, and began eight hours after sunset. 
 
  Looked; his look was accompanied with visible signs of his displeasure.  See  Exodus 14:25 .

title: Exodus 14:28
text: The way of transgressors is hard.  God is against them, and the time will come when they will see this.  Happy will it be if they see it while his is waiting to be gracious, saying, "Turn ye, turn ye; for why will ye die?"  and hearken to his voice, instead of madly persevering in rebellion against him.

title: Exodus 15:1
text: Those dispensations of Providence which excite our greatest fears, often so result as to call forth our loudest praises.

title: Exodus 15:2
text: A habitation; a place for his public worship.

title: Exodus 15:7
text: They that, being often reproved, continue to harden their hearts, will be suddenly destroyed, and that without remedy.  II Chronicles 36:16 Proverbs 6:14-15 Proverbs 29:1

title: Exodus 15:8
text:
Blast of thy nostrils; the wind which made the sea go back,  Exodus 14:21 , here represented as the breath of the Almighty.  Exodus 15:10  
 
  The depths were congealed; made to stand upon either side like walls of ice.

title: Exodus 15:10
text:
Didst blow with thy wind; a wind opposite to that which made the sea retire, and which hastened its return to overwhelm the Egyptians. 
 
When the enemies of God are most confident of success, they are often the nearest to destruction.

title: Exodus 15:12
text: The earth; the sea in the depths of the earth.   Psalms 77:14-20

title: Exodus 15:13
text: Thy holy habitation; the land of Canaan, where God would delight to dwell with his people.  But perhaps here, and  Exodus 14:17 , there is a prophetic allusion to mount Zion, which became God's special dwelling-place.

title: Exodus 15:14
text: Palestina; that is, the country of the Philistines.  See note,  Isaiah 14:29 .

title: Exodus 15:15
text: Dukes; leaders, princes.

title: Exodus 15:16
text:
Pass over; over the desert and through the intervening countries, to take possession of Canaan. 
 
  Purchased; redeemed or delivered from bondage, to be his peculiar people. 
 
That fear of coming evil which prevents exertion and leads to despair, instead of delivering from danger, only increases it, and prevents escape.

title: Exodus 15:17
text: The mountain of thine inheritance; the land of Canaan, especially Zion, and the temple where he would dwell.  See note,  Exodus 15:13 .

title: Exodus 15:20
text:
The prophetess; appointed of God to instruct the women, and lead them in their devotions.   Numbers 12:1-2 Micah 6:4 . 
 
  Timbrel; a musical instrument like the tambourine.

title: Exodus 15:21
text:
Miriam answered; she led the women, who sung responsively with the men. 
 
Great deliverances should be celebrated with manifestations of hearty gratitude to God, and sincere devotion of body and soul to his service.

title: Exodus 15:23
text: Marah; meaning bitterness; where was a fountain of bitter water.

title: Exodus 15:25
text:
Statute--ordinance; rule, direction, or decree, mentioned  Exodus 15:26 Jeremiah 7:22-23 . 
 
  Proved them; tried them by his providence, and thus gave them opportunity to show whether they would obey him.   Genesis 22:1

title: Exodus 15:26
text:
Healeth thee; removes all plagues, sicknesses, and infirmities, such as those which they had witnessed in Egypt.  These are always regarded in the holy Scriptures as chastisements for sin.  See  Deuteronomy 28:59 Deuteronomy 28:61 .  The outward healing of the body is a symbol of the more glorious healing and sanctifying of the soul by God's grace. 
 
The human heart cannot be safely trusted.  At one time it will sing praises to God, and at another murmur against him.  All true confidence in God, and all genuine love to him, are the fruit of his Spirit; and to him belongs the glory of every thing spiritually good in men.

title: Exodus 15:27
text: Elim; a place south-east of Marah, and on the way to mount Sinai.

title: Exodus 16:1
text: Fifteenth day of the second month; just one month after they started from Egypt.

title: Exodus 16:3
text:
Kill--with hunger; they had hitherto lived on provisions which they brought with them, or obtained by the way; but as they now entered the wilderness, where they thought they could not obtain any, they feared they should perish. 
 
Men are prone to undervalue their mercies and to magnify their trials. By comparing their present with their past condition they become discontented, and thus unfit themselves for duty and dishonor God.

title: Exodus 16:4
text: Prove them; put them to trial.  For the meaning of this, see  Deuteronomy 8:2-3 Deuteronomy 8:16 .

title: Exodus 16:5
text:
The sixth day; the sixth working day, the day before the Sabbath. The Sabbath is spoken of as an institution already existing and well known. 
 
Such was God's regard for the Sabbath before the establishment of the Jewish ritual, and before the ten commandments had been written on tables of stone, that he wrought a stupendous miracle, that his people might continue to keep it holy.

title: Exodus 16:6
text: Ye shall know; by the Lord's providing you a miraculous supply of flesh.   Exodus 16:13

title: Exodus 16:7
text: Set the glory of the Lord; in the miraculous provision of manna.  Exodus 16:14

title: Exodus 16:8
text:
Not against us; Moses and Aaron acted by God's direction.  The murmurings of the Israelites against them, were therefore in reality murmurings against Him who sent them. Compare  Matthew 10:40 Luke 10:16 John 12:44 John 13:20 . 
 
When men murmur against others for doing what God commands, instead of blaming men only, they are in reality blaming God.

title: Exodus 16:9
text: Near before the Lord; near to the cloudy pillar, in which he dwelt, and from which he spoke.   Exodus 16:10

title: Exodus 16:12
text:
I am the Lord your God; of course all their fears in following his guidance were groundless. 
 
The ingratitude and wickedness of men are often the occasion of wonderful manifestations of the patience, kindness, and grace of God.

title: Exodus 16:14
text: Round thing; rather, scale-like thing.

title: Exodus 16:15
text: It is manna; which might be translated, What is this?

title: Exodus 16:16
text: An omer; the tenth part of an ephah;  Exodus 16:36 .  According to a probable computation, the ephah contained one and one-twelfth bushels English; this would make the omer a trifle less than three and one-half quarts.

title: Exodus 16:18
text:
Mete; measure. 
 
  Gathered much had nothing over--gathered little had no lack.  These words may be understood in two ways: either that when each head of a family measured out to the members what he had gathered, it was miraculously brought about that there was just an omer apiece; or, that when the people measured the manna with an omer, the superabundance of one man went to supply the want of another.  This seems to be the view taken by the apostle Paul,  II Corinthians 8:14-15 . 
 
  According to his eating; according to the number of his household. 
 
Were it best, the Lord could furnish his people with the necessaries of life, and even with luxuries, without their labor; and he sometimes does this.  But generally he requires them to make efforts; and in all cases, having food and raiment, he requires them to be therewith content.   I Timothy 6:8 Hebrews 13:5

title: Exodus 16:19
text: Let no man leave of it till the morning; not that each one, under all circumstances, was required to eat the whole, but no one was allowed to lay up any of it or the next day, or for future use.  This was designed to teach them to depend on God, from day to day, for their daily bread.   Matthew 6:11 Matthew 6:34

title: Exodus 16:23
text:
The Lord hath said; God had told this to Moses, Ex16.5|, and Moses now tells it to the people. 
 
  Seethe; boil. 
 
  Remaineth over; above one omer for a man, or above what they would want for the sixth day. 
 
  To be kept; for their supply on the Sabbath.  It was cooked the day before, to prevent unnecessary labor on the Sabbath. 
 
Things should be so arranged on Saturday that all may rest from worldly employments on the Sabbath, and not be prevented by needless cooking, or any other labor, from remembering the day to keep it holy.

title: Exodus 16:27
text: However clearly it may be shown that God requires men to keep the Sabbath, some will neglect it.  And though he makes known that men cannot in the end be gainers by disobeying him, yet such as have no love to him, and no confidence in him, will violate the day.

title: Exodus 16:28
text: My laws; especially those which required them to rest from their ordinary employments, and keep the Sabbath-day holy.

title: Exodus 16:29
text: Go out of his place; for needless, worldly purposes.

title: Exodus 16:31
text:
Like coriander-seed; in shape and size. 
 
  Wafers; thin cakes.  When cooked it had something of the taste of sweet oil.   Numbers 11:6-8

title: Exodus 16:33
text:
Take a pot; this command seems to be mentioned here by way of anticipation, as the tabernacle was not yet made. 
 
  Before the Lord; in the ark of the testimony, the place of his presence.   Exodus 16:34 Exodus 25:16 Exodus 25:21 Exodus 30:6 .

title: Exodus 16:35
text:
Forty years; the time they spent in the wilderness.  Joshua 5:11-12  
 
All which will in the end benefit believers, they will, in the use of suitable means, receive. 
 
"All needful grace will God bestow, And crown that grace with glory too; He gives us all things, and withholds No real good from upright souls."

title: Exodus 16:36
text: Ephah; see note,  Exodus 16:16 .

title: Exodus 17:1
text: Rephidim; the last station before the Israelites reached Sinai.  Numbers 33:14-15

title: Exodus 17:2
text:
Did chide with Moses; found fault with him; murmured against him. 
 
  Tempt the Lord; try his patience by finding fault with his ministers, and provoking him to destroy them.

title: Exodus 17:3
text: No miracles or manifestations of divine power, wisdom, and goodness, will of themselves lead men to trust in God, or prevent them, when tried, from being dissatisfied with his dealings and murmuring against him.

title: Exodus 17:6
text: Stand before thee; in the cloudy pillar, that would rest upon the rock which Moses was to strike with his rod.

title: Exodus 17:7
text:
Massah; temptation. 
 
  Meribah; chiding; because there they chided with Moses, and tempted the Lord.

title: Exodus 17:8
text: Amalek; a people living south of Palestine, between Egypt and mount Seir.

title: Exodus 17:9
text: Joshua; this is the first time he is mentioned in the Bible.  His name in Hebrew means Saviour, the same as Jesus in Greek.  Hence he is sometimes, in the New Testament, which was written in Greek, called Jesus.   Acts 7:45 Hebrews 4:8

title: Exodus 17:10
text: Hur;  I Chronicles 2:1

title: Exodus 17:11
text: Held up his hand; in token of his seeking help from God.  I Timothy 2:8   In this first conflict between the Israelites and their enemies, it pleased God to require not only the intercessory prayer of Moses, but also the outward sign of it; that the people might thus be more deeply impressed with the truth that their salvation came from God, and was to be sought by earnest prayer.

title: Exodus 17:12
text:
Heavy; weary, tired. 
 
  His hands were steady; continued to be lifted up; showing that they felt that success must come from God. 
 
The servants of God may grow weary in prayer, and often they do so sooner than in the use of other means; but our great Advocate and Intercessor in heaven is never weary.  Ministers of the gospel need the aid and encouragement of God's people. 
 
There is no inconsistency between hearty dependence on God, manifested in believing, affectionate, fervent prayer for blessings, and the most skilful, vigorous, and persevering use of all appropriate means to obtain them; but the proper use of the one secures and gives efficacy to the right performance of the other.

title: Exodus 17:13
text: Discomfited Amalek; obtained a victory over the Amalekites.

title: Exodus 17:14
text:
Write this; that God would 
 
  Put out the remembrance; utterly destroy the Amalekites.  Deuteronomy 25:17-19 I Samuel 15:3-33 I Samuel 30:19 II Samuel 1:1-15 .

title: Exodus 17:15
text: Jehovah-nissi; the Lord my banner.

title: Exodus 17:16
text:
From generation to generation; till they are destroyed. 
 
National sins are followed by national judgments; and though the manifestation of divine indignation may long be delayed, in due time it will come; and those who fear not God, nor regard the welfare of their fellow-men, will be destroyed with utter destruction.

title: Exodus 18:1
text: Jethro;  Exodus 2:16 Exodus 3:1

title: Exodus 18:2
text:
Sent her back; he had sent back Zipporah to her father, while he and Aaron went to bring Israel out of Egypt.   Exodus 4:24-26  
 
It is sometimes proper for husbands and wives to live apart for a time, but generally it is best for them to live together, and by precept and example unite in training up their children in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.   I Corinthians 7:5 Ephesians 6:4

title: Exodus 18:3
text: Gershom;  Exodus 2:1

title: Exodus 18:4
text: Eliezer; meaning, my God a help.   Acts 7:29

title: Exodus 18:5
text: The mount of God; Sinai.   Exodus 3:1 Exodus 3:12 Exodus 19:11 Exodus 19:20

title: Exodus 18:6
text: He said unto Moses; sent word to him by a messenger.

title: Exodus 18:8
text: Travail; toils and trials.

title: Exodus 18:10
text: When friends who meet recount the goodness of God to them, it is calculated to honor him, to increase their gratitude, and better to fit them for the discharge of their duties.

title: Exodus 18:11
text: For in the thing--above them; or, yea, in the thing wherein they (the Egyptians) dealt proudly against them (the Israelites.)

title: Exodus 18:12
text:
Burnt-offering and sacrifices; in devout acknowledgment of the goodness of God, and as an expression of gratitude for his mercies. 
 
When those who have been separated meet again, it is not enough merely to speak of the kindness of God, but they should unite in worshipping him as the author of all the blessings they enjoy.

title: Exodus 18:13
text: Judge the people; hear and decide their controversies, and give them such instruction as they needed.   Exodus 18:16

title: Exodus 18:15
text: To inquire of God; to learn his will.

title: Exodus 18:17
text: Not good; it was not good for Moses to do the whole alone, because it would injure his health and shorten his life.

title: Exodus 18:18
text:
Wear away; he would become exhausted, and the people would suffer through the delay of their cases. 
 
It is not wise, nor is it right for men to labor so much as to injure their health and shorten their lives, even for the purpose of doing good; but they should proportion their labors to their ability most usefully to perform them.

title: Exodus 18:19
text:
God shall be with thee; he believed the plan he proposed would be approved of God. 
 
  To God-ward; Moses was to inquire of God for them, and make known to them his will.

title: Exodus 18:21
text:
Able men; capable men, who are disposed and qualified rightly to discharge the duties intrusted to them. 
 
Rulers and all civil officers should be capable men, who love God, speak the truth, hate covetousness, and are strictly honest: men who are able and willing promptly to discharge their appropriate duties, in order to honor God and do good to men.

title: Exodus 18:23
text:
If--God command thee; if he approve the plan, and direct thee to follow it. 
 
  Go to their place; to the land of Palestine, whither they were marching. 
 
  In peace; a well-ordered government would give them peace within and safety without.

title: Exodus 18:26
text: Division of labor greatly increases useful results.  Our object should be to have others do all the good they consistently can, and to do ourselves all we consistently can of what they leave undone.

title: Exodus 18:27
text: His own land; Midian.   Exodus 2:16 Exodus 2:21

title: Exodus 19:1
text: The same day; that is, the first day of the third month, called Sivan, answering to the last part of May and the first of June.  This was forty-five days after they left Egypt; namely, sixteen days of the first month and twenty-nine of the second.  The next day Moses went up to meet God.   Exodus 19:3   The day after he returned to God the answer of the people,  Exodus 19:7-8 , then three days were allowed the people to prepare themselves, and on the third day, which was the fiftieth from their departure out of Egypt, God came down on mount Sinai and gave them the law.   Exodus 19:11 Exodus 19:16   Hence the feast which was established in commemoration of this event was called Pentecost, meaning the fiftieth.  At this feast it was that the Holy Ghost descended on the disciples.   Acts 2:1-4

title: Exodus 19:4
text: Bare you on eagles' wings; saved them, and brought them safely and triumphantly to the enjoyment of his special presence and favor.  Deuteronomy 32:11 Isaiah 63:9

title: Exodus 19:5
text: If we hearken to the voice of God, believe his declarations, and obey his commands, he will delight in us, and esteem us as his peculiar treasure.   Deuteronomy 7:6 Deuteronomy 32:9 Psalms 135:4 Titus 2:14 I Peter 2:9 Revelation of John 5:10

title: Exodus 19:6
text: A kingdom of priests; the peculiar office of a priest is to minister to God in holy things.  Though there was a body of priests set apart from their brethren to offer the literal sacrifices and perform the other outward service of the tabernacle, yet all the Israelites as a holy nation were to render to God spiritual service, and offer spiritual sacrifices.  Compare  I Peter 2:5

title: Exodus 19:7
text: Laid before their faces; fully explained to them, and submitted to their consideration what God had said.

title: Exodus 19:8
text: Men are often much more ready to promise than to perform: and it is generally not wise to say what we will or will not do, but to say, "If the Lord will, we shall live and do this or that;" and while we resolve in his strength, we should depend on him for wisdom and grace to learn and do his will.

title: Exodus 19:10
text: Sanctify them; cause them to cleanse and prepare themselves.  The outward washing commanded was a sign of the inward cleansing of the heart from sin, which God required of every one.

title: Exodus 19:12
text: Whosoever toucheth; the presence of God made the mountain sacred, and it must not be profaned by the touch of man or beast.  Thus the Israelites were taught that every thing that pertains to God's service must be regarded with the deepest reverence.

title: Exodus 19:13
text:
To the mount; towards it, but not beyond the bounds prescribed for them. 
 
To meet God with acceptance, we must approach him feeling that we are sinners, and that he is of purer eyes than to behold iniquity but with abhorrence, and striving to cleanse ourselves from all filthliness of the flesh and of the spirit, and to perfect holiness in the fear of God.

title: Exodus 19:14
text: Sanctified the people; led them to purify themselves as directed,  Exodus 19:10 Exodus 19:15 .

title: Exodus 19:17
text: Nether; lower, outside of the prescribed line.   Exodus 19:12

title: Exodus 19:19
text: Moses spake, and God answered him;  Nehemiah 9:13 Hebrews 12:18-13:25

title: Exodus 19:21
text:
Break through; over the bounds set for them. 
 
All unholy curiosity in approaching God, gazing upon what he designed should not be seen, or prying into what is not revealed, is offensive to him and dangerous to ourselves.

title: Exodus 20:1
text: By proclaiming the ten commandments to the Israelites himself, and in circumstances of awful solemnity, God showed their fundamental importance, and took a course adapted to impress upon all men their obligations perfectly to obey them.

title: Exodus 20:2
text: Deliverance from bondage is a great and precious blessing, and special praises should be rendered to God by those who enjoy it.

title: Exodus 20:3
text:
Have no other gods; to have a god, is to love an object supremely. What a man most loves is his god.  Thou shalt not love any object in comparison with Jehovah, or worship any but him. 
 
  Before me; besides me, and in my sight. 
 
By forbidding men to regard any object more than God, or to worship any other, he would remove the temptation, and prevent the inclination to break his commandments which supreme regard to creatures occasions.

title: Exodus 20:5
text:
Not bow down--nor serve them; for that is giving them the place of Jehovah; worshipping and serving the creature in opposition to and defiance of the Creator. 
 
  Jealous God; displeased with those who bestow upon others what belongs only to him.
