  Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children; by suffering the sins of parents to bring evil upon children, and often suffering children, through the wicked influence of parents, to imitate their example and live and die in sin, and bring upon themselves its awful guilt and punishment. 
 
To treat creatures, or the likenesses of creatures, as if they were divine, by bowing down to them and worshipping them, is to act as if they were gods when they are not, and thus by actions to inculcate a falsehood suited to degrade, debase, pollute, and destroy the soul.

title: Exodus 20:6
text: Showing mercy unto thousands--that love me; not only by forgiving their sins and saving their souls, but often making them instrumental in leading others, especially their children and children's children, to become pious, and the means of salvation to their posterity to many generations.

title: Exodus 20:7
text:
Take--in vain; the highest violation of this command is in false swearing.  But it also prohibits every light and irreverent use of God's name. 
 
  Not hold him guiltless; will view and treat him as he truly is, exceedingly guilty and deserving divine displeasure. 
 
To use the name of God in a profane, light, or irreverent manner, or to mention it without good reason, tends to lessen the reverence which the soul ought to feel for him, to render it reckless and increasingly wicked, and is a flagrant offence against the Ruler of the universe.

title: Exodus 20:8
text:
Remember; that God in six days made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and that the seventh day he made for rest and spiritual duties; that on it he himself rested from all his work; that he blessed it and sanctified it, or set it apart form other days, to be devoted from the beginning to the end of time, not to secular but to sacred duties.  Genesis 2:1-3  
 
  Keep it holy; in accordance with the object for which God made it and gave it to men.  As a day not to be devoted to worldly business, conversation, reading, travelling, visiting, or amusement, nor to sleep, idleness, or worldly thoughts and feelings, but to be employed in religious worship, and in the promotion of our own spiritual good and that of our fellow-men.

title: Exodus 20:9
text: Six days--do all thy work; all the worldly business which men do must be done in the six working days, and what cannot be done in those days must be left undone, except what is needful to the best discharge of the appropriate duties of the Sabbath.

title: Exodus 20:10
text:
The Sabbath; the day of rest for men and beasts of burden. 
 
Men have no right to employ themselves, their children, servants, or cattle in worldly business more than six days in a week.  If they take the Sabbath for worldly purposes, they take what is not theirs, and thus show themselves to be dishonest men, taking that which does not belong to them, and in opposition to the express command of Jehovah.

title: Exodus 20:11
text:
Hallowed it; devoted it to sacred, in distinction from secular duties. 
 
As God has hallowed the Sabbath, or set it apart for sacred purposes, and for this end has blessed it, he makes it a blessing to all who rightly keep it, and through them a means of rich benefits to others.

title: Exodus 20:12
text:
Honor thy father and thy mother; love them, hearken to their teaching, and obey their commands.  Treat them with respectful and kind attention, assist them when they need, labor to supply their wants, promote their comfort, increase their usefulness, and do them all the good in your power.   Matthew 15:4-6 Matthew 19:19 Mark 7:10-13 Mark 10:19 Luke 18:20   Ephesians 6:1-3 Colossians 3:20 I Timothy 5:4  
 
  Days--be long; life be continued prosperous and happy. 
 
Children are bound to respect, love, and obey their parents, for the purpose of thus honoring and obeying God; and if they do not thus honor them, they dishonor and rebel against him.

title: Exodus 20:13
text:
Not kill; nor take the life of any human being, except when God requires it.   Genesis 9:6 Deuteronomy 25:17-19 I Samuel 15:1-3 I Samuel 15:18-19   This command forbids not only murder, but all those practices and kinds of business which tend to destroy human life; and requires the performance of those duties, and the pursuit of such courses as tend to preserve it and render it useful. 
 
By taking the life of a human being when not required by God, a man forfeits his own, and ought, in obedience to the divine requirement, to be put to death.

title: Exodus 20:14
text:
Not commit adultery; this command forbids all unchastity in thought, word, or deed.  It also forbids all those things which tend to this evil.  It is the application of the great law of supreme love to God and impartial love to men with regard to purity in heart and life.  Matthew 5:28  
 
Unchastity is a sin which greatly corrupts the human soul, and exposes it to numerous evils in this world, and to the wrath of God in the world to come.   Leviticus 20:10 Proverbs 6:25 Malachi 3:5 Matthew 5:28 I Corinthians 6:9   Galatians 5:19 Hebrews 13:4

title: Exodus 20:15
text:
Not steal; this command forbids us to appropriate to our own use what belongs to others.  It is the application of the law of love to property, and requires us to do to others, in respect to it, as we ought to wish them to do to us.   Micah 6:8 Colossians 4:1 II Peter 2:9  
 
Every man has certain things which God has given him, and which, by right from God, belong to himself.  They are his property.  To take them away, or without just cause deprive him of them, is theft, and exposes those who do it to be excluded from heaven.  Isaiah 10:1-2 Luke 16:11 I Corinthians 6:9 II Thessalonians 2:12

title: Exodus 20:16
text:
Not bear false witness; this is the application of the law of love to the reputation of others, and forbids us to speak differently of them from what, under similar circumstances, we ought to wish them to speak of us.   Matthew 12:37 Romans 13:10  
 
To utter falsehood concerning others, or truth for the purpose of injuring them, is a violation of duty, and will be condemned by God when the secrets of all hearts shall be revealed.   Matthew 12:37 James 4:11

title: Exodus 20:17
text:
Not covet; not desire what does not rightfully belong to us, in any such sense as would incline us wrongfully to take or retain possession of it.  Respect and treat the rights of all as you would wish them to respect and treat yours. 
 
All these ten commands express great moral obligations, arising from the nature and relations of things.  When they prohibit the highest form of any sin, as murder, adultery, and theft, they also forbid every thought and word that would lead to it.  Thus they extend to the thoughts and feelings as well as the outward actions, and are binding in all countries and in all ages. 
 
The law of God forbids us not merely to take what belongs to others, but to desire to take it.  It extends to the thoughts and feelings, requiring us to be content with such things as we have and can gain by doing right; loving Jehovah supremely and our fellow-men as we love ourselves, and pursuing that course which, under the direction of his word, this love requires.   Psalms 119:96 Matthew 22:37-40 Romans 13:7-10   I John 3:10 I John 4:8

title: Exodus 20:18
text: Saw; personally witnessed the thunderings and lightnings.

title: Exodus 20:19
text: Lest we die;  Judges 6:22 Judges 13:1

title: Exodus 20:20
text:
Fear not; not fear immediate death, but fear to disobey God. 
 
  Prove you; give you opportunity to show whether you will or will not obey him.

title: Exodus 20:22
text: Seen that I have talked; they heard his voice, but they saw no likeness of him; and this was designed to guard them against attempting to make any such likeness.  Ex 20.23

title: Exodus 20:24
text: Record my name; appoint to meet my people and receive their public worship.

title: Exodus 20:25
text: Thou hast polluted it; rendered it unfit for a place of public worship, by disobeying God in the manner of building it.  One reason of this prohibition doubtless was, to guard against the superstitious and idolatrous devices common to heathen altars.

title: Exodus 20:26
text: Neither--by steps; they were to go up by a gradual ascent, and thus avoid such exposure as might result from their being dressed in loose flowing garments.

title: Exodus 21:1
text: Judgments; rules or laws by which their civil government was to be conducted.  A collection of such rules is found in this and the two following chapters, to which this verse serves as an introduction.

title: Exodus 21:2
text:
If thou buy; God did not require or justify this, any more than the taking of two wives,  Exodus 21:10 , but both were then common, and many evils sprung from them.  God gave directions which would tend to lessen some of those evils, and render the case of those servants and wives less distressing than it otherwise would be.  The word translated buy, means to acquire, obtain, or possess.   Genesis 4:1  
 
  The seventh; one Hebrew should not be bound to serve another more than six years; about the time that an apprentice among us serves his master. 
 
  For nothing; however little work he had done during his time of service, he was not to be required to pay any thing for his freedom, because at the close of six years it belonged to him, and his master was bound not only to let him go, but also liberally to supply hinm. So with a woman-servant.   Deuteronomy 15:12-15

title: Exodus 21:4
text:
A wife; from his female servants. 
 
  Shall be her master's; neither her marriage nor the close of her husband's term of service shall release her from any previous obligation to serve her master. 
 
God, as civil ruler among the Jews, did not at once abolish all existing evils, but suffered some for a time to continue, on account of the hardness of their hearts.  Yet he adopted regulations which were suited to lessen some of the distressing consequences of those evils, and prepare the way, under the manifestations of increasing light and love, for their ultimate entire removal.  Matthew 19:8 Mark 10:5 Acts 17:30

title: Exodus 21:5
text: Plainly say; openly, freely, so as to make it manifest that it was his free, deliberate choice; thinking that it would on the whole be better for him to continue, than to take another course.

title: Exodus 21:6
text:
Bore his ear; this was to be the evidence, that from love to his master, his wife, and his children, he had voluntarily engaged to continue through life to work for his master. 
 
  For ever; through life.

title: Exodus 21:7
text:
Sell his daughter; under the expectation that the buyer or his son would marry her; and his thus buying her was an engagement to do so, as it was then customary for a man to buy his wife. 
 
  Not go out as the men-servants do; that is, in the seventh year,  Exodus 21:2 .  She should be better provided for, as specified,  Exodus 21:8-11

title: Exodus 21:8
text:
Who hath betrothed her; by thus buying her. 
 
  Let her be redeemed; cause her to be redeemed. 
 
  Unto a strange nation; in the Hebrew, a strange people, which some understand to be a foreign nation.  But the more probable meaning is, people who are strangers to him, not being of his family.  So "a strange woman" means another man's wife. 
 
  He hath dealt deceitfully; in not marrying her himself, or having her married in his family.

title: Exodus 21:9
text: After the manner of daughters; giving her a dowry, and treating her on her marriage as he should his own daughter.

title: Exodus 21:10
text:
Her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage; those of the wife whom he had bought and married. 
 
The giving of regulations to lessen the evils of an existing practice does not sanction the continuance of that practice, or afford any evidence that it ought not to be abandoned.

title: Exodus 21:11
text: Go out free; free from all further obligations to him.  She might be divorced and married, if she chose, to another man.

title: Exodus 21:12
text: Smiteth a man; intending to kill him.  One who commits murder.  Genesis 9:6 Leviticus 24:17 Numbers 35:30-31

title: Exodus 21:13
text:
Lie not in wait; had no malice against the man, and did not intend to kill him. 
 
  God deliver him; if the act was wholly providential, without human intention. 
 
  Whither he shall flee; and stay till the matter could be duly examined and the man rightly treated.

title: Exodus 21:14
text:
Slay him with guile; intending to murder him. 
 
  Take him from mine altar; even if he should flee there for refuge.  I Kings 2:28-34  
 
As King of the Jews, God adopted into their civil code many of those moral laws which had been obligatory on all men from the creation of the world, and among them was that which required the murderer to be put to death--a law binding on men under all dispensations.  Genesis 9:6 Numbers 35:31

title: Exodus 21:15
text:
vv 15,17. 
 
  Smiteth--curseth; rebellion against rightful parental authority was rebellion against God; and to smite or curse parents, under that government of which God was the civil as well as moral ruler, was at his command punished with death.

title: Exodus 21:16
text: Stealeth a man; taking him by force or guile, for the purpose of selling or enslaving him.  The guilt would be the same, should one hire or induce others to do it.

title: Exodus 21:17
text: See note on  Exodus 21:15 .

title: Exodus 21:18
text: If men strive; get into a quarrel.

title: Exodus 21:19
text: Be quit; free from the guilt of killing the man, and be punished only as specified.

title: Exodus 21:20
text: Surely punished; according to what, on judicial investigation, should appear to have been his intention and his crime.

title: Exodus 21:21
text:
Not be punished; not be punished, especially with death. 
 
  He is his money; the master had such a monied interest in the continued life of his servant, that it was not to be concluded that he meant to kill him, unless there should be clear evidence of the fact.

title: Exodus 21:22
text:
vv 21.25. 
 
  Eye for eye;  Leviticus 24:17-22 Deuteronomy 19:16-21

title: Exodus 21:26
text: A Jew by maiming his servant forfeited all claim to his services; and God, by requiring him to be set at liberty, and in many other things, showed a regard to the persons, property, and rights of servants, and to the mutual good of all, far beyond what was then shown in the civil code of any other nation.   Deuteronomy 4:5-9 Jeremiah 34:8-17

title: Exodus 21:28
text:
His flesh shall not be eaten; this was designed to impress upon all the sacredness of human life. 
 
  Be quit; not be held guilty of murder, nor suffer, except by the loss of the ox.  This was on the supposition that he did not before know that the ox was unruly, and that its going at large would endanger the lives of men.  But if he did know it, he was to be punished according to the circumstances and aggravations of the offence.  Exodus 21:29-31

title: Exodus 21:29
text: When a man has reason to believe that any thing under his control, if sent out or suffered to go out, will endanger the lives of men, he is bound to keep it in.  If he does not, and a man is killed by it, he is responsible for the life of that man, and will be treated accordingly at the bar of God.

title: Exodus 21:32
text: Thirty shekels; supposed to be about fifteen dollars.  Some have thought it to be more.

title: Exodus 21:34
text: Carelessness is forbidden by the law of God, as well as malice and covetousness; and if others suffer loss through our neglect, we are bound, as far as may be in our power, to remunerate them.

title: Exodus 22:2
text:
Breaking up; breaking into a dwelling in the night. 
 
  No blood be shed; the man who killed him was not to be deemed guilty of murder, or be punished.

title: Exodus 22:3
text:
If the sun be risen; if it was in the daytime, the man could be seen and secured.  There was no need of killing him, and the wanton killing of him would be murder. 
 
  Be sold for his theft; that thus restitution may be made to the man from whom he has stolen.  Among the Jews, men were sometimes sold or bound out for a time, as a punishment for their crimes.  Their services were sold till they had made compensation to those whom they had injured.  A poor man sometimes sold his own services, or those of his children, or his creditors sold them for the payment of his debts.  Exodus 21:2

title: Exodus 22:5
text: Restitution; a proper compensation to the person injured.

title: Exodus 22:6
text:
Make restitution; for the injury which his carelessness or neglect occasioned. 
 
When one man injures another through design or heedlessness, he is bound, as far as may be in his power, to make him suitable compensation.

title: Exodus 22:7
text: Stuff; furniture or articles of any kind.

title: Exodus 22:8
text: Put his hand; taken the article himself.

title: Exodus 22:9
text: Challengeth; affirms or declares.

title: Exodus 22:10
text: Fidelity in the safe preservation and good treatment of whatever is committed to us, is required by the law of God.  We should regard another's property as we ought to wish him to regard ours.

title: Exodus 22:12
text: Make restitution; on the ground of his not having taken proper care to prevent the theft.

title: Exodus 22:13
text: Bring it for witness; bring the animal, or some part of it, in proof of the fact.

title: Exodus 22:14
text: Make it good; presuming he had not taken proper care of it.

title: Exodus 22:15
text:
Not make it good; because the owner could see how it was treated. 
 
  It came for his hire; the price paid for the use of the beast was supposed to be enough not only to compensate for service, but also to cover the risk to which it would be exposed.  Of course, should the beast be hurt or die, the owner was to bear the loss. 
 
Whan a man hires property, giving a rent sufficient to compensate not only for its use, but also for the risk to which it is exposed, and the property without his fault is providentially injured or destroyed, the loss shall fall on the owner.

title: Exodus 22:16
text: Endow her; marry her, and suitably provide for her as his wife.

title: Exodus 22:17
text: According to the dowry; such as would be proper according to her rank and condition.

title: Exodus 22:18
text: A witch; one who professed to have conversed with evil spirits, and from them to receive supernatural power.

title: Exodus 22:20
text:
Shall be utterly destroyed; he not only broke the first commandment of the moral law, but also committed treason against the state, in acknowledging another God instead of Jehovah, who was then the civil head of the Jews. 
 
The restraints which are needful to keep men from outbreaking iniquity, show that their hearts are depraved; and tha all the holiness which there is among men is the fruit of divine grace.   James 1:17

title: Exodus 22:21
text: A stranger; one who came among them from another nation.

title: Exodus 22:25
text: Usury; interest.

title: Exodus 22:27
text: Strangers, widows, orphans, and poor persons are peculiarly exposed to be wronged by the wicked, and on this account God graciously makes them objects of his peculiar care, and with special severity will punish their oppressors.   Psalms 68:5 Proverbs 22:22-23 Jeremiah 49:11 Matthew 26:11

title: Exodus 22:28
text: The gods; magistrates, judges, and other civil rulers, officers under God.

title: Exodus 22:30
text: Give it me; this was an acknowledgment of God as the rightful proprietor of all.   Exodus 13:2

title: Exodus 22:31
text: Holy men unto me; separated from others to be peculiarly Jehovah's people.

title: Exodus 23:2
text: The majority as to numbers, wealth,and political influence are often wrong.  If in such cases a person would do right, he must not be governed by public opinion, however it may be expressed, but by the law of God.

title: Exodus 23:3
text: Countenance; unduly favor.  In deciding causes, they were not to favor the rich, the great, or the many; nor were they to be partial towards the poor, but to decide according to evidence, right, and duty.

title: Exodus 23:5
text:
Lying under his burden; fallen, and not able to rise without help. 
 
  Help with him; assist the owner in getting the beast up.

title: Exodus 23:7
text:
Far from a false matter; not attempt to support a false accusation. 
 
  Slay thou not; not be accessory to the death of an innocent person. 
 
The laws of Moses, as well as those of Christ, required men to love others as they loved themselves; and, under all circumstances, to do to others as they ought to wish that others should do to them.  Matthew 7:12 Matthew 19:19 Matthew 22:37-40

title: Exodus 23:8
text: Gift; a bribe offered to induce a magistrate to favor one in judgment.

title: Exodus 23:9
text:
A stranger; a foreigner.  They had learned by experience in Egypt the liability of foreigners to be oppressed, and remembered how they felt under oppression. 
 
Might never gives right; and to oppress or wrong any one because he cannot defend himself, or bring to justice the aggressor, is mean, base, and wicked.

title: Exodus 23:11
text: Let it rest; this was to teach them their dependence on God, and the safety of trusting in him.

title: Exodus 23:12
text:
Thy work; all worldly business except what was needful in acts of mercy, and for the best discharge of the appropriate duties of the Sabbath. 
 
  May be refreshed; one day's rest in a week from labor is, for man and beast, essential to the best refreshment, the greatest vigor, and longest life.   Exodus 34:21  
 
In requiring men to remember the Sabbath-day to keep it holy, God regards not only his own glory, but the comfort and highest good of all classes of men and of laboring animals.  To deprive them of the rest of the Sabbath is robbery of God, and of man and beast.

title: Exodus 23:13
text: Circumspect; very careful to obey his will.

title: Exodus 23:15
text:
Feast of unleavened bread; this followed the passover, instituted the night before they left Egypt.  It was called the feast of unleavened bread because they were required, during that feast, to eat nothing leavened, and to have no leaven in their houses.  Exodus 12:14-20  
 
  Empty; without an offering, or something devoted especially to the Lord.   Exodus 34:18-20

title: Exodus 23:16
text:
Feast of harvest; so called because the harvest then began to be ripe.  It was called also the feast of weeks, or of sevens, because it was kept seven weeks after the passover; also the feast of Pentecost, which means the fiftieth, because it commenced on the fiftieth day after the passover, and was commemorative of the giving of the law from mount Sinai, which took place fifty days after the departure of the Israelites from Egypt.   Exodus 34:22 Leviticus 23:14-21 Numbers 28:26-31  
 
  The feast of ingathering; so called because it took place after the gathering in or completion of the harvest.  It was called also the feast of tabernacles, in commemoration of their having dwelt forty years in tabernacles or tents in the wilderness.  The feast was kept from the fourteenth to the twenty-first day of the month Tishri, answering to the last part of September and the first part of October. It was the seventh month of their ecclesiastical, and the first of their civil year.   Leviticus 23:34-36 Deuteronomy 16:13-15

title: Exodus 23:17
text: Not only indidivuals but nations are bound to follow the directions of God.  Nor does their safety or their best interest ever require them, as nations or individuals, to break his commands.   Exodus 23:22-27 Exodus 34:24

title: Exodus 23:18
text: The blood of my sacrifice; or the feast of the passover.  Exodus 12:7-10 Exodus 34:25 Leviticus 2:11 Deuteronomy 16:4

title: Exodus 23:19
text: Seethe; boil or cook.  Some suppose that this precept was intended to guard against a superstitious usage of the heathen; others, that its design was to inculcate a humane spirit.

title: Exodus 23:20
text: An Angel;he who dwelt in the pillar of cloud and of fire.  Exodus 14:19 Exodus 32:34 Exodus 33:2 Exodus 33:14 Numbers 20:16 Joshua 5:13-15 Joshua 6:2 Isaiah 63:7-13

title: Exodus 23:21
text: My name is in him; he possessed and manifested the attributes of Jehovah.   Malachi 3:1

title: Exodus 23:23
text: Mine Angel shall--bring thee in;

title: Exodus 23:26
text: Thy days I will fulfil; he would preserve their lives to a good old age.

title: Exodus 23:28
text: Hornets;  Deuteronomy 7:20 Joshua 24:1

title: Exodus 23:29
text: Beast of the field; wild and ravenous beasts.   Deuteronomy 7:22

title: Exodus 23:31
text:
Sea of the Philistines; the Mediterranean sea, on the eastern shore of which the Philistines lived. 
 
  The desert;of Shur. 
 
  The river; Euphrates.   Joshua 1:4 I Kings 4:21  
 
Jehovah claims and exercises the right to dispose of all parts of the earth according to his pleasure.

title: Exodus 23:32
text: No covenant--with their gods; not worship them.

title: Exodus 23:33
text: A snare; it would draw them away from the worship of Jehovah, and bring upon them his wrath.

title: Exodus 24:1
text:
Come up; this command was given to Moses while he was yet with God in the mount,  Exodus 20:21 .  The meaning is, that he should come up again with the persons named, after he had first descended and done what is recorded in  Exodus 24:3-8 . 
 
  Nadab and Abihu; the two elder sons of Aaron.   Exodus 6:23  
 
We should approach God not only with reverence and holy fear, but with filial respect, confidence, and love.

title: Exodus 24:3
text:
All the words of the Lord--the judgments; those contained in the four preceding chapters.  The ten commandments were spoken by God himself to all the people. 
 
We often find that many who are forward to promise are backward to perform, and that nothing but the grace of God will make those who solemnly covenant with him steadfast and persevering in obeying his commands.   Numbers 14:11-35 Psalms 78:10-61 Psalms 106:8-43 I Corinthians 5:12

title: Exodus 24:4
text: All the words of the Lord; those which he had previously communicated to the people.

title: Exodus 24:7
text: The book of the covenant; that which he had written.  Exodus 24:4

title: Exodus 24:8
text:
The blood of the covenant; that by which the covenant which they had made was ratified.   Hebrews 9:19 Matthew 26:28 Mark 14:24 Luke 22:20  
 
The blood which was shed in sacrifices under the Old Testament dispensation, was designed to impress upon all the necessity of an atonement, in order to the forgiveness of sin and acceptance with God. It pointed forward to the blood of Christ, who, in due time, was to take away sin by the sacrifice of himself; and who would enter the holy place with his own blood, and thus obtain eternal redemption for all who should believe on him.   Hebrews 9:6-28

title: Exodus 24:9
text: Then went up Moses; as directed,  Exodus 24:1

title: Exodus 24:10
text:
Saw the God of Israel; compare  Isaiah 6:1 Ezekiel 1:26 . 
 
  A paved work of a sapphire; or, transparent sapphire.  This is the "sea of glass like unto crystal,'' in  Revelation of John 4:6 .  The sapphire is a precious stone of a sky-blue color.  The elders of Israel did not see God face to face as Moses did, but only from the lower part of the mount, where they were commanded to worship "afar off."  Exodus 24:1-2

title: Exodus 24:11
text: He laid not his hand; they received no harm, though they saw God; not his essence or shape, but his visible glory.   John 1:18 John 5:37   John 6:46 John 14:9 John 15:24 I John 4:12

title: Exodus 24:12
text:
Come up to me; still nearer to the visible glory. 
 
  Tables of stone; on which were the ten commandments.  Exodus 31:18   Exodus 32:15 Exodus 32:16 Deuteronomy 5:22 . 
 
A right understanding of the law which God wrote with his finger on tables of stone, is essential to a right estimate of human character. Ministers should therefore be very explicit in teaching it.  Without rightly understanding the law, men will not rightly understand the gospel, or their need of its blessings.

title: Exodus 24:13
text:
Minister; servant. 
 
  Into the mount; towards the top of the mount, on which was the visible presence of Jehovah.  It would seem that Moses with Joshua approached near to the cloud that covered the mount, and there abode six days.  On the seventh day God called Moses into his immediate presence, while Joshua remained behind and waited for him.  In  Exodus 32:17 , we find him descending with Moses.

title: Exodus 24:14
text: Matters to do; controversies to be settled, or cases to be decided.

title: Exodus 24:18
text: Moses received his directions from God, therefore all the children of Israel were bound to obey him.  If they did not, they rebelled against God, and were justly exposed to his wrath.  How much more aggravated will be the sin and doom of men who refuse to obey Jesus Christ.  Deuteronomy 18:15 John 1:45 Acts 3:22-26 Acts 7:37 Hebrews 10:28-31

title: Exodus 25:1
text:
We come not to the tabernacle and its furniture.  To guard against any intermixture of heathenish usages, as well as to impress upon the minds of the Israelites the truth that all acceptable worship of God must be in accordance with the rules of his appointment, Jehovah gave to Moses in the mount specific directions for the structure of the tabernacle and every thing pertaining to its service.  He showed him, moreover, a pattern, by which he was enabled at once to apprehend the meaning of all the directions he received, and to write them out in full, as is done in this and the six following chapters. 
 
The tabernacle was God's visible dwelling place.  As such it represented to the Israelites the great truth that Jehovah dwells spiritually with his people as their king and protector.  Thus the tabernacle, with all the services belonging to it, was "a shadow of good things to come."  It typified the higher blessings of the Christian dispensation, as is fully shown in the epistle to the Hebrews.

title: Exodus 25:2
text:
That giveth it willingly; thus God taught the people that he will have willing worshippers. 
 
God most justly requires of men that, whatever they do, they should seek to honor him and benefit their fellow-men.

title: Exodus 25:4
text: Blue, and purple, and scarlet; these colors were employed as being the most excellent.

title: Exodus 25:5
text:
Badgers' skins; according to some, the original word means the skin of a species of seal. 
 
  Shittim-wood; a species of acacia, an exceedingly fine and durable wood.  Gum arabic is obtained from the living tree.

title: Exodus 25:7
text: The ephod--breastplate; see the description of these,  Exodus 28:6-30 .

title: Exodus 25:8
text: Though God is in all places, yet he dwells especially in those which, according to his will, are consecrated to his worship; and from them he bestows peculiar blessings on his people.

title: Exodus 25:10
text:
An ark; this is a different word in the Hebrew from that rendered ark in  Genesis 6:14 , and means a chest. 
 
  A cubit; about eighteen inches.

title: Exodus 25:11
text: A crown; a cornice or border around the lid of the ark.

title: Exodus 25:13
text: Staves; poles or rods to go through the rings of the ark, by which to carry it.

title: Exodus 25:16
text:
The testimony; the tables of stone, on which were written the ten commandments, God's testimony as to the duty of men. 
 
What relates to the worship and glory of God, and to the redemption of men by Jesus Christ, is described in the Bible with greater minuteness, and treated as of greater importance, than the temporal interests of kingdoms, or all the mere worldly concerns of men.

title: Exodus 25:17
text: A mercy-seat; this was the golden covering or lid, the upper side of the sacred chest or ark, called the mercy-seat because on it was sprinkled the blood of atonement, and above it dwelt Jehovah in his visible glory, dispensing mercy to men.

title: Exodus 25:18
text: Cherubim; representations of creatures intensely studying, for the purpose of doing the will of God.  Some have supposed them to resemble the living creatures described  Ezekiel 1:4-14 .

title: Exodus 25:20
text: One to another; the cherub on one end looking towards the cherub on the other end of the mercy-seat, both looking towards the mercy-seat, and their wings stretched over it.   Hebrews 9:5 .  Between them, on the mercy-seat, was the shekinah, or the visible glory of Jehovah.  Hence, he is said to dwell between the cherubim.  I Samuel 4:4 Psalms 80:1 Psalms 99:1 .

title: Exodus 25:22
text: All things which, by divine appointment, are connected with the sanctuary, were designed by god to impress upon the worshippers a conviction of his presence, and communicate something of those truths which relate to the bestowment of mercy and the gift of salvation through Christ.

title: Exodus 25:24
text: A crown; cornice or rim.

title: Exodus 25:25
text:
Border; this was to be below the leaf, around the frame of the table. 
 
  Handbreadth; the width of the four fingers; about three or four inches. 
 
  A golden crown; a rim of gold around the border, like that around the leaf of the table.

title: Exodus 25:29
text:
Spoons; or bowls. 
 
  Covers; or cans. 
 
  To cover withal; better, to pour out withal.

title: Exodus 25:30
text:
Show-bread; twelve loaves of bread, equal to the number of the tribes.  It was placed on the table, and called show-bread, or bread of the presence, because it always stood in the presence of the Lord.  It was sprinkled with frankincense.  On the Sabbath the bread was taken away, and new bread put in its place.  The frankincense that was on it was burnt as an oblation to God, and the bread was eaten by the priests.   Leviticus 24:5-9 .  On one emergency mentioned in Scripture it was given to others.   I Samuel 21:1-6 Matthew 12:2 Matthew 12:4 .  This show-bread, and all the articles and worship in the tabernacle, and afterwards in the temple, pointed forward to the Bread of God, which was to come down from heaven, and give life unto the world.   John 6:32-58 . 
 
It is not enough, in order to salvation, that Christ tasted death for every man, and was made a propitiation for the sins of the world; but in order to be saved, men must receive from him spiritual life, be united to him, and receive from him permanently spiritual nourishment and support.   Hebrews 2:9 I John 2:2 John 6:32-58 John 15:1-11

title: Exodus 25:31
text:
A candlestick; it consisted of an upright shaft, with six branches coming out in pairs, three on each side, making a line of seven lamps. 
 
  Knops; knobs or embossed work.  These and the bowls and flowers were ornamental figures on the shaft and branches.

title: Exodus 25:33
text:
Like unto almonds; in the form of an almond. 
 
  In the six branches; three bowls, knobs, and flowers on each branch, and four on the shaft of the candlestick, making twenty-two in all.

title: Exodus 25:35
text: Of the same; the same material, pure gold.

title: Exodus 25:37
text:
Seven lamps; one for the shaft, and one for each branch of the candlestick. 
 
Jesus Christ is the light of the world.  All men, and especially his ministers, are bound to follow him, that they may not walk in darkness, but have the light of life; and to let that light so shine in godly, beneficent conduct, that men shall be led to glorify their Father in heaven.   John 8:12 Matthew 5:14-16

title: Exodus 25:38
text: The tongs; snuffers or scissors to trim the lamps.

title: Exodus 25:39
text: A talent of pure gold; estimated by some to be equal to about twenty, and by others, thirty thousand dollars.  The light of these lamps represented the spiritual light which God in Christ, by his word and Spirit, through the instrumentality of his people, especially his ministers, communicates to the world.

title: Exodus 26:1
text:
Tabernacle; the words tabernacle and tent are sometimes used in a general way to denote the whole structure of the movable temple described in the present chapter,  Exodus 26:1-37 Psalms 78:60 . But in a strict sense, the tabernacle is always the inner set of curtains described in  Exodus 26:1-6  while the tent is the covering above it of goats' hair.  See  Exodus 26:6 Exodus 26:11-13 . 
 
  Cherubim of cunning work; or rather, the work of a cunning deviser. It is generally agreed that these curtains were woven with different colors and figures of cherubim, while the hanging for the door of the tent,  Exodus 26:36 Exodus 26:37 , was embroidered.

title: Exodus 26:3
text: Coupled together; in the Hebrew simply joined.  Hence a great curtain formed from the union of several smaller curtains is called a joining, or "coupling."

title: Exodus 26:4
text:
The edge of the one curtain; that is of the one great curtain. 
 
  From the selvedge in the coupling; rather, on the edge in the coupling.  The coupling is the compound curtain made of five single curtains. 
 
  In the uttermost edge--coupling of the second; or, in the edge of the outermost curtain in the second coupling.  The simple meaning is, that in the edge of the outermost curtain of each coupling (compound curtain) on the adjacent sides should be loops, etc., corresponding to each other.

title: Exodus 26:5
text:
Coupling of the second; or, second coupling.  See note  Exodus 26:4 . 
 
  Take hold one of another; or, be opposite one to another.

title: Exodus 26:6
text: Taches; clasps to unite the loops, and thus the edges of the curtains.

title: Exodus 26:9
text: Double; double it over in an ornamental way.

title: Exodus 26:10
text: Which coupleth the second; or, in respect to the second coupling. See note  Exodus 26:4 .

title: Exodus 26:12
text: The half curtain that remaineth; that is, the half of the second great curtain made of five single curtains.  The framework of shittim-wood was thirty cubits long and ten cubits high.  The two great curtains of goats' hair, when united, made a covering 44 cubits long by 30 wide.  Of this, 4 cubits were doubled over in front; 30 more were needed to cover the framework; leaving 10 cubits, that is just half of the second great curtain, to hang over in the rear.

title: Exodus 26:13
text: That which remaineth in the length of the curtains of the tent; that in which the curtains of the tent exceed in length those of the tabernacle.  Here the sacred writer reckons according to the length of a single curtain.  The curtains of the inner covering (tabernacle) were 28 cubits long; those of the outer covering (tent) were 30 cubits in length.  When the two coverings were spread over the framework of shittim-wood, so that the curtains, regarded as single, lay across it and hung down on each side, the curtains of the tent must have extended just a cubit on each side below the curtains of the tabernacle, so as entirely to cover the latter.

title: Exodus 26:15
text: Boards; with the exception of  Ezekiel 27:6 , where the meaning is uncertain, the word here rendered "boards" is used only of the framework of the sanctuary.  It does not denote common boards, but rather thick planks.  See on  Exodus 26:22-25 .

title: Exodus 26:17
text: Tenons; projections to set into the sockets of silver.

title: Exodus 26:22
text: Six boards; it is generally agreed that the width of the tabernacle on the inner side was ten cubits.  The Jewish rabbins agree in representing the planks, or timbers, of the tabernacle to have been one cubit in thickness.  As they were a cubit and a half in width, this would require just eight to reach from outside to outside on the western end.  If they had a less thickness, then the two corner planks,  Exodus 26:23 , must have extended just so far beyond the side.

title: Exodus 26:24
text:
Coupled together; in the Hebrew, twinned, that is made double.  The meaning seems to be, that each corner-plank shall be joined above and below to the adjacent side-plank, so that the two shall make a pair. 
 
  Unto one ring; so that one ring shall serve to unite the two.

title: Exodus 26:26
text: Bars; these were to run through the sides of the framework, to increase its strength.

title: Exodus 26:30
text: In order to be accepted, we must consecrate to God the best that we have, and be careful in all things to follow his directions.

title: Exodus 26:33
text:
The holy place and the most holy; these were the two divisions into which the tabernacle was divided; the holy place being twenty cubits by ten, and the holy of holies ten cubits square.   Hebrews 9:6-9 . 
 
As the veil which separated the holy from the most holy place, in the tabernacle and afterwards in the temple, was at the crucifixion of Christ rent in twain, to show us that the way to the throne of mercy is open for all, all should, with believing and grateful hearts, draw near to God, in that new and living way opened by the death of Christ, that they may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in all times of need.  Hebrews 9:1-14 Hebrews 9:20-22

title: Exodus 26:36
text: The door; the entrance to the tabernacle, which was on the east.

title: Exodus 27:2
text: Horns; projections of the four corners.

title: Exodus 27:4
text: A grate of network of brass; the position and office of this it is difficult to determine. A common opinion has been, that it was suspended by the four rings in the hollow of the altar midway between the top and the bottom; and that on it the sacrifices were burned, the ashes falling through upon the ground below.  Others have supposed that all the hollow of the altar above the grave was filled with earth, upon which the sacrifices were placed.  The common Jewish tradition is, that the whole interior of the altar was filled with earth,  Exodus 20:24 , and that the grate went round the altar on the outside, which is favored by  Exodus 38:5 Exodus 38:7 .

title: Exodus 27:8
text: Every altar for sacrifice, erected by divine appointment under the Old Testament, pointed forward to the sacrifice of Christ; who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot unto God, to purge our consciences from dead works to serve the living God.   Hebrews 9:10-21

title: Exodus 27:9
text: Court of the tabernacle; a large open inclosure around the tabernacle.

title: Exodus 27:10
text: Fillets; rods passing from the top of one pillar to another.

title: Exodus 27:13
text: On the east side eastward; as this was the front, it had a gateway in the centre of twenty cubits, with a hanging of richer materials, leaving just fifteen cubits on each side for the curtain of common materials.

title: Exodus 27:17
text: Filleted with silver; connected at the top by silver fillets.

title: Exodus 27:20
text:
Oil-olive beaten; oil obtained from beating olives in a mortar, which was more pure than that obtained by pressing them in a mill. 
 
Intelligence and purity should ever characterize the followers, and especially the ministers of Christ.  He is the light of the world, and in following him they will not walk in darkness, but have the light of life, and be instrumental in communicating it for the salvation of their fellow-men.   Matthew 5:16 John 1:9 John 8:12

title: Exodus 27:21
text: Order it; see to the lighting of the lamp, according to divine direction.

title: Exodus 28:1
text: The high-priest, among the Jews, was a striking type of the Messiah, who, as a priest, entered the holy place with his blood, and obtained eternal redemption for his people.   Hebrews 9:11-12

title: Exodus 28:2
text:
Holy garments; garments to be used not on ordinary occasions, but when engaged in the public worship of God. 
 
  For glory and for beauty; the glory and beauty of the priestly garments represented the holiness, purity, and dignity of their office; and, since their priesthood typified that of Christ, these holy and glorious garments prefigured the infinite dignity, excellence, and spiritual beauty of Jesus Christ our great High-priest.

title: Exodus 28:3
text: The ingenuity of men, their genius and judgment, their ability to plan, and their power to execute, all come from God, and should all be devoted to his service.   James 1:17

title: Exodus 28:5
text: Gold; that is, golden thread.  The manner of forming them is described  Exodus 39:3

title: Exodus 28:6
text: The ephod; this, with the breastplate attached to it, was the outermost of the garments belonging to the high-priest.  The ephod was a short garment reaching down, according to the testimony of the ancients, to the middle of the thighs.  Originally it seems to have been without sleeves.  Each shoulder-piece consisted of two projections from the body of the ephod, the one coming up from before and the other from behind, and united on the shoulder at their extremities by an onyx-stone set in gold, which served also for a clasp.

title: Exodus 28:8
text: Shall be of the some, according to the work thereof; these words seem to mean, that it shall be woven as a part of the ephod; and be of the same materials and texture.

title: Exodus 28:9
text:
vv 9,12. 
 
Our great High-priest, of whom Aaron was a type, bears all his people upon his heart, presents their wants before his Father, and will save to the uttermost all who come unto God through him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.   I Peter 2:24 Hebrews 7:25

title: Exodus 28:11
text:
Signet; a seal. 
 
  Ouches; sockets.

title: Exodus 28:12
text: For a memorial; to put them in remembrance that Aaron, as priest appeared in their behalf before the Lord.

title: Exodus 28:14
text: Two chains; these are generally thought to be the same chains mentioned  Exodus 28:24-25 , their connection with the ephod being here considered, and there, their connection with the breastplate.

title: Exodus 28:15
text: Breastplate of judgment; so called because worn by the high-priest when he applied to the Lord for his judgment, or decision, in matters about which they inquired of him.

title: Exodus 28:16
text: Four square--being doubled; after being doubled over so as to form a sort of bag or pouch, it was four square: consequently the whole piece, before doubling, was two spans in length.  A span is half a cubit, that is, between nine and ten inches.

title: Exodus 28:21
text: The names of all his people are in the Lamb's book of life; he will never blot them out, but will acknowledge them as his redeemed people, before his Father and the holy angels.   Revelation of John 3:5 Matthew 10:32

title: Exodus 28:22
text: Chains at the ends; at the two upper corners on the outside were two rings of gold, to which these chains were attached,  Exodus 28:23-24

title: Exodus 28:25
text: The two ouches; the two sockets of the onyx-stones on the shoulder- pieces of the ephod.

title: Exodus 28:26
text: Two rings of gold; on the two lower corners of the breastplate on the inside, corresponding to the two rings in the ephod,  Exodus 28:27 .

title: Exodus 28:27
text: Two other rings of gold--ephod; this verse may be literally rendered thus: "And thou shalt make two rings of the ephod below, in its forepart, over against its coupling, above the girdle of the ephod."  The coupling is that of the shoulder pieces at the onyx-stones,  Exodus 28:7 .  These rings are to be directly opposite to this coupling below.  The two upper corners of the breastplate being fastened to the onyx-stones by wreathed chains of gold, and the two lower corners to the rings here mentioned by a lace of blue, the breastplate is thus made firm over the heart,  Exodus 28:29 ; a beautiful and most expressive symbol of the unchangeable love which Christ, our great High-priest, bears toward his people, and in which all his earthly ministers should strive to imitate him.  It has been well said that Christ bears his people on his shoulders by his almighty power and efficacious atonement, and on his heart by his everlasting love.

title: Exodus 28:30
text:
Urim--Thummim; that is, lights and perfections: according to some, these were no other than the precious gems themselves, through which God, by a supernatural lustre, manifested his will; others think that they were precious stones placed in the pouch of the breastplate, and used in consulting God's will.  The whole subject is involved in obscurity. 
 
All spiritual illumination and perfection are in Jesus Christ, and he is able and willing to communicate according to the wants of all who feel their need, and heartily apply to him.

title: Exodus 28:31
text: Robe of the ephod; worn underneath the ephod.

title: Exodus 28:32
text: The hole of it; the hole through which the head passed when it was put on.

title: Exodus 28:33
text: Pomegranates; balls in the form of pomegranates, a species of fruit shaped like an apple.

title: Exodus 28:34
text: A golden bell and a pomegranate; one after the other, alternately, round the hem of the robe.  The bell was an emblem of pleasant sound, and the pomegranate of abundant fruitfulness; indicating the duty of makng a good profession, and abounding in fruits of holiness.

title: Exodus 28:38
text:
Bear the iniquity of the holy things; typically make atonement for their sins, and thus obtain forgiveness through the atonement of Christ. 
 
Holiness to the Lord was the great and all-pervading characteristic of the Redeemer; and it is his great design, by his word, his Spirit, and his providence, in all his dispensations to make his people like him.  I Corinthians 15:49 I John 3:2

title: Exodus 28:41
text:
Anoint them; in token of their dedication to the sacred office. 
 
  Sanctify them; set them apart, and devote them to their work.

title: Exodus 28:43
text: Bear not iniquity; do not commit sin, by neglecting divine directions, thus exposing themselves to divine judgments.

title: Exodus 29:1
text:
Aaron and his sons being sinners, it is necessary that they be first cleansed by washing and expiatory sacrifices, before they can minister to the Lord as his priests.   Hebrews 5:3   This typical cleansing represents the purity and holiness of the priestly office.  The three different kinds of sacrifice--a sin offering, a burnt offering, and a peace offering--signify the completeness of their consecration. 
 
  To hollow; set apart from secular to sacred duties. 
 
  Without blemish; this was required in the case of every sacrifice. On the part of the offerer it signified his supreme love and devotion to God,  Malachi 1:8 ; on the part of the victim, it prefigured the perfection of Christ's sacrifice.   I Peter 1:19  
 
It is the will of God that those who minister in holy things, making known the will of God and leading the devotions of his people, should not only be called of him, but should be publicly set apart to their work.

title: Exodus 29:2
text: Wafers; thin cakes.

title: Exodus 29:6
text: Holy crown; the plate of gold.   Exodus 28:36-37

title: Exodus 29:7
text: Anointing oil; an oil prepared with various spices.  Exodus 30:23-33

title: Exodus 29:9
text: The bonnets; or turbans.   Exodus 28:40

title: Exodus 29:10
text:
Put their hands upon the head of the bullock; this expressed their conviction of guilt, and their hope that through the shedding of the blood of that victim, pointing forward to the blood of Christ, they should receive pardon. 
 
Ministers of religion, as well as their people, are sinners, and need pardon through the atonement of Christ and the purifying influences of his Spirit, in order rightly to discharge their duties.

title: Exodus 29:12
text: The horns of the altar;  Exodus 27:2

title: Exodus 29:18
text:
Burn the whole; denoting the necessity of an entire consecration of the whole man to God, as well as the necessity of an atonement, in order to salvation. 
 
The evidence of genuine repentance for sin, faith in Christ, and pardon through his atonement, is sincere and hearty consecration of body and soul to his service.

title: Exodus 29:19
text: The other ram; this was a peace-offering, on the flesh of which the offerer and his friends feasted, after the breast and right shoulder had been given to the priests.   Leviticus 7:28-34   On the present occasion, Moses, as performing the priestly office, received for his portion the breast,  Exodus 29:26 .

title: Exodus 29:20
text: Tip of the right ear--thumb--toe; this signified the completeness of their expiation and consecration.

title: Exodus 29:24
text: Wave them; move them to and fro.  This, as well as heaving upward, was a sign that they were consecrated to God.

title: Exodus 29:27
text:
vv 27-28. 
 
  Shalt sanctify the breast of the wave-offering; these two verses contain a general direction respecting all peace-offerings.  The breast was waved and the shoulder heaved, and both went to the priests as their portion.  On the signification of the different sacrifices see,  Leviticus 1:1-7:38 .

title: Exodus 29:28
text: The effects of reconciliation to God are peace and communion with him, access to his mercy-seat, and grace to help in all times of need.

title: Exodus 29:30
text:
That son; the one who should secceed his father in the high- priest's office. 
 
  When he cometh; before he should be permitted to discharge the duties of high-priest.

title: Exodus 29:31
text: The ram of the consecration; the second ram, mentioned  Exodus 29:19-26 .

title: Exodus 29:33
text:
Eat those things wherewith the atonement was made; denoting the necessity of union to Him by whom it was made.  Matthew 26:26 John 6:53-55 I Corinthians 6:17  
 
Continued union to Christ, by habitual trust in him, not only for pardon, but for wisdom, strength, consolation, and all needed good, is essential to progress in holiness and preparation for heaven.

title: Exodus 29:36
text: Sanctify it; set it apart to the worship of God.

title: Exodus 29:37
text:
For the altar; upon it. 
 
  Holy; devoted to God.   Matthew 23:19

title: Exodus 29:38
text: Continually; each day.  This is the morning and evening sacrifice, which was offered every day from year to year.

title: Exodus 29:40
text: A tenth-deal; one tenth of an ephah.  The ephah being about thirty- four and two-thirds quarts, a tenth-deal would be a little less than three quarts and a half; and a hin, which, according to the Jews, was the sixth part of an ephah, a little less than six quarts.

title: Exodus 29:42
text:
A continual burnt-offering; representing their continual need of the constant efficacy of the atonement, righteousness, and intercession of Christ. 
 
Habitual acknowledgment of God as the author of all good, and daily supplication to him for the blessings which we need for ourselves, our friends, and all our fellow-men, are the duty of all.  They are also a privilege, the enjoyment of which should not be sacrificed for any worldly good.

title: Exodus 29:45
text: Dwell among the children of Israel; by his continual presence in the shekinah, or visible glory, on the mercy-seat, where he was worshipped, and from which he made known his will.

title: Exodus 30:1
text: In the Mosaic ritual we are continually reminded of the priesthood, sacrifice, and intercession of Christ, through the incense of whose merits alone our prayers can ascend with acceptance before God.

title: Exodus 30:3
text: A crown; cornice or border.

title: Exodus 30:6
text: The veil; which separated the holy from the most holy place, so that the altar stood directly over against the ark of the covenant, being separated from it by the veil.

title: Exodus 30:7
text: Sweet incense; this represented the prayers of God's people made acceptable by the intercession of Christ,  Revelation of John 8:3-4 , as the burnt-offering did his atonement.

title: Exodus 30:8
text: Our need of Christ's intercession is constant; and day by day, morning and evening, continually our supplications should ascend before him as incense, and the lifting up of our hearts in prayer and praise as our habitual sacrifice.   Hebrews 13:15

title: Exodus 30:9
text: Strange incense; other than that prescribed,  Exodus 30:34-38:1

title: Exodus 30:10
text:
Once in a year; on the great day of atonement.  Leviticus 16:18 Leviticus 23:27-28  
 
  Shall--make atonement; this showed that atonement was necessary, in order to the efficacy of intercession.

title: Exodus 30:12
text:
The sum; the census; their number. 
 
  A ransom for his soul; a tribute paid to God for the preservation and blessings of life, and for the support of divine worship.

title: Exodus 30:13
text: Half a shekel; in value about twenty-five cents.

title: Exodus 30:15
text: Not give more--not give less; teaching that before God the rich and poor are of equal worth, and equally need the same atonement.

title: Exodus 30:16
text:
That it may be a memorial unto the children of Israel; more literally, "that it may be to the children of Israel for a memorial before the Lord;" that is, that it may remind God in their behalf,  Genesis 9:16 , of the ransom they have paid for their souls. 
 
  To make an atonement for your souls; so that God shall send no plague among them.   Exodus 30:12  
 
A portion of what God has given us should be gratefully devoted to the support of his worship, as a memorial of his goodness and a testimony of our obligations for all the blessings of his providence and grace.

title: Exodus 30:18
text: A laver; large bowl or basin.

title: Exodus 30:20
text: Wash with water; an emblem of the purifying influences of the Holy Ghost.

title: Exodus 30:21
text: Purity of heart and life is as needful as the pardon of sin; and for it we should look habitually to the Holy Spirit, the Author and Finisher of all that is spiritually good in the children of men.

title: Exodus 30:23
text:
Principal spices; of the purest and most precious kind. 
 
  Five hundred shekels; the shekel has been estimated at from ten to ten and three quarters pennyweights.  Five hundered shekels would then be from about nineteen to twenty-two and a third pounds, troy weight; or, from a little less than sixteen, to about eighteen and a half pounds avoirdupois.

title: Exodus 30:25
text: The apothecary; perfumer, or maker of ointments.

title: Exodus 30:30
text: Anoint Aaron and his sons; in token of the necessity of their being endued with the Holy Spirit, to fit them for their duties.

title: Exodus 30:31
text: All our services must be perfumed with the incense of Christ's merits, and be the fruit of his Spirit, working in us both to will and also to do, in order to be holy, or ascend before God with acceptance.  John 15:5 Revelation of John 8:4

title: Exodus 30:32
text: Upon man's flesh; the flesh of men who were not priests.

title: Exodus 30:34
text: Stacte--onycha, and galbanum; fragrant spices or gums.  Some, however, suppose onycha to be a species of shell which, when burnt, yields a strong odor.

title: Exodus 30:35
text: Confection; mixture, to burn on the altar of incense.

title: Exodus 30:38
text: While we rely on the atonement, righteousness, and intercession of Christ as the one only and all-sufficient Mediator, and look to his Spirit as the only Sanctifier, we should most carefully abstain from looking to or depending on any other; for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.   Acts 4:12

title: Exodus 31:3
text: God bestows various talents on men, not for the purpose of their lying useless, or being employed only for the gratification or benefit of their possessors, but for the promotion of his glory and the good of mankind.

title: Exodus 31:6
text:
Given with him; as his associate and assistant in making the tabernacle and its furniture, according to the pattern and directions which God had given to Moses. 
 
Different gifts are imparted to men, that they may feel their need of each other, and be mutual helpers in the discharge of their various duties, and the accomplishment of the work to which he calls them.

title: Exodus 31:11
text: The more exactly men follow the directions of God, the greater wisdom and goodness they will manifest, and the more useful they will be.

title: Exodus 31:13
text: A sign between me and you; a sign of the relation which subsisted between them.  By keeping the Sabbath holy, according to his directions,  Exodus 20:8-11 , they would show that they were his people, and that he was their God.  It would also be a great means of preserving among them a right knowledge of God, and thus making them holy and preparing them for heaven.

title: Exodus 31:14
text:
Holy unto you; set apart; devoted to sacred employments. 
 
  Defileth it; by devoting it to worldly business. 
 
  Put to death; by the magistrate, at the command of God, who was King of that nation, and had a right to dispose of life as he saw best. 
 
The Sabbath was not given to men for labor, even in preparing houses or furniture for the worship of God, but for rest, and for religious duties.  It is in keeping the day holy that men show that they rightly know God, belong to his people, and are preparing for the rest of heaven.   Hebrews 4:9

title: Exodus 31:17
text:
A sign; an evidence of God's kindness to men, and a public token that they who rightly keep it are his people, that he is their God, and will do for them all that he has promised. 
 
  Was refreshed; delighted in his work, especially in the Sabbath-- which he had provided and set apart as a day of rest for his people-- and in the benefits which the keeping of it holy would confer upon them. 
 
The holy keeping of the Sabbath is delightful to the pious.  It makes them more and more like God, and the manifestations which on that day he makes of himself, and in the everlasting and glorious ends which, through the Sabbath and its means of grace, he will accomplish.

title: Exodus 31:18
text: Tables of testimony; on which were written, by the finger of God, the ten commandments,  Exodus 20:3-17 , testifying his will and the duty of men.   Exodus 20:3-17 Exodus 24:12 Exodus 32:15-16

title: Exodus 32:1
text:
Out of the mount;   
  Gods; idols, or an idol to represent God. 
 
  Wot; know. 
 
Into whatever engagements men enter to serve the Lord, if left to their own sinful inclinations they will soon break them, and plunge into wickedness, to their disgrace and ruin.

title: Exodus 32:6
text:
Play; engage in revelling and wantonness. 
 
Those forms of religion which gratify the pride, selfishness, and carnal inclinations of men, while they attract great numbers, instead of making them better, only make them worse and ripen them for divine judgments.

title: Exodus 32:7
text: Thy people, which thou broughtest; he says not, my people, whom I brought; but, thy people, which thou broughtest; as if he would disown Israel as his people.

title: Exodus 32:9
text: Stiff-necked; refusing to yield obedience to the commands of God.

title: Exodus 32:10
text: Let me alone; do not ask me to spare them.

title: Exodus 32:11
text: Moses in reply says, Thy people, which thou hast brought, and adds also that it was with a mighty hand; because he means to plead the covenant relation of God to Israel, and the wonders He has already wrought in their behalf, as a reason why He should spare them.  In this prayer the one appeal of Moses is to Jehovah's glory; and this is a prevailing plea.

title: Exodus 32:12
text: Repent of this evil; not destroy the people, but spare them.

title: Exodus 32:14
text: Prayer for sinners, offered from regard to the glory of God, has great influence with him, and is often the means of changing his conduct towards them; so that, instead of destroying them, he brings them to repentance, and bestows upon them precious and everlasting mercies.

title: Exodus 32:15
text: Tables of the testimony; those on which God had written the ten commandments.

title: Exodus 32:19
text: He--broke them; to show the people, in a significant manner, that they had broken the covenant into which they had solemnly entered,  Exodus 24:4 Exodus 24:7 , and deserved to be destroyed.

title: Exodus 32:20
text: The water; which flowed from the rock,  Exodus 17:6 , and of which the people continued to drink.

title: Exodus 32:24
text: When good men connive at iniquity, and especially when they aid in promoting it, their guilt is exceedingly great, and the excuses which they make are both cowardly and foolish.  If such conduct does not bring destruction on themselves, it may on multitudes of others.

title: Exodus 32:25
text: Naked; stripped of their ornaments, and exposed.

title: Exodus 32:27
text: His brother--companion, and--neighbor; all who had been engaged in this idolatry.

title: Exodus 32:29
text:
Consecrate yourselves; devote yourselves to the Lord, in the execution of his will in punishing the transgressors. 
 
It is sometimes a duty to take away human life; and in doing it we may honor God, do good to men, and secure special divine favor.  When done at the command of God, or in obedience to his will, it is a proper and useful expression of his indignation against sin.

title: Exodus 32:30
text: Make an atonement; obtain mercy for them.

title: Exodus 32:32
text: Blot me--out of thy book; if thou destroy them let me die also, and not live to see thy dishonor and thy ruin.

title: Exodus 32:34
text:
Visit; that is, with evils. 
 
Respite or delay of punishment is not forgiveness; and persons may be spared for a time, and yet afterwards be destroyed.  The goodness of God in delaying punishment, should lead all to repentance.  If it does not, it will in the end aggravate their ruin.

title: Exodus 33:3
text: I will not go; not go with his visible, special presence, but would send an Angel to lead them, as stated  Exodus 33:2 Exodus 32:34 .

title: Exodus 33:4
text: No created beings and no earthly enjoyments can be an adequate substitute for the presence and favor of God.  Without him as our friend and portion, however many other things we may have, we shall ultimately be wretched.

title: Exodus 33:5
text:
I will--consume thee; this he might justly do; and this, should they continue their wickedness, he would do.  We may, however, render these words, If I come up into the midst of thee for one moment, I shall consume thee. 
 
  Therefore now put off thy ornaments; he will have them put themselves in the dress of criminals, while he, as it were, deliberates what he shall do to them.

title: Exodus 33:6
text: By the mount Horeb; or, at a distance from the mount Horeb.

title: Exodus 33:7
text:
The tabernacle; not the holy tent for the building of which directions had been given, for that was not yet made; but probably the public tent of the congregation, where Moses had been accustomed to hear causes, and where also, before the arrival at Sinai, he had received communications from God. 
 
  Without the camp; implying that the people's sins had cut them off from the privilege of having God's presence in the camp. 
 
  The Tabernacle of the congregation; the place where the penitent of the congregaiton should assemble, and where God would meet them. 
 
If men would find mercy and obtain the favor of God, they must seek him while he is to be found, and call upon him while he is near; repent of their sins, forsake their evil ways, and turn heartily to him: then he will abundantly pardon.   Isaiah 55:7

title: Exodus 33:10
text: Worshipped; bowed themselves in token of worshipping Jehovah, who was in the cloudy pillar.

title: Exodus 33:11
text: Departed not out of the tabernacle; he seems to have remained in charge of it.

title: Exodus 33:12
text:
Thou hast not let me know; he had only told him he would send an Angel before them,  Exodus 33:2 ; and Moses wished for more information, especially that God, by his own presence, would go with them. 
 
  By name; as his intimate and peculiar friend.

title: Exodus 33:13
text:
Thy way; God's way of dealing with men, including his purposes and will respecting Israel,  Psalms 25:4 .  This prayer is nearly related to that in  Exodus 33:18 . 
 
Clear views of the will and ways of God are earnestly desired by his people; especially such views as shall make plain the path of duty, and prepare them faithfully to walk in it.

title: Exodus 33:14
text:
My presence shall go; in the pillar of cloud and of fire, to guide and protect them.  Thus the prayer of Moses was answered. 
 
  Give thee rest; thee and thy people.

title: Exodus 33:16
text: Thou goest with us? in the cloudy pillar, thus showing that they were his people, and he was their God.

title: Exodus 33:17
text: The number and greatness of the favors which God has bestowed, may be pleaded as a reason why he should bestow still more and greater.  When rightly improved, the more numerous they are the more numerous will be those which shall follow.

title: Exodus 33:18
text: Show me thy glory; Moses asks and receives such a visible manifestation of Jehovah's glory as is at the same time a revelation of his glorious character and attributes. See  Exodus 33:23 Exodus 34:5-7 .

title: Exodus 33:19
text:
The name of the Lord; his glorious attributes; for his name is the sum of these. 
 
  Be gracious--show mercy; his sovereignty in dealing with sinners, which is always guided by infinite wisdom and goodness, is a part of his glory.

title: Exodus 33:20
text: My face; that is, my face when I appear to thee in my glory.  In conversing with Moses face to face, God had veiled his glory, that his servant might not be overwhelmed by its brightness.

title: Exodus 33:21
text: By me; on Sinai.

title: Exodus 33:22
text: Passeth by; in visible form, and, as appears from  Exodus 33:23 , in the form of man.  It was the eternal Word that made to Moses this revelation,  John 1:18 ; and it was an anticipation of the glory in which he now reveals himself at the right hand of the Father.  Compare  Matthew 17:2 Acts 26:13-15 Revelation of John 1:13-17 .

title: Exodus 33:23
text: However great the manifestations of the glory of God, his people desire to see more; and they will see more, and still more, as their blessedness and usefulness may require.  But however much they may see, and however long their knowledge may continue to increase, it will only increase their sense of the infinitude of what remains unseen.  II Corinthians 3:18

title: Exodus 34:1
text: Notwithstanding the indignation of Jehovah against backsliders, those who repent and seek his mercy he will forgive, renew his covenant with them, and take them again under his gracious care.

title: Exodus 34:5
text: The name; his various perfections, which are included in his name.

title: Exodus 34:7
text:
By no means clear; literally, clearing will not clear.  Even the penitent, while they escape destruction, will not wholly escape the consequences of sin; and the perseveringly inmpenitent will finally perish. 
 
  Upon the children; children often suffer from the sins of parents, while the punishment of no one is ever greater than his own sins deserve. 
 
Though God forgives his penitent believing people, he does not deliver them from all the consequences of their sins.  The evils of them they may feel, in numerous ways, to the end of life, and even transmit to future generations; while none who do not repent, and turn heartily to him, can escape utter and irretrievable ruin.

title: Exodus 34:10
text:
Make a covenant; he renewed his promise, though the people had so shamefully and wickedly broken theirs. 
 
  Do marvels; perform wonderful things in giving their children the land of Canaan. 
 
  A terrible thing; he would accomplish, through their means, towards their enemies.

title: Exodus 34:11
text:
That which I command; it is to be noticed that  Exodus 34:26  contain a repetition of that part of chapters 21-23, in which the duties of the Israelites towards God as his covenant-people are specified.  Thus he formally renewed with them the covenant which they had broken. 
 
No repentance of sin or professed reformation will avail to salvation, which does not lead men to do what God commands them.

title: Exodus 34:12
text:
A covenant; a treaty of peace. 
 
  A snare; means of leading them into sin.

title: Exodus 34:13
text: Their groves; or, their images of Ashtaroth, which were generally of wood.

title: Exodus 34:14
text:
A jealous God; especially displeased with those who worship any thing except himself. 
 
To regard any object above Jehovah, or pay even external worship to any but him, is exceedingly offensive in his sight, and exposes those who are guilty of it to his just indignation.

title: Exodus 34:15
text: Intimate connection with the openly wicked, and all apparent joining with them in their iniquity, or conniving at it, should be carefully avoided.

title: Exodus 34:17
text: Molten; that is, melted; idols cast in a furnace.

title: Exodus 34:18
text: The feast of unleavened bread; that connected with the passover.  Exodus 12:14-20

title: Exodus 34:19
text: Is mine;  Exodus 13:2 Exodus 13:12 Exodus 13:1

title: Exodus 34:21
text:
Earing; ploughing. 
 
  Harvest; in the most busy seasons of the year, when they would be most strongly tempted to break the Sabbath, as well as at other times, they were to rest and keep the day holy. 
 
Often, plainly, and expressly, God commands men to keep the Sabbath; and no pressure of worldly business, even in the most pressing season, should lead them ever to neglect it.  They have no right to do, to attempt, or wish to do any more business than is consistent with their remembering the Sabbath-day to keep it holy.

title: Exodus 34:22
text:
Feast of weeks; pentecost, which began seven weeks, or the fiftieth day after the passover.   Exodus 23:16 Deuteronomy 16:9-10  
 
  Feast of ingathering; of tabernacles, which was observed at the close of the harvest.   Exodus 23:14-16

title: Exodus 34:24
text:
Desire thy land; while all the able-bodied men should be absent, God would not only prevent their land from being invaded, but he would keep their enemies from desiring it.  This promise was literally fulfilled.  In the history of the Jews, no instance is known of their enemies' taking advantage of their attendance upon the appointed feasts to invade the land. 
 
God is able so to control the desires and efforts of men, that none shall in the end be losers from conscientiously and perseveringly obeying him.

title: Exodus 34:27
text: It is a great blessing to have the words of the Lord written in a book. And as we have the book which contains them, written not in words which man's wisdom taught, but which the Holy Ghost taught, their meaning should be communicated in the plainest manner to all the people.

title: Exodus 34:28
text: He wrote; the Lord wrote the ten commandments on these tables, as he had done on the first, which were broken; and the other commands Moses wrote as God directed him,  Exodus 34:1 Deuteronomy 10:4 .

title: Exodus 34:29
text: His face shone; this was the effect of being with God, and beholding his glory.

title: Exodus 34:33
text:
He put a veil on his face; to prevent their being afraid of him. The shining of his face indicated the glory, and his veiling it indicated the darkness of that dispensation, compared with the gospel. The veil also fitly illustrated the darkness of the human mind as to spiritual things, without the illuminating influences of the Holy Spirit.   II Corinthians 3:6-18  
 
The meaning and use of the Old Testament are, to a great extent, explained in the New.  They are parts of the same revelation, and a knowledge of both is necessary in order to a full understanding of either.  Those, therefore, who think that the Old Testament is out of date, and that the study of it can be neglected without sin, or without great loss to the soul, do exceedingly err, not knowing the Scriptures.

title: Exodus 35:2
text: The observance of the Sabbath was so essential to the civil welfare of the Israelites, and to the prevalence and perpetuity of true religion, that it was here placed first among the directions which God gave his people.  The command to keep it holy was often repeated, and on a variety of occasions; and the open, presumptuous violation of it was to be punished with death.

title: Exodus 35:3
text: Kindle no fire; for any worldly purpose; not even to manufacture articles for the tabernacle or sanctuary of the Lord.

title: Exodus 35:4
text:
vv 4-29. 
 
The tabernacle.   Exodus 25:2-40

title: Exodus 35:5
text: Free, voluntary offerings for the purpose of promoting the glory of God and the good of mankind, are peculiarly pleasing to him.

title: Exodus 35:10
text: Those whose talents and skill are employed in doing what God has commanded, are, in the best sense, wise-hearted; while those whose powers are not employed in obeying him, are, in the most emphatic sense, fools.   Psalms 14:1 Proverbs 17:16

title: Exodus 35:18
text: Pins of the tabernacle; supposed to be those to which the cords of the sacred tent were fastened, and which were driven into the ground, to keep it firm in its place.

title: Exodus 35:22
text:
Tablets; supposed to be ornaments worn around the head or neck. 
 
All who are truly wise, both men and women, when they know the will of God, will be disposed to do it; and in offering willingly to him of what he ahs given them, they will derive from it greater enjoyment and benefit than if they had hoarded it, or employed it on themselves.

title: Exodus 35:25
text: Wise-hearted; skilled in curious spinning.

title: Exodus 35:29
text: In giving to the Lord of what he has given to them, all may take a part, the poor as well as the rich, and their offerings may be equally acceptable.  If there be a willing mind, it is accepted according to what any one hath, and not acording to what he hath not.  Mark 12:43-44 II Corinthians 8:12

title: Exodus 35:34
text: Mechanical skill, as really as divine grace, men receive from God; but they can obtain and confer the benefits of neither without their own efforts.  And both, to be accepted, must be employed in the service and to the glory of the Giver.

title: Exodus 36:1
text: Then wrought; rather, and Bezaleel and Aholiab shall work. Accordingly Moses calls them,  Exodus 36:2 , to this service.

title: Exodus 36:3
text: Those who are intrusted with public contributions should conscientiously appropriate them to the objects for which they are given, and avoid both the reality and the appearance of employing any part of them for other purposes.

title: Exodus 36:7
text: The hearts of men, and all their powers, are so under the control of God, that he can at any time lead them to devote any portion of what he gives them to his service, and make them instrumental, in such ways as he sees best, of advancing his cause.

title: Exodus 37:1
text: As the dwelling of God in the tabernacle, and the sacrifices of his people, were preparatory to and emblematical of his tabernacling in human flesh, and by one offering of himself opening the treasures of his grace to mankind, every thing relating to them is recorded with minute exactness, and the fact carefully stated that all was done according to the pattern shown to Moses in the mount; thus indicating that redemption is peculiarly the work of God, and reflecting special honor on Christ as Redeemer.

title: Exodus 37:2
text: He overlaid it with pure gold; some have supposed that this was done with thin plates, others that it was gilt.

title: Exodus 38:1
text: The altar;

title: Exodus 38:8
text:
The laver;   
  Looking-glasses; mirrors of polished metal. 
 
  Which assembled; for religious purposes, and to unite in the worship of God. 
 
Religion has ever taken a strong and permanent hold upon the heart of woman; and while it has greatly elevated, adorned, and ennobled her character, increased her enjoyments, and extended her usefulness, it has been greatly promoted by her prayers, her example, her sacrifices, and her efforts.

title: Exodus 38:9
text: The court;  Exodus 27:1

title: Exodus 38:18
