text: The height in the breadth; the height of the gate, or entrance, was equal to the breadth of the curtain, or hanging, which closed it.

title: Exodus 38:21
text: The sum; enumeration or statement of the various articles for the tabernacle.

title: Exodus 38:24
text:
Talents--shekels; a shekel was half an ounce avoir-dupois, and a talent equal to three thousand shekels, or ninety-three pounds and twelve ounces.  In value, a shekel was about fifty cents, and a talent of silver about fifteen hundred dollars.  A talent of gold was equal, it is supposed, to about twelve times that amount. 
 
However much property, at the direction of God, is devoted to the promotion of his glory, in the establishment and support of his worship, instead of being lost, as many suppose, it is employed to the greatest advantage, both to the possessors and to the world.

title: Exodus 39:2
text:
vv 2-31. 
 
The high-priest's dress.   Exodus 28:1-43

title: Exodus 39:32
text: When numbers unite earnestly and perseveringly in a good work, much, with the blessing of God, may be accomplished in a short time.

title: Exodus 39:37
text: To be set in order; or, arranged in order, that is, in a row.

title: Exodus 39:42
text: When things are undertaken and accomplished according to the directions of God, they will be done in the best manner.

title: Exodus 39:43
text: When others have done will we should show ourselves pleased, ask God to bless them, and give to him the glory.

title: Exodus 40:1
text: The return of the seasons is well adapted to remind us of the goodness of God, and our obligations to him for his mercies.  And when, according to his will, we begin the year with devoutly acknowledging and adoring him, we may hope that whether we continue to its close in this world, or are removed to another, we shall still be happy in the service of God.

title: Exodus 40:2
text: The first day of the first month; they started from Egypt on the fifteenth day of the first month.  On the fiftieth day after, the law was given from mount Sinai; and Moses was eighty days in the mount.  A number of other things were done, and several delays occasioned, which must have occupied about six months, before the tabernacle was begun. As the first day of the first month would make a year from the time they left Egypt wanting fifteen days, they were probably employed not far from six months in preparing the tabernacle.

title: Exodus 40:15
text: Such is the nature of men, and such the ways in which they are most usefully impressed, that the setting apart of particular places for public worship, and of particular men to conduct it, is suited to promote their highest good.

title: Exodus 40:17
text: In the second year; after their departure from Egypt.

title: Exodus 40:20
text: The testimony; the tables containing the ten commandments, that solemn testimony of God with regard to the duty of men.

title: Exodus 40:21
text: The veil of the covering; that which covered or closed the entrance into the holy of holies, and thus prevented the ark from being seen, except by the high-priest once a year.   Exodus 30:10 Hebrews 9:7

title: Exodus 40:32
text:
As the Lord commanded;  Exodus 30:19-21 
 
The doing of all things as the Lord commands, is the sure way of promoting his glory, and of obtaining his blessing.  It is also the way to make our temporary sojourn on earth a preparation for an eternal dwelling with God in heaven.

title: Exodus 40:33
Exodus 40:34
text:
A cloud; that in which Jehovah dwelt. 
 
  The glory of the Lord; the resplendent brightness which manifested his presence.

title: Exodus 40:36
text: The cloud was taken up; and moved forward in the way that they should go.   Exodus 13:21-22 Numbers 9:15-23 Nehemiah 9:19 Psalms 78:14 Psalms 105:39

title: Exodus 40:38
text: All the preparation that was made to provide a dwelling-place for God, and institute his worship among the Israelites, the glory which filled the tabernacle, his guidance of them by the pillar of cloud and fire in all their journey through the wilderness, and his introduction of them into Canaan, prefigured his dwelling in human nature and becoming the light of the world, that such as should follow him might be guided by his counsel and afterwards be received to glory.   John 1:14 John 8:12   Hebrews 9:2-28

title: Leviticus 1:1
text: Out of the tabernacle; the previous directions God gave to Moses from the mount; the subsequent, from the tabernacle.

title: Leviticus 1:3
text:
A burnt-sacrifice; all the sacrifices signified the expiation of sin through the shedding of the blood,  Hebrews 9:22 ; and since "it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins,"  Hebrews 10:4 , they typified the efficacious atonement of Christ's blood,  Hebrews 9:12-14 .  When he offered himself on Calvary for the sins of the world, the Levitical sacrifices ceased to have any further office.  The first and most important sacrifice was the burnt- offering, which was wholly consumed on the altar, and is, for this reason, sometimes called a whole burnt-offering,  Deuteronomy 33:10 Psalms 51:19 . On the part of the offerer, this signified the entireness of his faith and devotion to God, and on the part of the sacrifice, the completeness of the expiation. 
 
  Without blemish; this was required in all sacrifices.  It indicated, on the offerer's part, that he gave to God the best he had; and, on the part of the victim, the perfection of Jesus Christ, the great atoning sacrifice. 
 
  Of his own voluntary will; or, that he may be accepted, as in  Exodus 28:38 , where the same word is used. 
 
We should be voluntary, cheerful, and hearty in all our offerings to God; for he looks upon the heart and loves a cheerful giver.  II Corinthians 9:7

title: Leviticus 1:4
text:
Put his hand upon the head of the burnt-offering; this also was required in the case of every sacrifice.  Thus the offerer solemnly devoted it to God, and signified his desire that the death of the innocent victim might be a substitute for his own death. 
 
The great doctrine of atonement by the sufferings of the innocent for the guilty, has ever held a conspicuous place in the communications of God with men; and he has shown himself to be just, as well as merciful, in his bestowment of blessings upon them.

title: Leviticus 1:6
text: Flay; take off the skin.

title: Leviticus 1:9
text:
Wash in water; showing the necessity of internal purification. 
 
  A sweet savor; acceptable to God, as pointing to the atonement of Christ. 
 
Purity of heart, as well as reliance on the atonement, is needful to acceptance with God.

title: Leviticus 1:11
text: Northward; the approach to the altar is supposed to have been from the south; the ashes and refuse to have been cast on the east side,  Leviticus 1:16 ; while the tabernacle stood on the west.  This left the north side vacant.

title: Leviticus 1:13
text: The offering of innocent animals for guilty men typified the death of Christ for sinners, that God might be just and yet justify the ungodly. See the epistle to the Hebrews, a book which may be profitably read in connection with the books of Leviticus and Numbers.

title: Leviticus 1:14
text: Turtledoves; emblems of meekness, innocence, and purity.  These were brought by the poor, who were not able to provide a more costly sacrifice.  Compare  Leviticus 5:7 Leviticus 12:8 .

title: Leviticus 1:17
text:
Not divide it asunder; not entirely separate one part from the other.   Leviticus 5:8  
 
The hearty offerings of the poor, though in the sight of men of small value, may through the atonement be as acceptable to God as the most costly offerings of the rich, and may receive as great reward.

title: Leviticus 2:1
text: A meat-offering; meat, in the Bible, means any kind of food; in this case, it means flour, and articles of food made of it.  Of the burnt-offerings described in the preceding chapter, the whole was burnt with fire; of the meat-offerings described in this chapter, a part, called the memorial,  Leviticus 2:2 , was burnt, and the rest was eaten by the priests,  Leviticus 2:3 .  As the bloody offerings typified the expiation of sin through the blood of Christ, so these unbloody oblations signified that the offerer devoted himself and all that he had to God in holy love and obedience.  From such oblations the priests had, in part at least, their maintenance.

title: Leviticus 2:2
text: Oil--frankincense; emblems of the influences of the Holy Spirit, and the acceptable intercession of Christ and the supplications of his people.   Isaiah 61:1 I John 2:27 Psalms 141:2 Revelation of John 8:3-4

title: Leviticus 2:3
text: God has ever required that a support be provided for his ministers. Under the Old Testament, he ordained that those who waited at the altar should be partakers with the altar; and under the New, that those who preach the gospel should live of the gospel.   I Corinthians 9:13-14

title: Leviticus 2:4
text: Wafers; thin cakes.

title: Leviticus 2:9
text: Christ, as our great High-priest and Intercessor, must present all our offerings perfumed with the incense of his merits, in order to have them rise with acceptance before God.   Revelation of John 8:3-4

title: Leviticus 2:11
text: No leaven, nor--honey; leaven was an emblem of hypocrisy, and honey of sensual indulgence, both of which are offensive to God.

title: Leviticus 2:13
text:
Salt; an emblem of purity, integrity, and perpetuity.   Mark 9:49   Colossians 4:6  
 
Pride, hypocrisy, and sinful indulgence of every sort must be avoided, and humility, sincerity, and self-denial assiduously cultivated, if we would meet the approbation and obtain the blessing of the Most High.

title: Leviticus 3:1
text: A sacrifice of peace-offering; the Hebrew word translated peace- offering signifies a rendering or paying to God of that which is his due, with the accessory idea that thus the offerer comes into a state of peace and communion with God.  The peace-offerings were of three kinds: thank-offerings, voluntary offerings, and offerings upon the payment of vows.   Leviticus 7:11-16   Certain portions only were burned on the altar; the breast and the right shoulder were given to the priests,  Leviticus 7:30-34 ; then the offerer and his friends feasted on the remainder; an expressive symbol of peace and communion with God through the blood of Christ, and of holy and joyous fellowship with each other.

title: Leviticus 3:2
text: Sprinkle the blood; typifying that blood which purifies the conscience from dead works to serve the living God.  Hebrews 9:11-14 Hebrews 12:24

title: Leviticus 3:5
text: Upon the burnt-sacrifice; the daily burnt-sacrifice, to consume which a fire was kept constantly burning upon the altar.   Leviticus 6:13

title: Leviticus 3:9
text: Rump; it is generally agreed that the Hebrew word signifies the very large and fat tail of the eastern sheep.

title: Leviticus 3:11
text: The food; that part of the beast or offering which was presented to God.   Leviticus 3:16 Leviticus 21:6 Leviticus 21:8 Leviticus 21:17 Leviticus 21:21 Leviticus 21:22 Numbers 28:2 Ezekiel 44:7 Malachi 1:7 Malachi 1:12   Revelation of John 3:20

title: Leviticus 3:17
text:
Neither fat nor blood; the fat of the inwards and the blood above-mentioned.  The one was to be burnt, and the other sprinkled upon the altar.   Leviticus 3:13 Leviticus 3:16  
 
While we receive with thanksgiving the mercies which God bestows, we should conscientiously abstain from using, and should sacredly consecrate to him, that portion which he requires.

title: Leviticus 4:2
text: Through ignorance; not sensible at the time of doing what was wrong, but becoming convinced of it afterwards.  Leviticus 4:23 Leviticus 4:28

title: Leviticus 4:3
text:
The priest that is anointed; the high-priest.   Exodus 29:7 Exodus 29:29 Exodus 29:30   Leviticus 8:12 Leviticus 21:10-12  
 
  According to the sin of the people; or to bring guilt upon the people; for he acted as their representative, and his sin involved them in its consequences. 
 
  For a sin-offering; in the burnt-offering and peace-offering there was an acknowledgment of general sinfulness which needed expiation. But the sin-offering was for particular transgressions of the law. 
 
There is no man or body of men on earth infallible, or perfect.  All are liable to sin, through carelessness, inattention, and the influence of temptation.  All need repentance and pardon through faith in the atonement of Jesus Christ.   Psalms 19:12-14

title: Leviticus 4:4
text: Lay his hand upon the bullock's head; solemnly consecreating the victim to God as an offering for sin; thus confessing his own sin, and his desire to have the liability to suffer transferred from himself to the sacrifice of God's appointment.

title: Leviticus 4:6
text: Seven; a number signifying fulness, completeness.

title: Leviticus 4:12
text:
The whole bullock; except the fat, which was burnt, and the blood.  Leviticus 4:6-10 . 
 
  With fire; a fire made upon the ground for that purpose. 
 
The way in which God pardons sin is suited to make a deep impression of its evil, and lead men to abhor and forsake it.

title: Leviticus 4:15
text: The elders; their chief men, magistrates, representatives of the people.

title: Leviticus 4:20
text: Make an atonement--be forgiven; he who, in the spirit of true faith and penitence, presented to God his sin-offering, was saved not only from the temporal punishment of his sin, but also, through the atonement of Christ which this offering typified, from its eternal consequences.

title: Leviticus 4:21
text: Nations, as well as individuals, may commit great iniquity; and without national repentance, reformation, and pardon through the atonement of Christ, such iniquity will draw down upon them the sore judgments of God.

title: Leviticus 4:26
text: Rulers and teachers, ecclesiastical and civil, often fall into sin like other men; and without repentance and forgiveness, in the way that God has provided and made known, they will perish.

title: Leviticus 4:35
text: Pardon of all transgressions is as free to the common people, to the poor and despised, as to the rich and the great.   Acts 2:21 Acts 10:34   Romans 10:11-13

title: Leviticus 5:1
text:
Hear the voice of swearing; literally, "the voice of an oath;" that is, an oath administered by the magistrate, when one is summoned to testify, under oath, as to what he knows about a matter in question. 
 
  If he do not utter it; does not tell what he knows. 
 
  He shall bear his iniquity; has sinned, and is exposed to punishment. 
 
We should hate sin in ourselves, and by all suitable means endeavor to prevent it in others.  When called in providence to testify before a magistrate, or in a court of justice, we should let nothing hinder us from doing it with fidelity.

title: Leviticus 5:3
text: He shall be guilty; of violating that ceremonial law, when he knows what he has done.

title: Leviticus 5:4
text:
A soul swear; rashly, as to what he will or will not do, and when it may be wicked, or not in his power to do it. 
 
  It be hid from him; if he was not aware at the time that it was wicked, or was not in his power. 
 
We should be careful never to declare what is false, or promise to do what is impracticable or wicked.  Especially should we avoid all rash and profane oaths.

title: Leviticus 5:5
text: We may do wrong without at the time being aware of it.  When we see the wrong, we should be ready to confess and forsake it.

title: Leviticus 5:7
text:
Sin-offering;  Leviticus 4:24-26 Leviticus 4:32-27:34 
  Burnt-offering;  Leviticus 1:14-17:1

title: Leviticus 5:10
text:
According to the manner; the manner prescribed in the previous chapters. 
 
No sins, not even those of ignorance or carelessness, even when truly repented of, can be forgiven except through the atonement of Jesus Christ.

title: Leviticus 5:11
text:
A sin-offering; in this case, from consideration of the offerer's poverty, an exception was made to the rule that an expiatory offering must be made through blood. 
 
It is not the greatness of the offerings which we present to God, but the spirit with which we offer them, that he principally regards.

title: Leviticus 5:12
text: A memorial;  Leviticus 2:1

title: Leviticus 5:13
text: A meat-offering;  Leviticus 2:1-3:1

title: Leviticus 5:15
text:
Holy things of the Lord; by withholding from God something which he required to be devoted to his ministers, or his worship and service. 
 
  Thy estimation; of the value of the things withheld, or perverted from the use which God required. 
 
  A trespass-offering; the exact distinction between a sin-offering and a trepass-offering it is difficult to determine.  The particular cases in which it was prescribed are enumerated in this book.  See  Leviticus 5:15-19 Leviticus 6:1-7 Leviticus 14:12-21 Leviticus 19:20-22 ; to which may be added,  Numbers 5:5-8 Numbers 6:9 Numbers 6:12 .

title: Leviticus 5:16
text: True repentance will lead a man not only to forsake his sins, but to make suitable restitution to those whom he has injured.

title: Leviticus 5:17
text:
Wist; knew. 
 
  Guilty; liable to suffer evil, and must, when he knows that he has broken the divine command, present the required offering.

title: Leviticus 5:19
text: We need the teaching of the Holy Spirit to see what is right, and be disposed heartily to do it.  We cannot faithfully review the past without perceiving that in many things we have done wrong, and need pardoning mercy through the atonement of Christ.

title: Leviticus 6:2
text:
In fellowship; or, in a deposit. 
 
When we wrong our fellow-men, we sin against God.

title: Leviticus 6:3
text: He who finds lost property, and does not wish to restore it to its rightful owner, when known, is dishonest.

title: Leviticus 6:5
text: Add the fifth part; this was the case when he voluntarily confessed his crime and restored that which was taken.  If he did not confess, but was convicted of the crime, he was to pay more.   Exodus 22:9-15

title: Leviticus 6:6
text: Thy estimation; of the amount which, according to the direction,  Leviticus 6:5 , he was to restore.   Leviticus 5:15

title: Leviticus 6:7
text: Though repentance, confession, and restitution are all needful in order to pardon, neither nor all of them can atone for sin, or of themselves obtain forgiveness.  There must also be application to that blood which was shed for many for the remission of sins.   Matthew 26:28

title: Leviticus 6:11
text: His garments; the holy garments which he wore in the sanctuary. These he was not allowed to wear elsewhere.

title: Leviticus 6:12
text: As the priest was every morning to put wood on the altar, that the fire might never go out; so we, who are called to be kings and priests unto God, should every morning kindle anew the flame of divine love in our hearts, that it may warm all our services, and shine brightly through all the duties and events of the day.   Matthew 5:16 Jude 1:21

title: Leviticus 6:13
text: The fire--shall never go out; this fire was first kindled from heaven; and the priests, by timely application of fuel, were to keep it continually burning.   Leviticus 9:24

title: Leviticus 6:14
text:
vv 14-17. 
 
  Meat-offering;  Leviticus 2:1-16:1

title: Leviticus 6:17
text: Often, and in various ways, God warns men against insincerity and hypocrisy, and urges upon them the habitual practice, in all things, of perfect sincerity and truth.   I Corinthians 5:7-8

title: Leviticus 6:18
text: Shall be holy; none but consecrated persons should touch them, and they must be free from ceremonial defilement.

title: Leviticus 6:19
text:
vv 19-23. 
 
  Offering of Aaron;  Exodus 25:1-25

title: Leviticus 6:25
text:
vv 25-30. 
 
  Sin-offering;  Leviticus 4:24-27:34

title: Leviticus 6:28
text: All the directions of God with regard to things connected with his worship, are suited to impress upon men the conviction of his purity and their pollution, and that without holiness no man can see his face in peace.   Leviticus 19:2 Leviticus 20:7 Hebrews 12:14 I Peter 1:16

title: Leviticus 7:7
text: Shall have it; that portion of it which was not burnt on the altar.

title: Leviticus 7:10
text: While God requires his ministers to devote their time and talents to his immediate service, he also requires that their temporal wants be supplied by those for whose spiritual good they labor.  Leviticus 7:31-36 Leviticus 10:13-15

title: Leviticus 7:13
text: Leavened bread; that which was offered to the Lord was to be unleavened, as before prescribed,  Leviticus 7:12 ; but that which the priest ate himself, in token of thanksgiving for mercies, might, like common bread, be leavened.

title: Leviticus 7:15
text: The same day that it is offered; this was probably to prevent its being reserved by the offerer for his private use.  He had devoted it to Jehovah, and now it was no longer his own.  Of it he was to make a feast for his friends, and especially for the poor of his people.

title: Leviticus 7:16
text:
A vow; a sacrifice offered upon the paying of a vow.  The flesh of this, and of the voluntary offering, might be eaten the second day; but what remained till the third day was to be burnt with fire.  In those warm regions it is difficult to keep flesh over the second day in perfect purity, which may have been one reason for this injunction. 
 
While we are called to mourning on account of our sins, we are also called to rejoicing on account of the goodness of God; and our joy may sometimes be appropriately express by feasting on the bounties of his providence and grace.

title: Leviticus 7:18
text:
It; his offering.  If he ate any of the flesh after the second day, his offering would be rejected. 
 
  Bear his iniquity; be held guilty, and exposed to punishment.

title: Leviticus 7:20
text: Cut off;  Genesis 17:1

title: Leviticus 7:23
text: No manner of fat; of that fat of beasts which was to be offered in sacrifice to God.   Leviticus 7:3-5 Leviticus 7:25

title: Leviticus 7:26
text: No manner of blood; that which flows from the arteries and veins, called the life, or the blood of the life.  The blood which mingled with the flesh when cooked, was not forbidden.   Genesis 9:4-5

title: Leviticus 7:30
text: Each individual, while he relies on the great atonement for salvation, must also himself be voluntary and active in presenting his offerings to God, and in doing what he requires.

title: Leviticus 7:34
text: Wave-breast--heave-shoulder; that had been consecrated to Jehovah by waving and heaving.

title: Leviticus 7:35
text: The portion of the anointing of Aaron; his portion in consequence of his having been anointed as high-priest.   Leviticus 7:36

title: Leviticus 7:37
text:
vv 37-38. 
 
  The law of the--offerings;  Exodus 29:1-40:38

title: Leviticus 8:1
text: The Lord spake unto Moses; after the tabernacle was finished, and the way prepared for the consecration of Aaron and his sons to the priesthood.

title: Leviticus 8:5
text: The thing which the Lord commanded;  Exodus 28:1

title: Leviticus 8:9
text: If the ministers of religion are comely in the sight of God, or in any measure fitted for their work, it must be through the comeliness which he puts upon them--clothing them with his righteousness, and adorning them with the graces of his Spirit.

title: Leviticus 8:12
text: Sanctify him; set him apart, or consecrate him to his sacred office.

title: Leviticus 8:14
text: Even those who are the most solemnly consecrated to the service of God are themselves sinners, and need the cleansing of atoning blood.

title: Leviticus 8:17
text: As the Lord commanded;  Leviticus 4:11-12:1

title: Leviticus 8:30
text: In every thing sinners need the purifying influences of the Holy Spirit, in order to offer acceptable sacrifice to a holy God, or be prepared for his presence.   Hebrews 10:22

title: Leviticus 8:34
text: As he hath done this day; or, as it hath been done this day.  Each of the seven days he was to offer sacrifice, as he had the first day.

title: Leviticus 8:36
text: Ministers of religion who have a right spirit, will feel deeply the responsibilities of their office; that they are called to it not merely by men, but by God; and will labor first of all to please him by seeking his glory and doing his will.

title: Leviticus 9:4
text: The Lord will appear; in a special manner, and show his approbation of their services.   Leviticus 9:23-24

title: Leviticus 9:5
text: Before the Lord; before the tabernacle, or sanctuary, in which he dwelt.

title: Leviticus 9:7
text:
Go unto the altar; the altar of burnt-offerings; in the court, near the door of the tabernacle.   Exodus 27:1-8  
 
Ministers, after being duly consecrated to their office, should without delay enter upon the faithful discharge of its duties.

title: Leviticus 9:8
text: Atonement through the blood of Christ, and purification by the Holy Spirit, are among the first great doctrines which a minister should preach; and which, in their various relations, he should continue to inculcate through the whole of his ministry.

title: Leviticus 9:9
text: The sons of Aaron; Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.  Leviticus 10:1-6

title: Leviticus 9:16
text: According to the manner; the manner that God had prescribed.  Leviticus 1:10-13

title: Leviticus 9:21
text: As Moses commanded;

title: Leviticus 9:22
text: He should not confine himself to the preaching of a few of the many doctrines of the gospel, but should, in due time, order, and proportion, labor to inculcate the whole; and in such a manner as shall be most profitable to the people.

title: Leviticus 9:24
text:
From before the Lord; from his visible presence in the tabernacle. 
 
True love and devotion to God in the human heart are enkindled by the Holy Spirit; and the manifestation of his approval is a just cause of rejoicing.

title: Leviticus 10:1
text:
Censer; a fire-pan for sacred uses. 
 
  Strange fire; common fire--not that which was kindled by the Lord on the altar.   Leviticus 9:24   This event seems to have taken place in the sanctuary, whither they had gone in an irreverent and presumptuous manner to burn incense. 
 
Recklessness in divine worship, and the offering of our own excited and proud emotions instead of that humble and obedient spirit which he requires, are peculiarly offensive to God.

title: Leviticus 10:2
text:
From the Lord; from his visible glory on the mercy-seat. 
 
  Devoured; killed. 
 
Great sins and great trials may speedily follow the reception of great mercies.

title: Leviticus 10:3
text:
The Lord spake;  Exodus 19:22 Exodus 29:1 
  Them that come nigh me; especially those who conduct religious worship. 
 
  Held his peace; submitted without a murmur to the righteous judgment of God. 
 
Prompt and cheerful submission to God, and hearty acquiescence in his will, under trials, however great, is a fruit of the Spirit which peculiarly honors him, and is useful to men.

title: Leviticus 10:5
text: Out of the camp; for burial.

title: Leviticus 10:6
text: Uncover not--neither rend; avoid all appearance of mourning.

title: Leviticus 10:7
text:
Not go out; not suspend any of the duties of the ministry, but continue to discharge them. 
 
Regard for our friends, or sorrow on account of their death, must not lead us improperly to manifest grief, or to neglect our appropriate duties.

title: Leviticus 10:9
text: Do not drink wine nor strong drink; it is supposed that Nadab and Abihu had been drinking, and became excited; that this was one cause of their transgression; and that God enjoined on his ministers, when about to engage in public worship, entire abstinence from the use of intoxicating drink, that they might not be unfitted for their work.

title: Leviticus 10:10
text: Holy and unholy--unclean and clean; things which God forbids in his worship, and those which he requires.

title: Leviticus 10:11
text: The use of wine or strong drink is exceedingly dangerous, and should be abstained from, especially by ministers when about to engage in sacred public dities; that they may rightly conduct the worship of God, and make known his will to the people.

title: Leviticus 10:12
text: Meat-offering;  Leviticus 2:3 Leviticus 6:16 Leviticus 7:29-27:34

title: Leviticus 10:14
text: A cheerful reception of the good things of Providence, and at proper times and in suitable circumstances even feasting with our families on the fruits of divine kindness, is not only allowable, but is a duty, the right performance of which will promote the divine glory and our own highest good.

title: Leviticus 10:18
text: Ye should--have eaten it; if its blood had been brought into that part of the tabernacle called the sanctuary, or holy place, they were to burn it without the camp; if not, they were to eat it.  Leviticus 6:26-30

title: Leviticus 10:19
text:
This day--they offered;  Leviticus 9:8-21:1 
  Such things; the death of his two sons. 
 
  If I had eaten; joined with his family in feasting, while thus heavily afflicted. 
 
  Should it have been accepted? would it, under those peculiar circumstances, have been suitable or pleasing to God? 
 
Some things which on ordinary occasions would be right, proper, and useful, may without sin be omitted on occasions of great affliction and distress; and some things which on ordinary occasions would not be proper, may at such times be done.  I Samuel 21:6 II Chronicles 30:18-20 Matthew 9:15   Mark 2:19 Mark 2:25-26 Luke 5:34

title: Leviticus 10:20
text: He was content; satisfied that God would not be displeased with Aaron and his sons for what they had done.

title: Leviticus 11:1
text: This chapter treats of the distinction between clean and unclean meats, which entered largely into Jewish habits of thinking and acting.  It cannot be reasonable doubted that the clean animals here allowed were those which, to the people of that region, furnished the most wholesome diet.  But the distinction had a much deeper meaning.  It typified the inward difference which God's servants should make between clean and unclean affections, and the holy of unholy acts that proceed from them. Another end of these distinctions was to keep the Hebrews separate from all other nations, as a people devoted to Jehovah.

title: Leviticus 11:2
text: In eating and drinking, we should seek not merely to gratify appetite or preserve life, health, and reason, but to fit ourselves for the best discharge of our duties.  Whatever as to kind, quality, or quantity, tends to unfit us for this, should be rejected.   I Corinthians 10:31

title: Leviticus 11:3
text: Cloven-footed; having the hoof divided into two parts, like that of the ox and sheep.

title: Leviticus 11:4
text: Unclean; not to be eaten.

title: Leviticus 11:5
text: Coney; a small animal inhabiting high, rocky places.  Proverbs 30:26

title: Leviticus 11:8
text: Great attention and care are needful to avoid the commission of sin, and exposure to its punishment.

title: Leviticus 11:10
text: An abomination;  to be loathed and rejected.

title: Leviticus 11:13
text: Among the fowls; it is plain that the unclean birds here named are mostly, if not entirely, birds of prey, or such as feed on carrion. But the particular species cannot, in all cases, be determined.

title: Leviticus 11:20
text: Fowls that creep; winged insects.  See  Leviticus 11:21-23 .

title: Leviticus 11:21
text: Legs above their feet; those which, in addition to the feet on which they walk, have long legs with which to jump; as locusts and grasshoppers.

title: Leviticus 11:23
text: Flying creeping things; as flies, wasps, and bees.

title: Leviticus 11:24
text:
For these; the creatures mentioned  Leviticus 11:26-28 . 
 
  Unclean until the even; not admitted to unite in public worship, or associate with others who united in it.

title: Leviticus 11:25
text: Pollution by sin, and need of spiritual cleansing by the Holy Ghost, were taught abundantly in the Jewish ritual; and none who understand its teaching, can be ignorant of the doctrine of human depravity and the necessity of being born in order to see the kingdom of God.  John 3:10

title: Leviticus 11:29
text: Creeping things; by these the Hebrews understand small animals that move with a low or a crawling motion, as well as serpents and worms. Few of the particular species here mentioned can be determined with any certainty.

title: Leviticus 11:45
text: Holiness is to all men the one thing needful.  In every heart where it exists, it is the fruit of the Holy Spirit.  Hence, the reason why all men should hearken diligently to his voice speaking to them in the Bible, receive his teachings as infallible truth, and cordially obey them.

title: Leviticus 12:2
text: Unclean; ceremonially; not allowed to enjoy society, attend public ordinances, or eat of the offerings of which she might otherwise partake.   Leviticus 15:19-25

title: Leviticus 12:4
text: Three and thirty days; during this time she might have society, but not attend public worship or partake of ordinances.

title: Leviticus 12:6
text:
vv 6-8. 
 
  A burnt-offering--a sin-offering; these were to express her need of pardon, her gratitude to God for his mercies, her faith in his great atonement, and her devotion of herself and all that she had to his service.   Luke 2:22-24

title: Leviticus 12:7
text: Parents have always been bound gratefully to recognize the goodness of God in the birth of their children, to acknowledge their need of his mercy, and to train them for his service and glory.

title: Leviticus 12:8
text: The poor, as well as the rich, may have access to God, and be accepted of him.  As to property, opportunities, and capacities, God requires according to what men have, or may have, and not according to what they have not, or cannot have.

title: Leviticus 13:2
text: Leprosy; a foul disease covering the body with a kind of white scales; from its loathsome and incurable character, it is often referred to as an emblem of sin.  The terms, "a rising, a scab, or bright spot," describe three different varieties in its form of appearing.

title: Leviticus 13:3
text:
Unclean; leprous, and therefore to be excluded from divine ordinances and from society. 
 
Sin occasions a great variety of diseases, and will finally consign the body to the grave, and the soul, unless cleansed from its pollution, to perdition.  All should therefore be solicitous to know whether they are under its power; and if so, to apply without delay to Him who can say with effect, I will; be thou clean.   Matthew 8:3

title: Leviticus 13:6
text: Dark; or pale, dim, in opposition to bright.

title: Leviticus 13:7
text: In doubtful cases, persons should not be hasty in deciding upon their own spiritual state.  They should obtain all the light they can from experienced ministers and Christians; from self-examination, from the Scriptures, and religious books.  Above all, they should go habitually to God, earnestly praying, Search me, O God, and know my heart; try me, and know my thoughts; and see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.   Psalms 139:23-24

title: Leviticus 13:9
text: The plague of leprosy; another variety in its form, namely, the rising,  Leviticus 13:10 .

title: Leviticus 13:11
text: Old habits of sin, unless they are effectually renounced and forsaken, will revive and break out at times into flagrant transgression, and the last state of a man be worse than the first.   Matthew 12:45

title: Leviticus 13:13
text: He is clean; either it is not a true leprosy, or the leprosy has in this way healed itself.

title: Leviticus 13:17
text: Ministers of the gospel, and those who are called not only to judge of their own state, but to give directions to others, need great wisdom. They should be familiar with the Scriptures, well acquainted with themselves, and accustomed in every thing, by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, to make known their requests unto God.  Ephesians 6:18 Philippians 4:6

title: Leviticus 13:24
text:
A hot burning; in the original, a burning of fire; which seems ot mean a sore made by fire in which the plague of leprosy appears.  Some, however, suppose that it is an inflamed sore. 
 
  And the quick flesh that burneth have; or, "and the mark of the burning be," that is, break out into.

title: Leviticus 13:28
text: Not every sin of which a man may have been guilty, of itself merely, proves him to be in an unregenerate state; while no transgression of God's law, known, allowed, and persevered in, or not repented of and forsaken, can consist with a gracious and safe state.

title: Leviticus 13:30
text: Beard; a disease in the part from which the beard grows, and affecting the beard itself.

title: Leviticus 13:31
text: There is no black hair in it; the presence of this would be a favorable sign,  Leviticus 13:37 .  Its absence makes the case doubtful.

title: Leviticus 13:39
text: Darkish white; or dullish white, in opposition to bright white spots.

title: Leviticus 13:44
text: Persons may be free from one kind of sin, and yet deeply involved in another; and we are not to conclude that we are not under condemnation because we are not guilty of all sorts of transgressions, of sins which others practise, or which are known to our fellow-men; but we are to search out and forsake all iniquity; crying unto God, Cleanse thou me from secret faults, as well as, Keep me back from presumptuous transgressions.   Psalms 19:12-14

title: Leviticus 13:45
text:
A covering upon his upper lip; this was a sign of mourning and humiliation.   Ezekiel 24:17 Ezekiel 24:22 Micah 3:7  
 
  Unclean, unclean; as a warning to others not to approach him.

title: Leviticus 13:46
text: Sin is contagious, and all suitable efforts should be made to prevent one wicked person from corrupting others; we should not have for our companions any who lead us into sin.  I Corinthians 15:33 Psalms 1:1 Proverbs 4:14-15   Proverbs 13:20

title: Leviticus 13:47
text: The plague of leprosy; some infection that had a general resemblance to leprosy.

title: Leviticus 13:51
text: A fretting leprosy; corroding and destroying the cloth.

title: Leviticus 13:55
text:
Bare; deprived of its nap. 
 
  Within or without; on the inner or outer side of the garment.

title: Leviticus 13:56
text: Out of the warp, or out of the woof; as neither the warp nor the woof could be removed separately, the meaning seems to be, that by rending out the part affected, he shall remove the leprosy, whether it have its seat in the warp or the woof.

title: Leviticus 13:57
text: We should avoid not only the commission of sin, but the occasions of it; and make whatever sacrifice is needful to be delivered from its power.   Matthew 5:29-30 Matthew 6:13

title: Leviticus 14:2
text: When any one has reason to believe that he is delivered from the reigning power of sin, he should make it known, and seek admission to the fellowship of the church.

title: Leviticus 14:4
text:
Scarlet; wool dyed red. 
 
  Hyssop; a bushy plant of a spicy, fragrant smell, much used in ceremonial cleansings.   Exodus 12:22

title: Leviticus 14:5
text: Running water; living, fresh water, in distinction from that which is stagnant, or has been long standing.

title: Leviticus 14:6
text:
vv 6-7. 
 
  Shall dip them--shall sprinkle--shall let the living bird loose; the fragrant hyssop and cedar wood, the bright scarlet, and the running water, are all symbols of purity, as the blood is of cleansing.  The sprinkling of the man with these is a sign of his purification.  The living bird is first symbolically purified by being dipped in the blood and water, along with the hyssop, cedar wood, and scarlet.  Then it is let go free, to signify that the leper thus purified is set free and restored to the camp.  But he needs a further expiation before he can be restored to the privileges of the sanctuary, as the sacred writer proceeds to state.

title: Leviticus 14:8
text: He who is really cleansed from the pollution of sin, will gratefully acknowledge his indebtedness for the blessing to the grace of God in Jesus Christ, and will seek to purify himself more and more, and to perfect holiness in the fear of God.

title: Leviticus 14:10
text:
Three tenth-deals; a tenth-deal, or an omer, is the tenth of an ephah.   Exodus 16:36  
 
  One log; somewhat more than half a pint.

title: Leviticus 14:11
text: Maketh him clean; cleanses him ceremonially, as described in the following verses.

title: Leviticus 14:12
text: The change which has been wrought in a sinner when he becomes pious, is never to be ascribed to himself or to creatures, but always to God, and the glory to be given to Him.

title: Leviticus 14:17
text:
vv 17-18. 
 
  Ear--thumb--toe--head; in token that all his members and faculties need cleansing through the efficacy of the atonement, by the Holy Spirit; and should all be consecrated to the service of God.

title: Leviticus 14:21
text: Although a man who repents and forsakes his sins, is pardoned through faith in Christ, yet, to be saved, he must devote his powers of body and mind as an offering of gratitude to his service.

title: Leviticus 14:32
text: None are excluded from the benefits of Christ's salvation on account of their poverty; nor can any be saved except through faith in him, and consecration to his service and glory.

title: Leviticus 14:37
text:
If the plague be in the walls; this has been supposed to be something corrosive, which caused the walls to moulder away. 
 
  Lower than the wall; indentations or hollow places in the wall.

title: Leviticus 14:44
text: Fretting leprosy; eating away the walls, or causing them to decay.

title: Leviticus 14:45
text: Not only our souls, but our bodies, and all that we possess, are affected by sin.  Moth and rust corrupt; thieves break through and steal.  The earthly house of this tabernacle must be dissolved; the earth and all in it burnt up.  Happy they, and they only, who have a building of God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.

title: Leviticus 14:53
text: Let go the living bird; signifying that the house, thus purified, is free to the use of its owner.  See note on  Leviticus 14:6 .

title: Leviticus 15:1
text: The Lord spake; the evils about which he speaks in this chapter, and which have prevailed more or less in all ages and countries, may some of them have resulted from natural diseases, and others from diseases occasioned by vicious indulgence.  All either directly or indirectly spring from sin; and should teach us the necessity, in order to escape endless death, of being delivered from the power of sin.

title: Leviticus 15:3
text: Be stopped; he speaks not of a healthy, but of an unnatural stoppage.

title: Leviticus 15:7
text: With depraved hearts, and in a world of temptation, we are always exposed to contract moral pollution; and need to be kept, by the restraining and purifying grace of God, from its defiling power.

title: Leviticus 15:15
text: Nothing can avail to the pardon of sin, and the sanctification of the soul, but the atoning blood of Christ efficaciously applied by the Holy Ghost.

title: Leviticus 15:22
text: Sin is contagious; and all occasions of being defiled with it, in thought, word, or deed, should be carefully guarded against, and the prayer offered to God continually, "Lead us not into temptation; but deliver us from evil."

title: Leviticus 15:31
text: The great object of God in his regulations is, that men may be holy in body and spirit, and offer unto him acceptable service, through Jesus Christ, their strength and Redeemer.

title: Leviticus 16:1
text: In this chapter are described the solemn rites connected with the great day of atonement.  On this day alone the high priest was allowed to enter the Holy of Holies.  Thus the people were constantly reminded that the way by which sinners can approach a holy God was not yet made manifest.   Hebrews 9:8   At our Lord's crucifixion the veil that covered the Most Holy place was rent in twain from the top to the bottom,  Matthew 27:51 ; the Holy Ghost thus signifying that now the way of approach to God was laid open to all through the blood of Christ.

title: Leviticus 16:2
text: In the dealings of God with men, his justice is no less conspicuous than his mercy.  Those who approach him must do it not only with filial confidence, but with reverence and holy fear--in the way of his appointment, and for the purpose of honoring him as well as of obtaining benefits for themselves and their fellow-men.

title: Leviticus 16:5
text: Two kids--for a sin-offering; both the goats constituted together one expiatory offering, though but one of them was sacrificed.

title: Leviticus 16:6
text:
Shall offer his bullock; this is spoken by anticipation; its actual sacrifice is described in  Leviticus 16:11 . 
 
Often are we taught that the most holy men, in their most holy duties, need the influence of atoning blood, and the life-giving communications of the Holy Ghost.

title: Leviticus 16:8
text: For the Lord; that is, to be sacrificed to the Lord.

title: Leviticus 16:9
text: Offer him for a sin-offering; this also is spoken by anticipation. See  Leviticus 16:15 .

title: Leviticus 16:10
text: To make an atonement with him; in the Hebrew, to make an atonement upon him, namely, by typically laying upon his head the sins of the people, to be borne away by him.   Leviticus 16:20-22

title: Leviticus 16:11
text: Make an atonement for himself; being a sinner, he must first offer his own sin-offering, before he could present that of the people.  Hebrews 7:27

title: Leviticus 16:15
text:
Bring his blood within the veil; into the Holy of Holies.  This beautifully typifies Christ entering into the presence of God with his own blood, and presenting it before the Father as a perfect atonement for the sins of his people.   Hebrews 9:23-24  
 
Christ has not only made a full atonement for sin, and procured the blessings of the Holy Spirit, but has entered into heaven itself, and there ever lives to make effectual intercession for all who come unto God through him.

title: Leviticus 16:16
text:
vv 16-19 
 
  Because of the uncleanness of the children of Israel; thus signifying that so deep and universal is the pollution of sinners, that all their services, and every thing with which they have to do, needs purifying by the blood of Christ.

title: Leviticus 16:20
text: Reconciling the holy place--the tabernacle--the altar; making atonement for them, according to  Leviticus 16:16 .

title: Leviticus 16:21
text:
Putting them upon the head of the goat; typically transferring them to him; as if he were to carry them away, and thus the people be delivered from them and their consequences: thus pointing to Christ and his salvation.  Isaiah 53:4-12 John 1:29 Romans 4:25 I Peter 2:24 I Peter 3:18 I John 2:2  
 
  A fit man; or, a man ready at hand.

title: Leviticus 16:22
text: As far as the east is from the west, so far he removes the transgressions of all who trust in him; so that they will never rise in this world to their shame, nor in the future to their condemnation.

title: Leviticus 16:26
text: Shall wash his clothes; being typically defiled by contact with the scape-goat upon which the sins of the people had been laid.  So,  Leviticus 16:28 , he that burns the flesh of the two sin-offerings without the camp, is commanded to do the same thing.

title: Leviticus 16:28
text: The perpetual offerings of blood, and the perpetual applications of water, under the Old Testament dispensation, show our perpetual need of pardoning mercy through Christ, and of the cleansing influences of his Spirit, in order to preparation for heaven.

title: Leviticus 16:29
text: Seventh month; Tishri; answering to the last part of September and the first part of October.  It was the first month of the civil, and the seventh of the ecclesiastical year.

title: Leviticus 16:31
text: Afflict your souls; mourn over, confess, and forsake their sins.

title: Leviticus 16:34
text:
An everlasting statute; perpetual, to the end of the Jewish dispensation. 
 
Stated seasons, according to divine appointment, of rest from worldly business, cares, and amusements, to search out and confess their sins, acknowledge and adore Jehovah, and seek his blessing on themselves and others, have been observed by the people of God, and been seasons of great comfort and benefit to them in all ages of the world.

title: Leviticus 17:3
text: That killeth an ox, or lamb, or goat; some understand these words to mean, that whoever would kill for food any animal used in sacrifice, should bring it to the door of the tabernacle, and offer to the Lord that part prescribed for a peace-offering; the object of this law being to prevent secret sacrifices to devils,  Leviticus 17:7 .  But since it is expressly said that this shall be a "statute for ever," while, in  Deuteronomy 12:4-16 , they are required, after their entrance into Canaan, to bring only their sacrifices to the tabernacle, and have full liberty to "kill and eat flesh in all their gates," others suppose that the present passage also refers only to sacrifices.

title: Leviticus 17:4
text:
He hath shed blood; is to be accounted as a murderer.  Compare  Isaiah 66:3 . 
 
In all htings, especially things connected with the worship of God, we should be careful to follow his directions, and avoid both the reality and the appearnace of worshipping any one but Jehovah.

title: Leviticus 17:7
text: Worship presented to any but Jehovah is peculiarly offensive in his sight, and exposes those who render it to his indignation.

title: Leviticus 17:10
text: Eateth any manner of blood; the eating of blood was forbidden, to produce a more sacred regard to human life, and to the atonement of which blood was the emblem.   Leviticus 17:11-14

title: Leviticus 17:12
text: God requires, and in various ways inculcates, a sacred regard to human life; and especially to the great atonement which he has made by the shedding of that blood without which there could be no remission of sin.   Hebrews 9:22

title: Leviticus 17:16
text: In this world of impurity, we must have recourse to the great Purifier, whom clean water represents, or we shall live and die in pollution, and bear for ever the sad consequences of our sins.

title: Leviticus 18:3
text: The doings; the sinful practices.

title: Leviticus 18:4
text: Judgments;  Exodus 21:1 Deuteronomy 4:1-2 Deuteronomy 6:1

title: Leviticus 18:5
text: The sinful maxims and customs of this world we must forsake, and be guided, in our connections and conversations with others, by the revealed will of God, or be shut out of the heavens.

title: Leviticus 18:6
text: Marriage is an institution of God, and when it is entered into, and its duties discharged according to his will, it is honorable in all, a means of rich blessings to the persons concerned, and of great usefulness to others; and the violation of his will with regard to it, is a crime tending to the greatest guilt, debasement, and wretchedness in this life and the life to come.

title: Leviticus 18:7
text: The nakedness of thy father, or--of thy mother; the Hebrew may be rendered, the nakedness of thy father, and the nakedness of thy mother; because they were one flesh, and the dishonor done to her was done to him also.  Compare  Leviticus 18:8 .

title: Leviticus 18:21
text:
Thy seed; children or posterity. 
 
  Pass through the fire to Molech; be offered to that idol. 
 
  Profane the name of thy God; by giving that worship to another which is due to Him alone. 
 
The strong tendency to idolatry, and its great prevalence for so long a time and in so many nations, is conclusive evidence that men do not naturally like to retain the knowledge and worship of Jehovah, or to walk in his ways.

title: Leviticus 18:24
text: The nations--which I cast out; the Canaanites, which he would cast out.

title: Leviticus 18:25
text:
Vomiteth out her inhabitants; a strong expression, to denote their loathsomeness in the sight of God. 
 
That it should ever be needful for God to prohibit practices so unnatural and detestable as are here referred to, or that men should be disposed to degrade and sink themselves so low, is demonstration that madness, defilement, and death are in their hearts; and that except they be quickened, justified, and sanctified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of God, they can never see the kingdom of heaven.

title: Leviticus 18:28
text: It spued out; would spue out or eject the inhabitants.

title: Leviticus 18:30
text: I am the Lord your God; this is often mentioned as a strong and conclusive reason why they should in all things obey him.

title: Leviticus 19:2
text: As God is holy, so must we be in order to meet his approbation or enjoy his presence.

title: Leviticus 19:3
text:
Fear--mother--father; honor, reverence, esteem, and in all things right, please them.   Exodus 20:12 Matthew 19:19  
 
Due subordination and affection in families is inseparably connected with the right keeping of the Sabbath; and the neglect of the one tends directly and powerfully to the destruction of the other.

title: Leviticus 19:4
text: That men should ever forsake Jehovah for gods of their own making, is demonstration of their strong and active opposition to him.

title: Leviticus 19:5
text: At your own will; or, that ye may be accepted, namely, when ye comply with all the divine precepts concerning it.

title: Leviticus 19:7
text: It is abominable; the eating of it in opposition to the command of God was wicked, and incurred the divine displeasure.

title: Leviticus 19:8
text: To meet the approbation of God, men must not only be cheerful and hearty in serving him, but must be guided in their efforts by his directions.

title: Leviticus 19:10
text: God requires, and holiness leads men, to be not only pious, but benevolent; to be disposed, as there is opportunity and ability, to help the poor; and one of the best ways of helping them, is to lead them to help themselves.

title: Leviticus 19:12
text: Falsehood is intimately connected with theft; and profane swearing with both.  Let a man be guilty of one of these sins, and you have no security that he will not commit any sin to which he may be tempted.

title: Leviticus 19:13
text: Refusing promptly to pay just wages for labor, and robbing men by fraud or violence of their dues, are sins which God abhors, and against which he denounces his dreadful curse.   James 5:2-5

title: Leviticus 19:14
text: To reproach or despise men, or to bring any evil upon them, on account of any natural infirmity or calamity, is mean, ungrateful, and wicked.

title: Leviticus 19:15
text:
In judgment; in deciding cases of right between man and man. 
 
Partiality in judicial decisions, and injustice under the cover of law, are an abomination in the sight of Jehovah, and expose those who are guilty of them to his vengeance.

title: Leviticus 19:16
text:
Stand against the blood; take a course suited to procure the death of the innocent.   I Samuel 22:9 I Samuel 22:18 I Kings 21:13 Mark 14:57  
 
Tattlers, those who go about retailing scandal, and delight in accusing, ridiculing, or depreciating others, especially the good, are following Satan the great accuser, and in a way which leads to his place of torment.

title: Leviticus 19:17
text:
Hate thy brother in thy heart--rebuke thy neighbor; instead of cherishing a secret grudge against our neighbor, it is our duty frankly to reprove him, wherein we think he has done wrong. 
 
  Not suffer sin upon him; better, not bear sin on his account, that is, by neglecting our duty towards him.

title: Leviticus 19:18
text: Real love, such as God requires and holiness of heart produces, leads men to desire and strive to deliver others from all evil, especially from sin, and to do them all the good in their power.  Let this love fill all hearts, and it will make earth resemble heaven.

title: Leviticus 19:20
text:
She shall be scourged; literally, there shall be scourging--as is supposed, of the man, as well as the woman. 
 
  Not be put to death;  Deuteronomy 22:23-27:1

title: Leviticus 19:22
text: Without repentance and faith in the atoning blood of Christ, none to whom he is made known can be forgiven, or escape the just punishment of their sins.

title: Leviticus 19:23
text: As uncircumcised; that is, unclean and not suitable to be eaten by them.   Leviticus 19:24

title: Leviticus 19:25
text: Jehovah is the God of providence as well as of grace; the giver of all temporal as well as spiritual blessings, which should be received as from him, and used for his glory and the good of his kingdom.

title: Leviticus 19:26
text: Observe times; or, practice magic arts.  See note to  Leviticus 19:31 .

title: Leviticus 19:27
text: Round--mar the corners; according to the superstitious observances of the heathen.

title: Leviticus 19:28
text:
Cutting in your flesh; in mourning for the dead. 
 
There are means of sin, as well as of holiness.  Among them are all pretended conversations with evil or departed spirits, sorcery, enchantments, jugglery, fortune-telling, and every thing which tends to lead men away from God as their portion, from his word as their guide, from his service as their employment, and his favor as their reward. All such things should be avoided, and only such occupy the attention of men as tend to make them holy, and lead them to love, trust in, and obey God.

title: Leviticus 19:30
text: Stated, regular, conscientious attendance on public worship, when God gives opportunity, is an essential part of the right keeping of the Sabbath; and highly promotive of all the social, civil, and religious interests of men.

title: Leviticus 19:31
text:
Them that have familiar spirits; those who profess to have conversation with demons or the spirits of the dead, and by their aid to foretell future events and do other supernatural things. 
 
  Wizards; who profess to have supernatural power by the aid of magic arts.  Sorcery and witchcraft existed among the ancients in a great variety of forms.  Those who practiced them are called in the holy Scriptures, wizards, diviners, enchanters, sooth-sayers, etc.  Of these, some professed simply to interpret signs and omens, and thus to draw from them a knowledge of the future; others, by means of certain mysterious words and forms, to call up demons or the spirits of the dead, that they might obtain from them supernatural revelations, or accomplish through their aid supernatural deeds.  All such practices are essentially idolatrous, as they withdraw men's faith and love from God and his word to things that cannot profit them. 
 
Those who pretend to wisdom they do not possess, especially to receiving it from disembodied spirits, or conversation with invisible agents, and thus to be able to reveal secrets and foretell future events, are morally defiled and defiling, and should be treated accordingly.

title: Leviticus 19:32
text: Respect to the aged is a mark of wisdom, and essential to virtue; a source of comfort, and a means of usefulness; an ornament to character, and a passport to influence, reputation, and honor.

title: Leviticus 19:34
text: Kindness to strangers is a dictate of true religion, and peculiarly grateful to persons in a strange country.  It so much resembles the kindness of God, that it is one of the best means of leading men to love him, and thus show their gratitude to him for his love.  Ephesians 2:19

title: Leviticus 19:35
text:
Meteyard; measure of lengths. 
 
  Measure; of liquids.

title: Leviticus 19:36
text:
Ephah--him; names of different measures.  Leviticus 5:11 Exodus 16:36 Exodus 29:40  
 
Strict honesty in trading, and in all business transactions, and the doing to others as we ought to wish others to do to us, is a duty required by God, by our own good, and the good of all.

title: Leviticus 20:2
text:
Molech; an idol of the Ammonites to whom children were sacrificed. According to the Rabbins his statue was of brass and hollow; and this being heated from below, the children to be sacrificed were put into its arms. 
 
Capital punishment by the hand of magistrates is sometimes not only right, but a duty which they owe to God and their fellow-men.  It is a needful means of restraining iniquity; and the people, when God commands it, are bound to see that it is executed.

title: Leviticus 20:5
text: If the magistrates and people neglect to prosecute criminals, and to punish the guilty, they encourage crime, incur guilt, and expose themselves to divine judgments.

title: Leviticus 20:8
text: Sanctify you; separate them from other nations, and set them apart for himself.   Leviticus 20:24 Leviticus 20:26

title: Leviticus 20:9
text: That laws should be needful to keep parents from destroying children, and children from cursing parents; and people to whom Jehovah is known from forsaking him for idols, and committing the most polluting and degrading abominations, shows the strength and malignancy of sin, and the necessity, in order to salvation,of being delivered from it by the mighty power of God.   I Corinthians 6:9-11 Ephesians 1:19-20

title: Leviticus 20:23
text: Cast out; shall cast out.

title: Leviticus 21:1
text: Priests--defiled for the dead; by touching dead bodies, going where they were, or assisting in burying them, except in the case of near relatives, mentioned in  Leviticus 21:2-3 ; and the high-priest might not do it even for them.   Leviticus 21:10-12

title: Leviticus 21:5
text: Not make baldness; in token of mourning.

title: Leviticus 21:6
text: Ministers of religion should be distinguished for sobriety, purity, and elevation of character, and for the faithful discharge of their appropriate duties; that to their instructions they may add the weight of their example.

title: Leviticus 21:13
text: Ministers of religion, even those most distinguished, should in all ordinary cases be examples of purity, propriety, and excellence.

title: Leviticus 21:15
text: Profane his seed; render his sons unfit for the priesthood, by disregarding these divine directions.

title: Leviticus 21:17
text: Hath any blemish; the priest, as well as the victims he offered, must be without blemish, to typify the moral perfection which God's service demands; and especially, to shadow forth the perfect priesthood of Christ.

title: Leviticus 21:22
text: He shall eat the bread of his God; though the blemishes mentioned disqualified them from offering sacrifices, they did not exclude them from performing such duties as were suited to their condition, and receiving a support.

title: Leviticus 21:23
text: All should avoid engaging in duties for which they are disqualified, and be diligent in the discharge of such as are suited to their condition, and by which they may honor God, and benefit themselves and their fellow-men.

title: Leviticus 22:2
text: Separate themselves from the holy things; abstain from partaking of them when they were ceremonially unclean, and could not partake without defiling them.   Leviticus 22:3-7

title: Leviticus 22:3
text:
Hallow; consecrate. 
 
Known and allowed iniquity, secret or open, unfits a man for the acceptable discharge of sacred duties; and without repentance and reformation he will be excluded from the holy society and worship of heaven.

title: Leviticus 22:7
text: Eat of the holy things; that part of them which belonged to the priests.

title: Leviticus 22:9
text: Neglect of the ordinances of God, or a profane attendance on them, exposes men to punishment for their iniquity.

title: Leviticus 22:11
text: He shall eat of it; because he belonged to the family, and was entitled to its privileges.

title: Leviticus 22:13
text: Those who minister in holy things have a right to support, not only for themselves, but for their families.

title: Leviticus 22:14
text:
Unwittingly; not knowing that it was holy, or consecrated to God. 
 
  The fifth--give it unto the priest; he should pay for what he ate and one fifth part more.  This was designed to make them careful not to offend ignorantly.

title: Leviticus 22:16
text:
Or suffer them to bear the iniquity; more literally, lade them with the iniquity of trespass, namely, by eating of their offerings in an unlawful way.  For the priests acted in behalf of the people, and their sins would bring God's displeasure upon the congregation of Israel. 
 
Ministers of religion should labor to enlighten the people as to the will of God, that they may not sin ignorantly; and if they have so sinned, should use all suitable means to reclaim them, and bring them in future to know and obey the truth.

title: Leviticus 22:19
text: At your own will; rather, for your acceptance; and so  Leviticus 22:29 . The expressions, for acceptance, for your acceptance, it shall be accepted, etc., are often added to signify that the offerer is to comply with the rules of the Levitical law.  So in  Leviticus 22:19-21 Leviticus 22:23 Leviticus 22:25 Leviticus 22:27 Leviticus 22:29 , in the Hebrew.

title: Leviticus 22:21
text: God justly requires that which is perfect; and the best that we offer can be accepted only through the atonement, righteousness, and intercession of Christ.

title: Leviticus 22:27
text: Under the dam; with its mother.

title: Leviticus 22:31
text: Notwithstanding all that Christ has done, no one is or can be saved by him, unless as he is made willing heartily to obey God's commands.

title: Leviticus 22:32
text:
Profane my holy name; by disregarding his directions. 
 
  Hallowed; reverenced, honored, obeyed.

title: Leviticus 23:2
text: Holy convocations; assemblies for religious purposes.

title: Leviticus 23:3
text: No other seasons or occasions of public worship are ever to set aside, supersede, or lead nay to neglect the habitual and holy observance of the weekly Sabbath.

title: Leviticus 23:5
text:
First month; Abib or Nisan, the first month of the ecclesiastical and the seventh of the civil year; answering to the last part of March and the first part of April. 
 
  The Lord's passover;  Exodus 12:3-17:1 
 
The reasons why believers in Christ are passed over or spared, and made partakers of the riches of grace, should ever be remembered, and the love which procured their salvation be celebrated according to his command, with gratitude and joy.   Luke 22:19 I Corinthians 5:7 I Corinthians 11:24

title: Leviticus 23:10
text: Shall bring a sheaf of the first-fruits; this sheaf, as well as the accompanying offerings,  Leviticus 23:12-13 , was presented to the Lord by the priest in the name of the whole congregation.  It is thought to have been a sheaf of barley, which begun to be ready for the harvest at the passover.

title: Leviticus 23:11
text:
Wave the sheaf; as a sign of consecreation to the Lord. 
 
  On the morrow after the sabbath; the Jews understood the Sabbath here to mean not the weekly Sabbath, but the first day of unleavened bread, which was kept as a Sabbath,  Leviticus 23:7 .  As this fell on the fifteenth of the month Abib, the sheaf was presented on the sixteenth.

title: Leviticus 23:14
text:
Bread--parched corn--green ears; that is, of the new crop. 
 
The blessings of providence, as well as of grace, are from the Lord. They should all be acknolwedged as his gifts, and used to his glory.

title: Leviticus 23:15
text:
From the morrow after the sabbath; see note to  Leviticus 23:16 . 
 
  Seven sabbaths; seven weeks or forty-nine days.  These with the preceding day, the first day of unleavened bread, made fifty days. Hence this was called the feast of Pentecost, a Greek word meaning, The fifieth.  It was a feast of thanksgiving at the close of the harvest, which began about the time of the passover.  It also coincided with the giving of the law on Sinai, and was afterwards made memorable by the gift of the Holy Spirit.   Acts 2:1

title: Leviticus 23:16
text: A new meat-offering; made of the new flour.

title: Leviticus 23:17
text: Bring out of your habitations; the people seem to have generally brought on this occasion, offerings of flour made from the new corn. From a portion of these, two loaves were made and offered by the priest, with the accompanying sacrifices and oblations,  Leviticus 16:29 , in the name of the whole congregation.

title: Leviticus 23:21
text: After gathering in the fruits of the earth, a day of annual thanksgiving, appropriately observed by all the people in commemoration of the goodness of God, is suited to honor him and benefit them.

title: Leviticus 23:24
text: The seventh month; Tishri.   Leviticus 16:29

title: Leviticus 23:27
text: Afflict your souls; by fasting and confession of sin.

title: Leviticus 23:31
text:
A statute; a law that the tenth day of Tishri should be observed as a sabbath, or day of atonement, of rest, and of religious worship.  It was a day of annual fasting, humiliation, and prayer. 
 
A day annually, of humiliation, fasting, and prayer, when labor and amusements are suspended, and the people unite in confessing and forsaking their sins and imploring divine mercy, is highly proper, and has often been blessed.

title: Leviticus 23:34
text: Feast of tabernacles; in commemoration of their having dwelt in tabernacles during forty years in the wilderness.

title: Leviticus 23:40
text: Deliverances from great evils, as well as the reception of great favors, call for peculiar gratitude to God, and should be celebrated with special thanksgiving.

title: Leviticus 23:42
text: Booths; temporary dwellings, made of boughs or other slight materials.

title: Leviticus 24:4
text: Ministers of religion should constantly endeavor, from the word, the Spirit, and the providences of God, to enlighten the minds of men as to their duty, and set before them the motives to obedience which God has revealed.

title: Leviticus 24:5
text: Two tenth-deals; two omers, or tenths of an ephah; between six and seven quarts.   Exodus 16:36

title: Leviticus 24:8
text: Every sabbath; the bread was taken away and eaten by the priests, and the frankincense was burnt as an offering by fire to the Lord; and new bread and frankincense were put in their place.

title: Leviticus 24:12
text: Ward; prison, or safe custody.

title: Leviticus 24:16
text: Blasphemy against God is great and aggravated wickedness; and under the Jewish dispensation, was, as treason, punished with death.

title: Leviticus 24:17
text: Killeth; murdereth.

title: Leviticus 24:20
text: Breach for breach; this was a law for the magistrate in punishing crimes, not for private persons.  It was in accordance with the general usage of those times, and applied only to malicious injuries.

title: Leviticus 24:23
text: The execution, at the command of God, of notorious criminals, is a solemn duty, the performance of which is suited to give timely warning to the wicked and exercise upon them salutary restraint.  By commanding that some should thus be put to death in this world, God gives indications of the terrible punishment which awaits the perseveringly wicked in the world to come.  Hence a reason why some who deny punishment in the future world, are opposed to capital punishment in this: because one fore-shadows the other.

title: Leviticus 25:5
text: Not reap, neither gather; as in other years, but share what grew with others as they might need, and with the beast of the field.

title: Leviticus 25:6
text:
The sabbath of the land; the spontaneous produce of the sabbatical year. 
 
God requires that we should in all things feel our constant dependence on him; and he so orders things in his providence as to supply the wants of those who trust in and obey him.

title: Leviticus 25:9
text: The day of atonement;  Leviticus 23:27-32

title: Leviticus 25:10
text: Hallow; keep sacred as a season of rejoicing.

title: Leviticus 25:16
text: According to the multitude--and--the fewness; the price of what they sold was to be regulated according to the distance of time from the year of jubilee, when it would revert ot its former owner.  Leviticus 25:10 Leviticus 25:23

title: Leviticus 25:17
text: God is the friend of justice and mercy, and the eternal enemy of covetousness and oppression.  None can obtain his favor without doing justly, loving mercy, and walking humbly with him.   Micah 6:8

title: Leviticus 25:21
text: For three years; these words refer not to the year of jubilee, but to the regular sabbatical year.  This must have begun, not in the spring, when the crops were yet standing, but in the fall, after the fruits of the year had been gathered in.  The day for its commencement seems to have been the tenth of the seventh month, Tishri, when the jubilee plainly began,  Leviticus 25:9 .  But Moses here computes the years from the first month Abib,  Exodus 12:2 .  The crop, then, sown on the sixth year, which is the one that God promises shall serve for three years, would be reaped at the beginning of the seventh year.  The sabbatical year beginning in the fall of the same year, there would be no sowing, and consequently no harvest at the beginning of the next, the eighth year.  But in the fall of the eighth year, after the sabbatical year was closed, they would sow, and gather the harvest at the beginning of the ninth year, using the corn sown on the sixth year till this work was accomplished.  For the year of jubilee no special directions are given.  As it occurred but once in fifty years, special provision could be easily made for it as it approached.

title: Leviticus 25:22
text: For individuals and for nations, obedience to God is the sure means of competence and safety.

title: Leviticus 25:23
text: Not be sold for ever; so as to be alienated from its original owner for ever.  It must return to him at the year of jubilee; for it belongs to Jehovah, and he will not allow any one to take perpetual occupation of it.

title: Leviticus 25:27
text: Count the years; from the time he sold it to that date, and also to the year of jubilee, and give accordingly.  If he sold it twenty years before the year of jubilee, and ten of them had expired, he would, for the redemption, give half as much as he had sold it for; if but five years had passed, he would give three quarters; and so in proportion for any length of time.   Leviticus 25:50-55

title: Leviticus 25:35
text: Relieve him; by taking no interest, or increase, for what was needful for the poor man's support.   Leviticus 25:36-37

title: Leviticus 25:37
text: God has special regard for the poor, sympathizes with them in distress, and requires that such as have the means, and know their condition, should relieve their wants.

title: Leviticus 25:39
text: Sold unto thee; becomes obligated to yield service.   Leviticus 25:42

title: Leviticus 25:53
text: Jehovah is a God of kindness and compassion.  These traits of character he requires in all his people; and without them none can meet his approbation or enjoy the blessings of his everlasting favor.

title: Leviticus 26:1
text: In this chapter and the twenty-eighth of Deuteronomy, is recorded a most wonderful prophecy of the future history of God's covenant people, the fulfilment of which through so many centuries is an irrefragable proof of the divine inspiration of the record that contains it.

title: Leviticus 26:2
text: One of the most effectual means of preservation from idolatry, and all sins, secret and open, personal and national, is the due observance of the Sabbath, with habitual attendance on public worship.

title: Leviticus 26:8
text: Five--a hundred--ten thousand; definite numbers are here used for indefinite.

title: Leviticus 26:10
text: Bring forth the old; from their granaries, to make room for the new crop.

title: Leviticus 26:11
text: Set my tabernacle; continue to dwell among them with his visible presence on the mercy-seat, and to do them good.

title: Leviticus 26:12
text: Obedience to divine commands is not only the surest, but the only way to personal and national excellence, and permanent prosperity, happiness, and glory.

title: Leviticus 26:13
text:
Made you go upright; delivered you from bowing down under oppression or in despondency. 
 
God speaks of deliverance from bondage as a blessing which lays those who receive it under peculiar obligations to love and obey him.

title: Leviticus 26:16
text: Appoint over you; as the executioners of my wrath.

title: Leviticus 26:18
text: Seven times; the number seven is a symbol of completeness.  Out of the inexhaustible storehouse of his omnipotence, God will continually bring upon them new plagues in full measure.

title: Leviticus 26:19
text: As iron, and--as brass; the clouds would give no rain, any more than if they were iron, and the earth no fruit, any more than if it were brass.   Leviticus 26:20

title: Leviticus 26:22
text: Your highways shall be desolate; men would not travel in them, on account of the danger.   Judges 5:6 II Chronicles 15:5 Isaiah 33:8

title: Leviticus 26:24
text: The reason why God sets himself against individuals or nations, or ever punishes them, is because they oppose him, and act in opposition to what he directs, and what their good and the great interests of his kingdom require.

title: Leviticus 26:25
text: Avenge the quarrel of my covenant; in the Hebrew, avenge the avenging of my covenant, that is, execute vengeance upon you for breaking it.

title: Leviticus 26:26
text:
Ten women--bake--in one oven; on account of the small quantity they would have to bake. 
 
  By weight; each man shall have a small portion weighed out to him, as is the custom in extreme want.

title: Leviticus 26:29
text:
Eat the flesh of your sons, and--daughters; on account of the scarcity of food.  2Ki 6.29; La 4.10 
 
The dreadful evils which sin often occasions in this world, are indications of evils still more dreadful which it will occasion in the world to come; but neither in this nor the future world will any sinners suffer more or greater evils than their iniquities deserve.

title: Leviticus 26:35
text:
It shall rest, because it did not rest; in four hundred and ninety years, the time from the reign of Saul to the Babylonish captivity, there would be seventy years of sabbaths, and also seventy sabbatical years--equal to the number of years the land lay desolate during their captivity in Babylon; and, as some have supposed, equal to the number of sabbatical years the observance of which they had neglected.  II Chronicles 36:21 Jeremiah 25:8-11  
 
The desecration of Sabbaths, or the neglect to observe them according to divine appointment, is highly offensive to God and injurious to men. It is treasuring up wrath against the day of wrath, and exposes both individuals and nations to desolating judgments.

title: Leviticus 26:38
text: Eat you up; consume them: many would die in their enemies' country.

title: Leviticus 26:39
text: Children often suffer greatly in consequence of the sins of their parents; but not more than their own sins deserve, nor more than, if they repent of and forsake them, will be overruled for their good.

title: Leviticus 26:41
text: Accept of the punishment; feel and acknowledge that God was just in punishing them, and humbly submit themselves to his disposal.

title: Leviticus 26:42
text:
Remember my covenant; granting them the blessings promised in it. 
 
  Remember the land; cause it again to be inhabited by the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

title: Leviticus 26:45
text: A deep conviction and hearty confession of the righteousness of God in all the evils he brings upon us, humble submission to his will, and true devotion to his service, will end in deliverance from all evil, and the everlasting enjoyment of all needed good.

title: Leviticus 27:2
text:
Make a singular vow; in the Hebrew, set apart a vow; that is, set apart one's self or any thing belonging to him by a vow, as given to the Lord.
