Men might thus devote themselves to Jehovah, or their children, as Hannah did Samuel,  I Samuel 1:28 , or a portion of their property.  By a wise regulation they had the right of redeeming themselves, or the person or thing vowed, at a certain estimation, as given in this chapter. 
 
  The persons--for the Lord by thy estimation; the persons thus devoted shall belong to the Lord, to be redeemed at the estimation ordered by Moses in God's name. 
 
It is good to be ready and zealous in good things, but wisdom and discretion are also needful.  Persons sometimes devote themselves or others to services for which they are not wanted, or are unfit.  In such cases it is better for them to aid the cause of Christ in some other way.  Their money may be more useful than their personal service, or their services more useful in some other employment than that to which they aspire.

title: Leviticus 27:9
text: Shall be holy; it could not be reclaimed, but must continue devoted to the object to which it was consecrated, provided it was a thing suitable to be offered in sacrifice to God.  If not, then he must pay the value of it, according to the estimation of the priest, and one fifth part more.   Leviticus 27:13-15 Leviticus 27:19 Leviticus 27:27

title: Leviticus 27:10
text: Rash promises, and inconstancy in performing such as are right, should be carefully avoided.

title: Leviticus 27:14
text: Sanctify; set apart, to be devoted to the service of the sanctuary.

title: Leviticus 27:16
text:
According to the seed; the seed that it would take to sow the field, or which the field would produce. 
 
  A homer; ten ephahs, or a little less than eleven bushels.

title: Leviticus 27:19
text: All our possessions belong to the Lord, and should be used in such a manner as will please him; some part of them should be devoted especially to the support and extension of his worship.  The proportion which should be thus devoted is not now definitively prescribed, and the manner in which persons feel, judge, and act in the use of property, is one of the prominent indications and evidences of their character, and one which will have a momentous influence on their future condition.   Matthew 25:35-46

title: Leviticus 27:25
text:
Twenty gerahs; a gerah was about two and a half cents. 
 
Strict integrity towards God and men is a duty, the desire and conscientious endeavor to practise which, is essential, in the sight of God, to the character of an honest man.

title: Leviticus 27:26
text: It is the Lord's;  Exodus 13:2 Exodus 13:12-15:1

title: Leviticus 27:28
text: Devoted thing; a thing irrevocably devoted by the offerer to God, which could not be redeemed, but must be applied to the object to which it was devoted.  In this respect it differed from the things previously mentioned, and is expressed in the original by a different word.

title: Leviticus 27:29
text: Devoted of men; it is not to be understood that a private person could thus devote to destruction a member of his family.  The cases mentioned in Scripture are such as that recorded in  Numbers 21:2-3 , where the Israelites devoted to destruction a Canaanitish people that had made war upon them; or where God himself ordered such a devotion to be made, as in the case of Jericho and all its possessions. Jos 6.17-19

title: Leviticus 27:31
text: Tithes; a tenth part of the products of the land, after the first-fruits had been deducted.  This the Israelites were bound to give for the support of the ministers of religion.  Leviticus 27:30-33 Numbers 18:21-32   Another tenth of what remained was to be brought to Jerusalem and used for offerings and for the support of the worshippers while there.   Deuteronomy 12:5-7 Deuteronomy 14:22-29

title: Leviticus 27:32
text: The rod; which had some coloring matter on the end, by which one tenth part was marked as a tithe to be devoted to the Lord.

title: Leviticus 27:33
text: An honest man will not retain, or appropriate to his own use, what he knows of right belongs to another, in opposition to the known will of the owner, whether human or divine; but his will be disposed to render to all what rightfully belongs to them.  It is a great thing to be truly honest.   Micah 6:8 Matthew 22:21 Luke 16:10-13

title: Numbers 1:1
text: The second month; called Zif; answering to the last part of April and the first part of May.

title: Numbers 1:2
text: Take ye the sum of all the congregation; the Hebrew civil division was into thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens,  Exodus 18:25 Deuteronomy 1:15  and this served also as the basis of the military division, 1Sa 8.12; 22.7.  The present numbering was an enrolment of the men of war in regular military array.  A numbering had been made of the people a few months before.   Exodus 30:11-12 Exodus 38:25 Exodus 38:26 .  The tables prepared on that occasion seem to have served for the present enrolment, the men appointed to oversee it simply filling up the vacancies occasioned by death from those who had in the meanwhile reached the age of twenty years.  Hence the sum is in both cases the same, namely, six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty. It is to be noticed further,that with the single exception of the tribe of Gad,  Numbers 1:25 , no divisions lower than hundreds are reckoned.

title: Numbers 1:16
text: Renowned of the congregation; rather, "the called of the congregation;" that is, men of standing and influence, who were regularly called to the assemblies of the people; for these assemblies consisted not of the whole mass of the people, but of certain representatives from each family.

title: Numbers 1:18
text: Their pedigrees; the line of their forefathers.

title: Numbers 1:20
text:
vv 20-25. 
 
  Reuben--Simeon--Gad; the tribes are grouped in three, according to their encampment, as described in the following chapters, these three tribes having their place on the south side of the tabernacle.

title: Numbers 1:45
text:
vv 45-46. 
 
  All that were able to go forth to war in Israel--were six hundred thousand; the number able for war shows that the whole people must have amounted to more than two millions.

title: Numbers 1:46
text: From the great increase of the Israelites in their bondage, and from their deliverance according to the divine prediction, we have evidence of the faithfulness of God, and are encouraged to trust in him for the fulfillment of all his promises.

title: Numbers 1:53
text: Keep the charge of the tabernacle of testimony; guard the tabernacle from the approach of all improper persons, and thus keep them from the punishment threatened in  Numbers 1:51 .

title: Numbers 2:2
text:
Standard--ensign; the standard was that belonging to each grand division, embracing three tribes: the ensigns are generally understood to have been those of single tribes, perhaps also of the subdivisions of these tribes. 
 
The Lord appoints the habitation and circumstances of all as seems good in his sight.  If these are favorable, we should be grateful; if trying, submissive; and in all things seek to honor him.

title: Numbers 2:9
text: The camp of Judah; a division of the main host, consisting of three tribes, of which Judah was the head.

title: Numbers 2:16
text: The camp of Reuben; the division of which this tribe was the head.

title: Numbers 2:24
text: Of Ephraim; of which Ephraim was the head.

title: Numbers 2:31
text: The camp of Dan; this made four divisions into which the tribes were divided, and they were arranged in the order above mentioned.

title: Numbers 2:33
text: Not numbered; not numbered as men of war, from which they were exempted by their office.

title: Numbers 2:34
text: Jehovah is a God of order, requiring each one to take and to keep his proper place, by the faithful discharge of duty.  Thus he will not only most honor God, but be most happy himself and most useful to others.

title: Numbers 3:4
text: In the sight of Aaron; under his direction.

title: Numbers 3:6
text: Minister unto him; wait upon and assist him in the service of the sanctuary.   Numbers 3:7-9

title: Numbers 3:7
text:
And they shall keep his charge; shall perform, under his direction, the services entrusted to their care. 
 
  The charge of the whole congregation; the services of the sanctuary which belonged to the whole congregation, being performed by the Levites in their behalf.

title: Numbers 3:10
text: The stranger; not of the seed of Aaron, and not appointed by God to the priest's office.

title: Numbers 3:12
text:
Be mine; consecrated to the service of the sanctuary. 
 
The ministers of religion should be in a peculiar sense devoted to God; not entangling themselves with the affairs of this life, but employing their time and talents in the discharge of the appropriate duties of their office.

title: Numbers 3:13
text: Hallowed unto me; set apart for his particular service.  Exodus 12:29-30 Exodus 13:11-15

title: Numbers 3:25
text: The charge of the sons of Gershon; the things committed to their particular case.

title: Numbers 3:31
text: The hanging; the veil that hung immediately before the ark, and separated the inner from the outer sanctuary.  Exodus 26:31-33

title: Numbers 3:38
text: The Lord appoints to all their places and their work; and as it is his will that there should be division of labor, each one should strive to fill the place assigned him, and faithfully perform the duties to which he is called.

title: Numbers 3:39
text: Twenty and two thousand; the sum of the Gershonites, Kohathites, and Merarites, as separately given in  Numbers 3:22 Numbers 3:28 Numbers 3:34 , amounts to twenty-two thousand three hundred.  It is supposed that from these Moses deducted the first-born, amounting to three hundred, who, as already devoted to God, could not be taken in exchange for an equal number of first-born from the other tribes.

title: Numbers 3:43
text: All the first-born males; that is, since the destruction of the first-born in Egypt; as the smallness of the number, in comparison with the sum of the whole congregation, shows.  It was from that event that the first-born were to be reckoned as devoted to God.

title: Numbers 3:47
text: Five shekels; about two dollars and a half.

title: Numbers 3:51
text: Different persons are called to promote the cause of God in different ways; some by their personal services, others by their property, and all by their prayers, their influence, and their example.  If from love to him they employ what he gives them in his service, they will all be accepted in Christ, and receive an abundant reward.

title: Numbers 4:3
text:
From thirty years old and upward; in  Numbers 8:24  it is said, "From twenty and five years old and upward they shall go in to wait upon the service of the tabernacle of the congregation."  But this seems to have been an introductory admission to a sort of apprenticeship, while the full service was reserved for the age between thirty and fifty. 
 
Maturity of body and mind, and thorough preparation, are needful to the proper discharge of the duties of the ministry; and none unprepared or uncalled should assume the responsibilities of the sacred office.  I Timothy 3:6

title: Numbers 4:4
text: About the most holy things; rather, even the most holy things; that is, the charge and bearing of them; for these were committed to their care.

title: Numbers 4:5
text:
The covering veil; between the Holy and Most Holy places.  See note to  Numbers 3:31 . 
 
  Cover the ark; the covering of the ark, with other things committed to their care, was designed to hide them from the eyes of the people. Thus was signified their sacredness as devoted to God's immediate service, and reverence was fostered in the hearts of the Israelites.

title: Numbers 4:7
text: Covers to cover withal; or, vessels for libation.

title: Numbers 4:15
text:
The burden of the sons of Kohath; the things connected with the tabernacle, which they were to carry.   Numbers 3:31  
 
Sacred things should be treated with reverence, and we should not attempt to reveal or discover what God designed to conceal.

title: Numbers 4:16
text: The daily meat-offering; see  Exodus 29:1

title: Numbers 4:18
text: Cut ye not off--the Kohathites; by suffering them to see the holy things which they were to carry, and thus incur the penalty of death.  Numbers 4:20

title: Numbers 4:19
text: We should use all suitable means to prevent others from committing sin, lest, by our neglect, we become the occasion of their ruin.

title: Numbers 4:32
text: By name ye shall reckon the instruments--of their burden; keep an exact inventory of them.  This was especially necessary in respect to the pins, cords, and sockets, which were very numerous, and needed to be carefully counted upon each removal.

title: Numbers 4:47
text:
Service of the ministry; all the other labor belonging to the charge of the Merarites distinct from that of bearing the burdens.  As their service included the heaviest articles, four wagons were assigned to them, while the Gershonites had but two.   Numbers 7:7-8  
 
While men should not enter the ministry too young, they should also not continue to sustain its responsibilities, and attempt to discharge its duties, when they are too old; but the Scriptures do not fix the age at which the public ministry now should cease.  Different duties are suited to different periods of life, and wisdom from above is needful in order to judge rightly as to what are appropriate duties, and also as to the time and manner of performing them.

title: Numbers 5:3
text: As Jehovah is holy, and requires men to be holy, all causes of mental and moral defilement, and especially whatever tends to increase and extend it, should be carefully avoided.

title: Numbers 5:6
text: A trespass against the Lord; by defrauding his fellowmen.

title: Numbers 5:7
text: Unjustly to obtain or keep possession of another's property, is a sin which God abhors.  No professed repentance, which does not lead a man who is conscious of this sin to forsake it, and, if in his power, make restitution, will deliver him from divine wrath.

title: Numbers 5:8
text: If the man have no kinsman; if the injured man were dead, and he had no relative to receive restitution, then it was to be made to the Lord by being given to the priest.   Numbers 5:9-10

title: Numbers 5:10
text:
Shall be his; shall be at the disposal of the offerer to give to the priest who presents his offering. 
 
  It shall be his; shall be the priest's.

title: Numbers 5:13
text: Adulterers and adulteresses are highly criminal, and exposed to the vengeance of God.  Though their crime may be known only to him and themselves, he will reveal it--if not in this world, in the world to come--and will visit them with his terrible indignation.

title: Numbers 5:15
text:
Barley-meal--no oil--nor put frankincense; the coarseness of the material and the absence of oil and frankincense well represent the design of the offering, which is not to give thanks for past mercies nor obtain future blessings; but to bring upon the woman, if guilty, a dreadful curse. 
 
  Bringing iniquity to remembrance; that is, before the Lord, by appealing to him to punish the woman if guilty.

title: Numbers 5:16
text: Near; near to the holy place, where the Lord dwelt upon the mercy- seat.

title: Numbers 5:17
text: Holy water; water from the laver in the tabernacle; called holy because devoted to a sacred or religious use.   Exodus 30:18

title: Numbers 5:18
text: The bitter water; so called from its effects.

title: Numbers 5:21
text:
Charge the woman with an oath of cursing; lay upon her an oath which brings with it an awful curse if she swear falsely. 
 
  A curse and an oath; an accursed person by whom men shall swear, saying, The Lord make thee like that woman.  Compare  Jeremiah 29:22 .

title: Numbers 5:22
text: Amen; be it so.

title: Numbers 5:23
text:
In a book; on parchment, or on something from which it could be washed off. 
 
  Shall blot them out with the bitter water; the original Hebrew implies that he does this by dipping the writing into the water, and thus symbolically infusing the curse into it, that she may drink it down with the water.  Compare  Psalms 109:18 .

title: Numbers 5:27
text: The diseases which the licentious often suffer, and with which they infect and torment each other, are a manifestation of divine wrath against their sin, and a warning that, unless they repent and become pure and holy, the curses of God will sonner or later overwhelm them.

title: Numbers 5:28
text: She shall be free; from all harm.

title: Numbers 5:31
text: Satan tries hard to promote domestic jealousy, because it tends to destroy family peace, religion, and usefulness; all should therefore avoid occasions of producing it, and withstand all temptations to indulge it.  If any are unjustly suspected, they should in calmness, patience, and well-doing, commit themselves to the disposal of God, and in due time he will remove suspicions, or overrule them for the advancement of his glory and the good of his kingdom.

title: Numbers 6:2
text: A Nazarite; the Nazarite was one specially consecrated to God by his parents or himself, and that either for life or for a limited term. See note to  Leviticus 27:2 .  In this chapter the case of those only whose Nazariteship continued for a limited time is considered.

title: Numbers 6:4
text: Eat nothing that is made of the vine-tree; this was a symbol of sobriety, and of abstinence from all the intoxicating pleasures of sin.

title: Numbers 6:7
text: He shall not make himself unclean; by approaching the dead body. The Jews add that he was required to abstain from the customary signs of mourning, as in the case of the high-priest.  This and all the other regulations were designed to impress upon his mind the sacredness of his peculiar relation to God, and the deadness to worldly joys and sorrows demanded by it.

title: Numbers 6:8
text: Holiness to the Lord is the badge of his people, and should ever be their peculiar characteristic.  They should abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul, moderate their desires for earthly things, place their affections on things above, and regulate all their acts by the will of God.

title: Numbers 6:12
text: Days--shall be lost; they would not be counted as a part of the time of his Nazariteship, but he must begin again.

title: Numbers 6:14
text: His offering; these offerings were an acknowledgment that in his best services he needed the efficacy of atoning blood and of the purifying Spirit, and also tokens of gratitude for the goodness of God.

title: Numbers 6:15
text: Meat-offering--drink-offerings; those accompanying the sacrifices mentioned in the preceding verse.  See  Numbers 15:3-10

title: Numbers 6:19
text: Sodden shoulder; the boiled shoulder, which was the left shoulder, the right with the wave-breast having been given to the priest by a general law.   Leviticus 7:32-33

title: Numbers 6:20
text: We are always exposed in this world to moral defilement, and in our best services need the application of the blood of Christ and the purifying influences of his Spirit, in order that our offerings may be acceptable in his sight.

title: Numbers 6:21
text: That his hand shall get; such freewill-offerings as he shall be able to make.

title: Numbers 6:24
text:
vv 24-26. 
 
This three fold divine benediction is supposed by many interpreters to contain an intimation of the Trinity in the godhead.

title: Numbers 6:27
text:
Put my name; call Israel by my name, and teach them to obey me as my peculiar people. 
 
The blessing of Jehovah, in the love of the Father, the grace of the Son, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, bestowed upon his believing, obedient people, will make them all for ever truly and perfectly blessed.

title: Numbers 7:2
text:
The princes of Israel;  Numbers 1:16 . 
 
Those who are truly devoted to God, and thankful for his mercies, will not be satisfied with doing merely what is specifically commanded, but will make voluntary offerings of time, talents, and property, from love to him and his cause, and to promote his glory and the good of their fellow-men.

title: Numbers 7:3
text: Their offering; these were voluntary offerings in addition to those which were commanded.

title: Numbers 7:5
text: None need be discouraged when called to great and laborious services; God will provide for them, that as their duties are, their strength and all needful mercies may be.

title: Numbers 7:9
text: Bear upon their shoulders; the ark and the sacred things which they were to carry.   Numbers 3:31

title: Numbers 7:11
text:
Each prince on his day; by this orderly arrangement increased solemnity was given to the transaction, and the great truth that God notices and rewards the gifts of his servants individually was taught in a very forcible way. 
 
Jehovah would have all things, especially with regard to his worship, conducted with propriety, and in such a way that the personal responsibility of each worshipper shall be made manifest, and thus the greatest blessing upon the whole be secured.

title: Numbers 7:13
text:
His offering was one silver charger; the word in the original denotes a deep dish or bowl.  Its weight shows it to have been of a large size. 
 
  A hundred and thirty shekels; nearly five and a half pounds.  Exodus 38:24  
 
  One silver bowl; a sacrificial bowl for receiving the blood of the victims. 
 
They whom God has blessed with wealth, or elevated to stations of honor and influence, should esteem it not only their duty but their privilege to be examples of liberality in his service.

title: Numbers 7:84
text: That which is publicly given for God's service and the advancement of his cause, should be managed in an orderly way, and a careful account kept of it, that nothing may be lost, and no scandal given to the cause of truth.   John 6:12 II Corinthians 8:20-21

title: Numbers 7:88
text: Jehovah is a bountiful God, and is delighted with liberality in his people.  Much may be devoted to the support of his worship, and when so used, it is not wasted or unprofitably employed, but is spent to the highest advantage.   Psalms 145:16 Proverbs 11:25 Isaiah 32:8 II Corinthians 9:13

title: Numbers 7:89
text:
Him; God, to whom the altar and tabernacle had been dedicated. 
 
  The voice of one;  Exodus 25:1

title: Numbers 8:2
text: Over against the candlestick; the meaning of these words, which occur also in  Exodus 25:37 , is doubtful.  The candlestick stood on the south side of the sanctuary over against the table of show-bread on the north side.   Exodus 40:24   Some suppose the direction to be, that the lamp-cups should be so arranged that their wicks should incline towards the north, and thus throw their light towards the table of show-bread; others, that the six wicks of the branches should all incline towards the central lamp, called here the candlestick by way of distinction.

title: Numbers 8:3
text: Ministers of the gospel who communicate a knowledge of God and his will to men, shine as lights in the world holding forth the word of life; and multitudes who were in darkness, are, through their instrumentality, made light in the Lord, and prepared to shine as the brightness of the firmament and as the stars for ever.

title: Numbers 8:6
text:
Levites; those of the tribe of Levi not descended from Aaron. These assisted the priests, Aaron's sons, in various services about the tabernacle, and afterwards about the temple. 
 
The best of men need cleansing through faith in the blood of Christ, and by the influence of his Spirit, in order that their services may be accepted of God.

title: Numbers 8:7
text: Sprinkle water of purifying upon them; the preparation of which is described in  Numbers 19:1-19 .  Compare  Hebrews 9:13-14 .

title: Numbers 8:11
text: Offer the Levites; consecrate them to the service of the Lord in the various duties of the sanctuary.   Numbers 8:14-19

title: Numbers 8:19
text: To make an atonement for the children of Israel; to make propitiation for the children of Israel, in whose behalf they acted; that is, to avert form them the judgments that would come upon them if they should presume to meddle with the sacred things.  Numbers 1:53 Numbers 18:1-5

title: Numbers 8:21
text: Though God is the author of spiritual cleansing, he accomplishes it through the means of his appointment; and men are bound to use these means according to his will, and thus cleanse themselves from all filthiness of the flesh and of the spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.   II Corinthians 7:1 Isaiah 1:16-17 Ezekiel 18:31

title: Numbers 8:24
text: Twenty and five years old; at this age they began to wait upon the priests, learn their duties as Levites, and do some things about the tabernacle; but they did not enter fully on their work as Levites till they were thirty.  See note to  Numbers 4:3 .

title: Numbers 8:26
text:
Keep the charge, and--do no service; after the age of fifty, they had the general charge of the sanctuary, assisted their younger brethren in various ways, and instructed the people; but were released from the most laborious duties of their offices, especially the bearing of the sacred things. 
 
After ministers of the gospel have become too old to perform the laborious duties of their office, they may still be very useful by wise counsel, judicious instruction, habitual prayer, and a holy example; and should be provided for to the end of life.

title: Numbers 9:1
text: The first month; Abib.

title: Numbers 9:2
text: The passover;  Exodus 12:2-14:1

title: Numbers 9:3
text: As the death of Christ is the procuring cause of the salvation of his people, it is his will that they should from time to time to celebrate it according to his appointment, with humility, penitence, gratitude, and joy.   Matthew 26:26-28 Luke 22:19 I Corinthians 11:23-26

title: Numbers 9:11
text: The fourteenth day of the second month; this was in the month Zif, and one month after the usual time of keeping the passover.

title: Numbers 9:13
text:
Forbeareth to keep the passover; at the usual time. 
 
To obey God, we must neither neglect to commemorate the death of Christ, nor do it in an unholy manner; but must examine ourselves and see whether we believe on him, feel our need of his salvation,a nd make it our great object in all things to do his will.   I Corinthians 11:27-30

title: Numbers 9:18
text: At the commandment of the Lord; as manifested by the moving or resting of the cloud.

title: Numbers 9:23
text: If we are disposed to obey God, he will, by his word, his Spirit, and his providence, make so plain the path of duty, that in walking in it we shall be safe, useful, and happy.

title: Numbers 10:5
text: Blow an alarm; this was done by blowing long and loud with a broken, interrupted sound.

title: Numbers 10:8
text: Christian ministers are placed as watchmen, and should give the people counsel and warning from God.  When they speak, it should be with such plainness as to be understood, and with such affection as is best suited to persuade the people to follow their directions.  I Corinthians 14:6-19 Ephesians 4:15

title: Numbers 10:10
text: May be to you for a memorial before your God; may, as it were, remind him of his engagements to you as his covenant people.  Compare  Numbers 10:9 .

title: Numbers 10:12
text: Puran; between Sinai and Palestine, west and southwest of Edom, there were two intervening encampments.   Numbers 11:35 Numbers 12:16 Numbers 33:16-18

title: Numbers 10:13
text: All men are on a journey through this world.  Jehovah offers to be their guide, and if they follow him he will direct them to the Canaan of eternal rest.  If they reject him, and continue to walk in their own way, they will wander in darkness and find no rest for ever.

title: Numbers 10:14
text: The standard of the camp of--Judah; that of the first grand division of three tribes.

title: Numbers 10:17
text: Set forward, bearing the tabernacle; the Gershonites and Merarites followed immediately after the first division, that they might have time to set up the tabernacle before the Kohathites came.

title: Numbers 10:21
text:
Bearing the sanctuary; that is, the most holy things, as the ark, the altar of incense, the candlestick, etc.  See  Numbers 3:31 . 
 
  The other; the Gershonites and Merarites.

title: Numbers 10:29
text:
Raguel; supposed to be the same as Reuel and Jethro.  Exodus 2:18 Exodus 3:1 Exodus 18:1  
 
Those who have chosen God for their guide, and are on their way to heaven, should urge others, especially their relatives and friends, to accompany them, and present as a motive the good which God has promised to those who follow him.

title: Numbers 10:31
text: Be to us instead of eyes; Hobab was acquainted with the country, and could assist on their journey.

title: Numbers 10:32
text: Those who are journeying towards heaven need help not only from God, but also from one another; and they may be of great assistance to each other in guarding from danger, and guiding in the way of safety, usefulness, and peace.

title: Numbers 10:33
text: Three days' journey; namely, from Sinai to the wilderness of Paran.  Numbers 10:11-13

title: Numbers 10:36
text: However much assistance the people of God may receive from men, their desires can never be fully met, nor their wants satisfied, without the permanent presence and favor of God.

title: Numbers 11:1
text:
The fire of the Lord; a miraculous fire proceeding from Jehovah's presence.  Compare  Leviticus 10:2 . 
 
Discontentment with the dealings of God is unwise and wicked.  Those who indulge in it provoke him, and expose themselves to his wrath.

title: Numbers 11:2
text: The wicked are more indebted to the righteous than they are apt to imagine, and in their distresses they often feel this, and look to them for help.

title: Numbers 11:3
text: Taberah; a burning.

title: Numbers 11:4
text:
Mixed multitude;  Exodus 12:1 
  Fell a lusting; impatiently desired other kinds of food.

title: Numbers 11:6
text:
Our soul is dried away; we languish and are suffering for want of other food. 
 
We are apt to depreciate and undervalue the blessings we have, and to magnify and overrate those which we desire.

title: Numbers 11:7
text:
As coriander-seed; a small round seed. 
 
  Bdellium; according to some, the pearl; according to others, a gummy secretion of a yellowish-white color.

title: Numbers 11:11
text: The best of men are but partly sanctified; and not unfrequently in their hearts, and sometimes in words, they find fault with God.

title: Numbers 11:15
text:
Out of hand; at once, now. 
 
Those who kill themselves, or ask God or men to kill them, are not in a proper state to die.  Did they feel right, whatever their trials, they would say, All the days of my appointed time will I wait, till my change come.  Not my will, but thine be done.   Job 14:14 Luke 22:42

title: Numbers 11:17
text:
Put it upon them; furnish them with the special influences of my Spirit, as I have furnished thee, to fit them for their work. 
 
God is often kind and gracious in withholding from them what they need. If he calls them to great and difficult services, they have no reason to complain or to despond; if they trust in him he will provide for them, that as their duties are, their ability may also be.

title: Numbers 11:18
text: Sanctify yourselves; by the customary rites,  Exodus 19:10 .  These signified and demanded of the people inward purification.

title: Numbers 11:20
text:
Come out at your nostrils; they would eat flesh till they were not only satisfied, but made sick by it and loathed it. 
 
What people impatiently and wickedly desire, God sometimes suffers them to have, and to abuse to their ruin.

title: Numbers 11:23
text:
Waxed short; is God unable to do what he has promised? 
 
It needs stronger faith than good men often have, or without the influences of the Holy Spirit would ever have, to believe that God will do all that he has promised.

title: Numbers 11:25
text: Prophesied; prophecy is here used in the widest sense, as often in the New Testament, to denote all religious discourse delivered under immediate inspiration.  Compare  I Corinthians 12:10 I Corinthians 14:3-5 .  In the same sense it is also employed elsewhere in the Old Testament.  I Samuel 10:9-13

title: Numbers 11:28
text: Forbid them; Joshua seems to have thought that, in remaining behind, they had been guilty of disrespect towards Moses.  But Moses rejoiced in every gift of God's Spirit, though some irregularity might be connected with it.  Compare  Luke 9:49-50 .

title: Numbers 11:29
text: It is natural for men to envy others on account of the blessings which God gives them; but divine grace teaches us to rejoice in the blessings of others, and to desire that, if consistent, such blessings may be given to all.

title: Numbers 11:31
text:
From the sea; that it, from Africa beyond the Red sea, where quails are found at the present day in prodigious numbers. 
 
  Two cubits high; that is, in heaps about two cubits high.

title: Numbers 11:32
text: Ten homers; an ephah is estimated to have contained about one and one-twelfth bushels, and a homer was ten ephahs.  We are not, however, to understand ten homers for each individual, but rather, for each head of a household.  Some propose to render "ten heaps," as the word is elsewhere used,  Exodus 8:14 ; but the sacred writer plainly means to indicate a definite quantity.  This immense provision showed not only the abundance of the quails, but also the inordinate lust for which God punished the people.

title: Numbers 11:33
text: God may in wrath give men what they desire, to show them and others the wickedness and folly of wishing to have their own way, and refusing to be guided and governed by him.

title: Numbers 11:34
text:
Kibroth-hattaavah; that is, the graves of lust. 
 
Lust, and the use of things lusted after, are plagues which have opened and filled many graves.

title: Numbers 11:35
text: Hazeroth; a place still farther on the way towards Canaan.

title: Numbers 12:1
text:
Miriam; the sister of Moses and Aaron.   Exodus 15:20  
 
  Ethiopian woman; supposed by some to be Zipporah, called and Ethiopian, or, as in the original, a Cushite, because a native of that part of Arabia which was settled by the descendants of Cush.  Exodus 2:16 Exodus 2:21   Others suppose that she was a Cushite woman whom Moses had married after the death of Zipporah. 
 
The most inoffensive character, and the most useful life, may not secure persons from being blamed, even by their nearest relatives; but, if humble, patient, and submissive, the Lord will plead their cause, and in due time bring forth their righteousness as the light, and their judgment as the noonday.   Psalms 37:1-11

title: Numbers 12:2
text: The Lord hears all that men say; and he is especially displeased with those who, without good reason, talk against and find fault with his people.

title: Numbers 12:3
text: Meek; not easily provoked or disposed to complain, not proud of self-sufficient, but humble, patient, and submissive.

title: Numbers 12:6
text: In a vision--in a dream; that was the usual way in which he communicated with prophets.

title: Numbers 12:8
text:
Mouth to mouth; the same as face to face,  Exodus 33:11 Deuteronomy 34:10 . 
 
  Apparently; in open vision. 
 
  Similitude; form,  Exodus 33:23 Exodus 34:5-8 Ezekiel 1:26 . 
 
Those who wickedly oppose such as God loves and peculiarly favors, have great cause to fear; for he views what is done to them as in a sense done to him.   Matthew 25:40

title: Numbers 12:10
text: Sin is sometimes visited with immediate punishment.

title: Numbers 12:11
text: To commit known sin is foolish, because it always tends not only to dishonor God, but also to injure those who commit it.

title: Numbers 12:14
text:
Spit in her face; an eastern way of administering a very severe rebuke. 
 
  Be ashamed seven days; manifest her sense of shame and humiliation by a separation of seven days from the ordinary privileges and society of the family.  The inference is, that much more should Miriam be separated seven days from God's household--the camp of Israel--when he has so rebuked her. 
 
However great the sins of transgressors, when they truly repent and turn to the Lord he will forgive them.  His people, so far as they have his Spirit, will do the same; and desire for such the greatest blessings.   Matthew 18:21-35

title: Numbers 13:2
text: Send thou men; this was no command originally given by Jehovah.  He would have had the people go immediately forward under his all- sufficient guidance,  Deuteronomy 1:20-21 .  But when the people proposed first to search the land, he was pleased to permit the measure, and to give directions respecting the manner of executing it.  Deuteronomy 1:22-23

title: Numbers 13:3
text: God deals with men according to the measure of their faith; those counsels that have their origin in an unbelieving spirit must be expected to have a disastrous issue.

title: Numbers 13:16
text:
Hoshea; salvation. 
 
  Jehoshua; Jehovah is salvation.  The Greek form of this name is JESUS, of whom Joshua was appointed to be an eminent type.

title: Numbers 13:20
text:
Fat or lean; fruitful or barren. 
 
  Time of the first ripe grapes; about the month of August.

title: Numbers 13:21
text:
Wilderness of Zin; lying south of Canaan. 
 
  Rehob; a city near the north part of Canaan. 
 
  Hamath; a city of Syria, lying still further north.

title: Numbers 13:22
text:
Hebron; a city in the south part of Canaan, about twenty miles from Jerusalem. 
 
  Anak; son of Arba, a distinguished man, after whom Hebron was called Kirjath-Arba, or the city of Arba.   Genesis 23:2 Joshua 14:15

title: Numbers 13:23
text: Eshcol; a fruitful valley near Hebron.

title: Numbers 13:24
text: Called the brook Eshcol; Eshcol meaning a cluster.

title: Numbers 13:26
text: Kadesh; Kadesh-barnea,  Deuteronomy 1:19 .  It lay on the south border of Canaan, towards Edom.

title: Numbers 13:27
text: Those who trust the promises of God and follow his directions, will find that what he has promised is true, and their own experience will realize its fulfilment.

title: Numbers 13:28
text: Children of Anak; a family of giants.

title: Numbers 13:29
text: Men may do externally what God directs, and yet with such a spirit and for such a purpose as may tend to their ruin.

title: Numbers 13:30
text: Different men may unite externally in doing the same things, and yet with a very different spirit and for totally different ends.  Thus what is done may be to one a savor of life unto life, and to another a savor of death unto death.

title: Numbers 13:32
text:
Eateth up the inhabitants; causing them to die from the unhealthiness of the climate, or some other cause.  If this were so, it must have been strange that they were so large and strong. 
 
In making excuses for not doing their duty, and saying that they are not able to do what God requires and is ready to enable them to perform, men are often very inconsistent and contradict themselves.

title: Numbers 14:1
text: A long course of bondange, whether bodily or spiritual, is suited to produce a weak and cowardly spirit; to degrade and debase the human mind, and unfit it for great and noble deeds.

title: Numbers 14:5
text: Fell on their faces; as a sign of their deep grief for the sin of the people, and their earnest intercession with God in their behalf.

title: Numbers 14:6
text: Rent their clothes; thus they expressed deep sorrow and holy indignation for the unbelieving and rebellious spirit of the people.

title: Numbers 14:9
text:
Are bread for us; food for our swords.  Compare  Numbers 24:8 . 
 
Rebellion against God is the great cause of human sorrow.  By trusting in him and doing his will, men may obtain all needed blessings, in the best way, at the right time, and with only those sacrifices which will in the end promote their highest good.

title: Numbers 14:10
text: The most unreasonable men are most ready to use mob violence.  Instead of answering their opponents, they attempt to kill them.  Sometimes they for a time succeed, but often they bring ruin on themselves.  Acts 7:59

title: Numbers 14:11
text: Men may see the most stupendous miracles, and receive the greatest temporal mercies, and yet remain enemies to God.  No means, without the converting influences of his Spirit, will ever lead them to love and serve him.

title: Numbers 14:16
text:
Therefore he hath slain them; this, Moses thought, would be greatly to God's dishonor. 
 
Good men dread what will dishonor God more than any temporal evils, and desire the promotion of his glory more than the reception of all temporal mercies.

title: Numbers 14:17
text: Let the power of my Lord be great; be greatly manifested in forgiving their iniquity, and bringing them into the land of promise.

title: Numbers 14:20
text:
According to thy word; God so far hearkened to Moses as to spare the people for a time, and to bring their children into the promised land.   Numbers 14:31  
 
The righteous are foten the means of averting great calamities from the wicked, and bringing upon them unspeakable good.

title: Numbers 14:21
text:
But as truly as I live--filled with the glory of the Lord; though Jehovah, upon the intercession of Moses, would spare the people from immediate destruction, he would yet deal with them in such a way as to manifest to all the earth his glorious attributes, mingling justice with mercy. 
 
God will bestow mercy only in such a way as is consistent with justice, wisdom, goodness, and truth--only in such a way as will glorify himself, give a correct view of his character, and fill the hearts of all holy beings with admiration and delight.

title: Numbers 14:22
text: Ten times; that is, often, a definite number for an indefinite.

title: Numbers 14:24
text: Steadfastness in duty, however unpopular or dangerous, is the way to glory, honor, and blessedness.

title: Numbers 14:25
text: Dwelt in the valley; probably the valley at the foot of the hill mentioned  Numbers 14:40-41 , whence they could easily take possession of the hill-top.   Numbers 14:43   These words are inserted by Moses in a parenthetical way, to explain the reason of the command that follows.

title: Numbers 14:28
text: God sometimes takes men at their word, and evils which they wickedly imprecate, he in righteous judgment brings upon them.

title: Numbers 14:31
text: Ye said;  Numbers 14:3

title: Numbers 14:33
text:
Bear your whoredoms; suffer the effects of their sins.  Exodus 20:5  Apostasy from God is spiritual whoredom.   Deuteronomy 31:16  
 
  Forty years; from the time they left Egypt. 
 
Many evils come upon children in consequence of the sins of parents; but, if they do not imitate their parents; but, if they do not imitate their parents, nor disobey God, he will overrule these evils for their highest good.   Numbers 14:31

title: Numbers 14:34
text: Know my breach of promise; or my turning away from you; that is, experience its bitter effects in your destruction.

title: Numbers 14:38
text: In due time, all will see the difference between the righteous and the wicked, between him that serveth God and him that serveth him not.

title: Numbers 14:39
text: These sayings; what God had told him.   Numbers 14:29-35

title: Numbers 14:40
text: The mountain; which lies north-west of Kadesh.

title: Numbers 14:41
text: As the Lord never brings evils upon any but for the wisest and best reasons, when he does bring them, none should murmur against him, but all should cheerfully submit, feeling that he afflicts them less than their iniquities deserve, and saying, It is the Lord; let him do as seemeth good in his sight.

title: Numbers 14:45
text: Hormah; a place in the south part of Canaan, not many miles from Kadesh.  It was before called Zephath.   Numbers 21:3 Judges 1:17

title: Numbers 15:2
text:
Ye; the children of those who were to die in the wilderness.  Numbers 14:31  
 
  The land of your habitations; Canaan. In the wilderness, which was a land not sown nor planted with vineyards, they would not all be able to comply with these requirements. 
 
Though ever so many prove unfaithful to God, and cut themselves off from his blessings, it will not annul his faithfulness, or render his promises of no effect.   Romans 3:3-4

title: Numbers 15:4
text: A tenth-deal--a hin; an ephah contained between thirty-four and thirty-five quarts.  A tenth-deal was the tenth, and a hin the seventh part of an ophah.

title: Numbers 15:14
text: As ye do, so he shall do; not only to prevent the introduction of heathenish rites, but to convey the idea that there is one religion and one way of salvation for Jews and Gentiles.

title: Numbers 15:16
text: Persons of all nations may have access to God through Jesus Christ, and by faith in him may be freely pardoned, sanctified, and saved; whether they be Jews or Gentiles, high or low, bond or free.

title: Numbers 15:21
text: God is the giver of all our mercies, and in partaking of them we should gratefully acknowledge and adore him.   Proverbs 3:6 Philippians 4:6

title: Numbers 15:24
text: According to the manner; the manner above directed for the meat-offering,  Numbers 15:8-9

title: Numbers 15:26
text: The law of God is exceeding broad.  We often violate it through inattention, without at the time being aware of it; and are in continual need of pardoning mercy through Christ.   Psalms 19:13

title: Numbers 15:28
text: Sinneth ignorantly; through carelessness or inattention, violating some law without at the time being aware of it.

title: Numbers 15:30
text:
Doeth aught presumptuously; violates a known law by design, and in defiance of Jehovah. 
 
The open transgression of known divine laws is a reproach upon their Author, and brings upon the soul his awful displeasure.

title: Numbers 15:31
text: His iniquity shall be upon him; shall rest upon him unforgiven, requiring his punishment.

title: Numbers 15:32
text: Gathered sticks upon the sabbath-day; presumptuously, in open defiance of God and his laws.   Numbers 15:30-31

title: Numbers 15:36
text: Wilful sabbath-breaking, in opposition to the known command of God, is a sin of presumption, and exposes those who practise it to be cut off for ever from his favor.

title: Numbers 15:38
text: A ribbon of blue; to distinguish them as the true worshippers of God from their heathen neighbors, and to remind them of the law of God and their duty to keep it.  In our Lord's day the Pharisees made this precept the occasion of vain ostentation; keeping it in the letter, but breaking it in the spirit.   Matthew 23:5

title: Numbers 15:39
text: The disciples of Christ should be continually mindful of their high calling; and should endeavor to be so distinguished from the men of this world in their daily spirit and conduct, that all may recognize them as the true children of God.

title: Numbers 15:40
text: All the directions of God are designed and adapted to make his people holy, to remind them of their obligations, and lead them so to keep his commandments as to receive the blessings of his everlasting love.

title: Numbers 16:2
text: Famous in the congregation; rather, "the called of the congregation."  See note to  Numbers 1:16 .

title: Numbers 16:3
text:
Are holy; they mean to say that they all stand in as near a relation to God as Aaron and Moses, and ought not to be excluded from priestly offices. 
 
  Above the congregation; by acting as rulers and taking the direction of their concerns.   Numbers 16:10 Numbers 16:13 Numbers 16:28  
 
When some are raised to power and influence, others often overlook the hand of God in their elevation, and ascribe it all to men; and instead of being contented with the palce which he assigns them, and seeking to discharge its duties, they envy and blame those above them, and, in so doing, find fault with God.

title: Numbers 16:4
text: He fell upon his face; expressing his deep sense of their guilt and danger.

title: Numbers 16:5
text: Will he cause to come near; God would show whom he had chosen to be priest and leader in his worship.

title: Numbers 16:7
text:
The man whom the Lord doth choose; that is, as priest.  This he will do by giving some token of approbation of his conduct. 
 
  He shall be holy; acknowledged and treated as high-priest. 
 
Servants of God, in the use of suitable means, are disposed to refer their cause, and that of their friends, to him; and in faith, patience, and prayer, to wait for his decision.

title: Numbers 16:11
text:
Against the Lord; their conduct was rebellion against his arrangement, and of course against him. 
 
Men who ungratefully overlook the goodness of God to them, neglect the appropriate duties of their station, and ambitiously strive to usurp the places of those above them, are under the influence of pride and ripening for ruin.

title: Numbers 16:14
text: Put out the eyes of these men; treat them as blind, and attempt to lead them at pleasure.

title: Numbers 16:15
text:
Respect not thou their offering; regard it not with favor, but with just indignation. 
 
When falsely charged with baseness and crime, conscious integrity, and the expectation that God will vindicate those who trust in and obey him, give unfailing support, and prepare the soul to go forward in duty with firmness, courage, and success.   Psalms 37:3-9

title: Numbers 16:26
text: All such connection with the wicked as tends to encourage them in sin, and all appearance of conniving at their transgressions, should be carefully avoided.   II Corinthians 6:17

title: Numbers 16:30
text: Quick; alive.   Numbers 16:33

title: Numbers 16:33
text:
All that appertained to them; all that belonged to them and were with them.  The children of Korah, who were manifestly not present in this seditious assembly, died not.   Numbers 26:11   His posterity are subsequently mentioned among the servants of God.   I Chronicles 9:19 I Chronicles 26:1  
 
Though this is a state of trial rather than of retribution, God sometimes manifests his hatred of sin in such a manner as to show that he is a God that judgeth in the earth, and that the wages of sin is death.   Psalms 58:11 Romans 6:23

title: Numbers 16:35
text: Two hundred and fifty men;  Numbers 16:2 Numbers 16:1

title: Numbers 16:37
text:
Out of the burning; from the fire that had destroyed the men. 
 
  They are hallowed; the censers, or pans for incense, were set apart for the sacred purpose mentioned in  Numbers 16:38-40 .

title: Numbers 16:41
text: Punishment of itself will not change the hearts of the wicked, or lead them to love and serve God.  Such a change, whenever it takes place, is by the grace of God, through the influences of the Holy Spirit.

title: Numbers 16:46
text: Make an atonement for them; by offering the incense to the Lord, and supplicating his mercy; thus typifying the atonement and intercession of Christ.

title: Numbers 16:48
text:
The plague was stayed; expressive of the efficacy of the great atoning sacrifice and the all-prevalent intercession of Christ. 
 
A good man is kind, compassionate, and forgiving; and does not desire the destruction of the wicked, however much they may have injured him.

title: Numbers 16:49
text: No finite mind can fully comprehend the evil of sin.  It has slain not only thousands, but millions and hundreds of millions.  Deliverance from it is the greatest of blessings, and all who receive this blessing will be for ever indebted for it to the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost.  None who continue to love and practise sin can escape perdition.   Ezekiel 33:11

title: Numbers 17:5
text:
Whom I shall choose; to be high-priest. 
 
  Make to cease--the murmurings; about the priesthood, by showing his will with regard to it. 
 
To the clear manifestations of the divine will all should cheerfully submit; and they who do not, incur the guilt of rebelling against God.

title: Numbers 17:8
text: God is the author of nature as well as of grace.  All its laws are under his direction, and subject to his control.

title: Numbers 17:10
text:
Their murmurings; on account of the priesthood's being confined to the family of Aaron. 
 
God uses all reasonable and proper means to prevent men from continuing in sin; but his mercies, of perverted and abused, will increase their guilt and aggravate their ruin.

title: Numbers 17:12
text: We die--we all perish; words of terror and despondency, in view of the severe and oft-repeated judgments which had fallen upon them.

title: Numbers 18:1
text:
Thou and thy sons and thy father's house; this includes the Levites with the priests; for by his father's house are meant the sons of Levi. 
 
  Bear the iniquity of the sanctuary; of all the service pertaining to the sanctuary.  It was now shown that Aaron and his sons were confirmed in the honors of the priesthood, and the Lord informed him that they must bear its responsibilities.  If any thing should be done wrong, they would be accountable. 
 
  Thou and thy sons; this includes only the priests.

title: Numbers 18:3
text: The ministry is a great and responsible work.  To be intrusted with it is a peculiar honor; and to be made faithful in discharging its duties is an unspeakable blessing.

title: Numbers 18:4
text: A stranger; one not of the tribe of Levi.

title: Numbers 18:5
text: Keep the charge of the sanctuary; to see that every thing with regard to the worship of God was done according to his direction.

title: Numbers 18:6
text: Do the service; the less sacred and more laborious parts of it.

title: Numbers 18:7
text: The stranger; one not of the family of Aaron.

title: Numbers 18:8
text: The charge of my heave-offerings; the heave-offerings and wave-offerings were presented under the priest's direction, and then, as a general rule, went to his maintenance.  Compare  Numbers 18:11 .

title: Numbers 18:9
text:
Reserved from the fire; from such offerings as were partly burnt upon the altar. 
 
  Meat-offering--sin-offering--trespass-offering; the meat-offerings were the unbloody oblations of flour, cakes, etc.  After a portion of these had been burned on the altar, the rest fell to the priest.  The same was the law in respect to sin-offerings and trespass-offerings. But the peace-offerings belonged to the offerer, with the exception of the wave-breast and heave-shoulder.  Thus a provision was made for the support of the priests and their families.  See  Leviticus 7:1-38 .

title: Numbers 18:12
text: The best of the oil--the best of the wine; the reference here is to the first-fruits of the wine and oil, of which it was the duty of the Israelites to give a portion to the priest, and which were to be of the best quality.

title: Numbers 18:14
text: Devoted; solemnly given to God.  Provided it was any thing that might be eaten or otherwise consumed, it went to the priest.  But vessels of gold, silver, or brass, went to the service of the sanctuary.

title: Numbers 18:15
text: Shalt thou redeem; this was done by the priest's receiving a specified sum of money in exchange for it.

title: Numbers 18:16
text:
That are to be redeemed; that is, of men.  The first-born of unclean beasts were to be redeemed by a lamb.   Exodus 13:13  
 
  According to thine estimation; that is, according to the valuation prescribed to thee in the law; for this was not left wholly to the priest's discretion.

title: Numbers 18:19
text:
A covenant of salt; a perpetual, permanent covenant. 
 
While ministers of religion are precluded by their office from engaging in worldly business, and thus obtaining a support for themselves and their families, it is the will of God that they should be supported by those for whose spiritual good they minister.

title: Numbers 18:20
text: No inheritance; no landed property.

title: Numbers 18:21
text: The tenth; a tenth part of the produce or increase of the property of the other tribes.

title: Numbers 18:23
text: They shall bear their iniquity; if any thing is done wrong, they shall bear the blame.

title: Numbers 18:27
text: As though it were the corn of the threshing-floor; that is, it shall be given by you to the high-priest just as common Israelites give a tithe from the corn of their threshing-floor to the common priests.

title: Numbers 18:32
text:
Ye shall bear no sin; they would not do wrong in eating, as they would if they should not first offer a tenth for the use of the priests according to the Lord's directions. 
 
God requires not only that his ministers and their families should be supported, but also that they should have something for pious and charitable uses; and in devoting all to him, they may gratefully partake of what they need, and expect his blessing to rest upon them.

title: Numbers 19:4
text: In the Old Testament, as well as the New, we are often reminded of the prevalence and evil of sin, and the necessity of the atonement of Christ, and of purification by the Holy Spirit, in order to acceptance with God and preparation for heaven.

title: Numbers 19:9
text: Water of separation; with which to purify those who had been separated from the congregation on account of ceremonial uncleanness.

title: Numbers 19:10
text: Though God is the author of spiritual purification, men do not abtain it without the use of means.  They must make efforts according to his directions, or they will fail of his blessing.

title: Numbers 19:12
text: It; the water of separation,  Numbers 19:1

title: Numbers 19:20
text: Sin is the cause of death, and the putrefaction of a dead body may well remind us of the pollution of a corrupt soul.  All the washings and sprinklings under Levitical institutions were designed to teach the necessity of the washing of regeneration and the renewing of the Holy Ghost.   Titus 3:3-7

title: Numbers 20:1
text:
Desert of Zin; a desert south of Canaan, and west of Edom.  Numbers 20:16  
 
  The first month; of the fortieth year after they left Egypt, having during that time wandered in the wilderness, as God foretold,  Numbers 14:27-35 Numbers 33:19-36 .  A list of places visited in these wanderings is given in  Numbers 33:1-56 .

title: Numbers 20:5
text: Inclination to sin is common to all men.  No dispensations of Providence, without the teaching of the Holy Spirit, will prevent their indulging it, or keep them from rebelling against God.

title: Numbers 20:11
text:
vv 11-12. 
 
  Smote the rock twice; this repetition of the stroke seems to have been unauthorized, and to have preceeded from a mixture of impatience and unbelief. 
 
  Believed me not, to sanctify me; they were guilty of an impatient spirit,  Numbers 20:10 Psalms 106:33 ; of a rebellious temper,  Numbers 20:24   Numbers 24:14 ; and did not manifest full confidence in God, or suitably honor him before the people as the author of the miracle.

title: Numbers 20:12
text: The best of men are defective, even in those virtues for which they are most distinguished.  Abraham was wanting in faith, Moses in meekness, and Job in patience: and if any are saved, it must be by grace through faith; and that not of themselves, it is the gift of God.  Ephesians 2:8 James 1:17

title: Numbers 20:14
text: Travail; labor, hardship, suffering.

title: Numbers 20:16
text: An Angel; the Angel of his presence; the Messenger of the covenant; the Word of God.   John 1:1

title: Numbers 20:21
text: The Israelites were not at liberty to engage in war with any nation, except as directed by God.  In destroying the Canaanites, and taking possession of their country, they were the appointed instruments of his wrath against those nations on account of their sins.

title: Numbers 20:22
text: Mount Hor; one of the summits of Seir, a chain of mountains running through Edom towards the eastern gulf of the Red sea.

title: Numbers 20:24
text: The sins of good men are peculiarly offensive to God, and lead him often to visit them with sore calamities.

title: Numbers 20:29
text: The most distinguished and useful must soon die.  Their death is a public calamity, and a just cause of general grief and mourning.

title: Numbers 21:1
text:
In the south; the south part of Canaan. 
 
  By the way of the spies; the way by which the spies had entered the land of Canaan, namely, by the south,  Numbers 13:22 .  Some, however, render, "by the way of Atharim."

title: Numbers 21:3
text: Hormah; meaning, utter destruction.

title: Numbers 21:5
text:
This light bread; the manna.   John 6:31  
 
However much men may suffer on account of their sins, they frequently repeat them; and under the calamities which come upon them, they often find fault not only with men, but with God, and thus multiply and increase their troubles.   Proverbs 19:3

title: Numbers 21:6
text: Fiery; probably so called from the burning heat of their bite.

title: Numbers 21:9
text: Jehovah answers prayer in a manner suited to try the faith of his people.  Though he is the great efficient Cause, they must use the means appointed in order to avail themselves of his blessings.  If they do this as he has directed, through grace they will live; if they do not, they will die, and the blame be all on them.  John 3:14 John 6:29 John 11:25-26

title: Numbers 21:10
text: Set forward; to go round the land of Edom, and up north, through its eastern border, to the land of Moab.   Deuteronomy 2:1-8

title: Numbers 21:12
text: The valley of Zered; a valley north-east of the Red sea, on the way towards Canaan.  The Zered empties into the Dead sea.

title: Numbers 21:13
text:
Arnon; a small stream which empties into the Dead sea from the east. 
 
Life is like a journey through a wilderness.  We are never stationary, but constantly passing onward to our final and everlasting abode.

title: Numbers 21:14
text:
The book; some book describing the wars referred to. 
 
  In the Red sea; or "in Suphah;" apparently designed to confirm the statement just made, that the Arnon was the northern boundary of Moab.  Numbers 21:28

title: Numbers 21:15
text: Ar; the capital of Moab.   Numbers 21:28 .

title: Numbers 21:16
text:
Beer; meaning a well.   Numbers 21:18  
 
Though we have many and great trials in this world, yet they are never as many or great as our sins deserve, and the Lord graciously bestows many and great mercies, which, if gratefully received and rightly used, will eventually prepare us for deliverance from all trouble, and the reception of unmingled eternal joy.   Ephesians 3:10-21

title: Numbers 21:20
text:
And from Bamoth--to the top of Pisgah; or, "and from Bamoth to the valley that is in the country of Moab by the top of Pisgah." 
 
  Pisgah; the summit of Nebo, one of the range of mountains called Abarim, between the mountains of Gilead on the north and the mountains of Seir on the south.   Deuteronomy 32:49  
 
  Jeshimon; meaning, the wilderness.

title: Numbers 21:21
text: The Amorites; th tribes so called inhabited the south of Palestine,  Genesis 14:7 Genesis 14:13 Numbers 13:29 ; also the region beyond the Jordon, as far south as the river Arnon.

title: Numbers 21:23
text: Jahaz; a city near the northern border of Moab.

title: Numbers 21:26
text: Heshbon; the city in which Sihon lived, about sixteen miles north of the Arnon.   Numbers 21:34

title: Numbers 21:27
text: In proverbs; that is, in a figurative and poetic style.  The words that follow seem to be a triumphal song of the Amorites, celebrating their victory over Moab.

title: Numbers 21:28
text: A fire gone out of Heshbon; a fire, that is, a desolating force, has gone out from Shion, to whom Heshbon now belongs, and who has made it his residence.

title: Numbers 21:29
text: Chemosh; one of the idols of Moab.

title: Numbers 21:30
text: Dibon--Medeba; cities between Heshbon and the Arnon.

title: Numbers 21:31
text: In this world we have many enemies, and if we would be saved we must fight, not with flesh and blood only, but with the principalities and powers, with the rulers of the darkness of this world, and with spiritual wickedness in high places.

title: Numbers 21:33
text:
Bashan; a country east of the Jordan, between mount Gilead and mount Lebanon. 
 
  Edrei; one of the chief cities of Bashan.

title: Numbers 21:34
text: Those who trust in God and do his will have no reason to fear any enemies, however numerous or powerful.  He will in due time make them conquerors and more than conquerors, through Him that loved them and gave himself for them; and to him they will for ever give all the glory.

title: Numbers 22:1
text:
The plains of Moab; in the Jordan valley; so called because they had once belonged to Moab.  They had afterwards been taken by the Amorites, and now by the children of Israel. 
 
  This side; the east side of Jordan. 
 
  Jericho; a city of Canaan on the west side of Jordan.

title: Numbers 22:3
text: Those who know not Jehovah and do not trust in him, are always exposed to distressing fears, and to many evils from which no human wisdom or power can save them.

title: Numbers 22:4
text:
Elders; the word translated elders means also princes or rulers.  Numbers 22:8 Numbers 22:14-15  
 
  Midian; a people living near the Moabites, and who on this occasion acted in concert with the Moabites,  Numbers 22:7 . 
 
  Lick up all; overcome and swallow us up.

title: Numbers 22:5
text:
Balaam; a noted sorcerer or soothsayer, of Mesopotamia.  Numbers 22:7 Joshua 13:22  
 
  Pethor; a place near the Euphrates.   Numbers 23:7 Deuteronomy 23:4

title: Numbers 22:6
text:
Wot; know. 
 
The wicked place that confidence in men which should be placed only in God, and hope for that from them which can come only from him.

title: Numbers 22:7
text: Rewards of divination; money or presents to induce him to come and curse Israel.

title: Numbers 22:8
text: As the Lord shall speak; this shows that Balaam had some knowledge of Jehovah, and of his obligations to follow his guidance.

title: Numbers 22:9
text:
God came unto Balaam; whether he had ever done this before we are not informed. 
 
God has sometimes held communications with wicked men, and given them a knowledge of his will.  But knowledge alone, without love, will not lead them so to obey him as to obtain his blessing.

title: Numbers 22:12
text: All whom god blesses will in the end be truly blessed; and all whom he curses, will in the end be wretched.

title: Numbers 22:13
text: Refuseth to give me leave; the Lord not only did this, but told Balaam not to go.

title: Numbers 22:17
text: Those who supremely regard this world often think that other men, like themselves, for a sufficient reward, can be persuaded to do what they wish.

title: Numbers 22:18
text: I cannot go beyond the word of the Lord; it was true that he could not, consistently with his duty, though it seems he earnestly desired to do so.

title: Numbers 22:19
text: To love the reward of iniquity and desire to do wrong to obtain it, is exceedingly dangerous.  It exposes men to be given up to the practice of iniquity till they sink into irremediable ruin.

title: Numbers 22:20
text: Rise up, and go with them; in this, God suffered.  Balaam, from the love of unrighteous gain, to follow his own inclinations. 2Pe 2.13-16

title: Numbers 22:22
text:
Because he went; Balaam's object and course were wrong and displeasing to God.   Numbers 22:32-34  
 
  The angel of the Lord; supposed to be the same which spoke to him,  Numbers 22:12 Numbers 22:20 , and who is spoken of,  Numbers 22:31-35 .

title: Numbers 22:27
text: Men are often angry with dumb beasts and cruelly beat them, when the fault is all in themselves.

title: Numbers 22:30
text: God could speak through the mouths of dumb animals, and cause them to tell a tale which would make the hearts of their owners quake with fear, and show that, through sin, man has sunk below the beasts that perish.

title: Numbers 22:33
text: Beasts sometimes see what men do not, and by doing that for which they are abused, save their owners from death.

title: Numbers 22:34
text: To have God for an adversary is an unspeakable calamity, and one that should by all needful sacrifices and labors be avoided.

title: Numbers 22:36
text: Utmost coast; boundary of his kingdom.

title: Numbers 22:39
text: Kirjath-huzoth; meaning, a city of streets; probably of many streets--a large city.

title: Numbers 22:40
text:
Balak offered oxen; as is supposed, to his idols. 
 
  Sent to Balaam; to come and feast on the sacrifice.

title: Numbers 22:41
text:
Baal; an idol worshipped by many eastern nations. 
 
All expectations from men, in opposition to the purposes and will of God, are vain, and will end in disappointment.

title: Numbers 23:2
text: Wicked men often take much pains, perform many labors, and are at great expense, to induce God to favor their selfish designs.  Numbers 23:14 Numbers 23:30 Numbers 24:12

title: Numbers 23:3
text: Peradventure; perhaps; it may be.

title: Numbers 23:4
text: Evil-doers often boast of what they have done, and seem to think that their hypocritical, proud, and wicked services entitle them to the special favor of God.   II Kings 10:16 Luke 18:11

title: Numbers 23:5
text: Put a word in Balaam's mouth; directed him what to say.

title: Numbers 23:7
text:
Took up his parable; began to speak in solemn, figurative, prophetic style. 
 
  Aram; afterwards called Mesopotamia; a mountainous country north- east of Moab, between the rivers Euphrates and Tigris. 
 
  Curse--defy; devote to destruction.

title: Numbers 23:9
text: Dwell alone--not be reckoned; they should continue to be a distinct people, and not be united with, swallowed up, or lost in other nations.

title: Numbers 23:10
text:
Who can count--the number? they would be exceedingly numerous. 
 
  The righteous; those whom God accepts and blesses as his redeemed people. 
 
Many have a conviction of the reality, excellence, and importance of true religion, and wish to die the death, who refuse to live the life, of the righteous.

title: Numbers 23:14
text:
Field of Zophim; that is, watchers, because thence they could see to a great distance. 
 
  Pisgah;  Numbers 21:1

title: Numbers 23:16
text: God can speak by the mouth of a wicked man, or of a dumb beast, and communicate momentous truth without changing the nature of the one or the character of the other.   Numbers 23:20 Numbers 23:26 Numbers 24:13

title: Numbers 23:19
text:
God is not a man; he is unchangeable and almighty. 
 
  Make it good; do as he has declared.

title: Numbers 23:21
text:
He hath not beheld iniquity in Jacob; the nation of Israel as a whole was free from idolatry and faithful in God's service. 
 
  Shout of a king; of one who will conquer all his foes.

title: Numbers 23:22
text: Unicorn; in the Hebrew, reem.  This word, in our English translation, which agrees with that of the Greek Seventy and other ancient versions, means one-horned; that is, a one horned animal of great strength, a view which some prefer: but many understand it of the eastern buffalo, an animal of great size and strength.

title: Numbers 23:23
text:
Enchantment--divination; arts by which heathen sorcerers and magicians sought to deceive and overcome their enemies. 
 
  What hath God wrought! he hath wonderfully delivered them, and caused them to overcome their enemies. 
 
No enchantment, divination, devices, or efforts of men or devils can injure those who please God, and have him for their guide, protector, and friend.

title: Numbers 23:24
text: As a great lion; conquer his enemies as a lion does beasts of the forest.

title: Numbers 23:28
text: Peor; a high place in Moab.

title: Numbers 24:1
text:
Enchantments; this word seems to describe the superstitious means which Balaam employed to obtain revelations from God. 
 
  Wilderness; where the Israelites camped. 
 
The Lord will cause all men to see htat it is his unchangeable purpose to bless his people.  Those who rejoice in it will be partakers of his joy, and those who are grieved at it be filled with ever-growing sorrow.

title: Numbers 24:3
text: Whose eyes are open; the eyes of whose mind are opened to see God's revelation.

title: Numbers 24:4
text: However much men may know of God and his ways, and however much they may see of the blessedness of his people, if they do not love and obey him, their knowledge will but increase their guilt and aggravate their ruin.

title: Numbers 24:6
text: Lign-aloes; an oriental tree remarkable for the fragrance of its wood.

title: Numbers 24:7
text:
He shall pour the water out of his buckets; or, "water shall flow from his buckets," that is, in a full stream.  Water is here an emblem of the divine blessing which shall make Israel strong and numerous. 
 
  In many waters; or, by many waters,  Numbers 24:6 .  His posterity shall flourish like trees planted by many waters.

title: Numbers 24:8
text: Eat up the nations; overcome and destroy them.

title: Numbers 24:9
text: God will treat men in some measure as they treat his people.  The blessings which they bestow, or the curses which they heap upon them; will return upon themselves.

title: Numbers 24:11
text: By refusing to please the wicked, men often fail of those worldly honors which by doing wrong they might obtain.

title: Numbers 24:13
text: Men may feel their dependence on God, that they are under his control and cannot escape out of his hands, without rejoicing in their dependence, receiving mercies with gratitude, or giving him the glory of what they enjoy.

title: Numbers 24:14
text: Advertise; inform.

title: Numbers 24:15
text: Whose eyes are open; to see and foretell many things that will hereafter take place.

title: Numbers 24:17
text:
See him--behold him; the Star and the Sceptre that shall rise out of Israel.  The reference is undoubtedly to the Messiah, but in such a way that it includes David's kingdom also, which was perpetuated and received a spiritual form in Christ.   Luke 1:32-33   David's victories over the Moabites and other enemies of Israel were but anticipations and pledges of the final victory which Jesus Christ, his son according to the flesh and sitting upon his throne, should gain over all the enemies of His people.  Psalms 2:12 Psalms 110:1-7 Isaiah 11:10-16  
 
  The children of Sheth; or, as many prefer, the children of tumult, the tumultuous warriors of Moab.  Jeremiah 48:45

title: Numbers 24:21
text: The Kenites; apparently a Midianitish people dwelling in near connection with the Amalekites.   I Samuel 15:6

title: Numbers 24:22
text: Asshur; the Assyrians.

title: Numbers 24:23
text:
Who shall live? who can escape destruction in the midst of such desolations? 
 
A view of the future, while it awakens gladness in the righteous, fills the wicked with apprehension and dismay.

title: Numbers 24:24
text:
Ships; armed forces coming in ships. 
 
  The coast of Chittim; the countries of the west lying on the Mediterranean.  This prophecy was fulfilled in the conquests of the Greeks and Romans over the East. 
 
  Eber; the posterity of Eber living on the east of the Euphrates. To this people and region Abraham belonged, and thence he migrated to the land of Canaan.  To this country Balaam also belonged, so that he who was called to curse Israel was compelled to foretell the doom of "the children of his people." 
 
  He also; probably, the power that comes from Chittim, but some understand the words of Eber.  Balaam having thus far foretold the perpetual triumph of God's people and the overthrow of all their enemies, ceases and departs.

title: Numbers 25:1
text:
Shittim; a place in the plains of Moab, east of Jordan. 
 
  Commit whoredom; this was in consequence of the advice of Balaam.  Numbers 31:15-16 II Peter 2:15-16 Revelation of John 2:14

title: Numbers 25:3
text:
Baal-peor; an idol worshipped by the Moabites. 
 
The greatest evil which any one can do to his fellow-men is to induce them to commit sin, and thus provoke the Lord to destroy them.

title: Numbers 25:4
text: Take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord; these words have been interpreted in two different ways: either, Take all the heads of the people who are involved in this sin and hang them, (the heads of the people;) or, Take with thee all the heads of the people as assistants, and hang them, (the guilty persons.)  The latter interpretation seems to be favored by  Numbers 25:5 .

title: Numbers 25:5
text: It is the will of God that great transgressors against him and against the laws of the state, should in some cases, by the magistrates, be put to death.

title: Numbers 25:7
text: Javelin; a kind of spear.

title: Numbers 25:8
text: The death of notorious criminals is often a great blessing to survivors.

title: Numbers 25:9
text: Twenty and four thousand; supposed to include twenty-three thousand mentioned in  I Corinthians 10:8 , and one thousand who were slain,  Numbers 25:4-5 .

title: Numbers 25:13
text:
Everlasting priesthood; to continue till the end of the Jewish state. 
 
  Made an atonement; did out of regard to which God spared the rest of the people.

title: Numbers 25:15
text: The higher the station and the greater the influence of those who commit iniquity, the greater the evil and the more necessary their punishment.

title: Numbers 25:17
text: Vex--and smite; destroy them.

title: Numbers 25:18
text:
For Peor's sake; because they worshipped Baal-peor. 
 
Tempters to iniquity are among the most dangerous and destructive enemies, and, as far as may be consistent, should be avoided and put away.

title: Numbers 26:53
text: The land; Canaan.

title: Numbers 26:64
text: As the murder of one man is a sin so great as justly to incur the penalty of death, how great must be the evil of sin, which has caused the death of millions, and will cause the death of millions more; and how great the guilt of those who love and practise it, and thus unite with him who was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth.   John 8:44

title: Numbers 26:65
text:
Not left a man; except the two mentioned, and also some of the tribe of Levi, who were not included in the numbering referred to in  Numbers 26:64 . 
 
The declarations of God will in due time all be accomplished, and those who cleave to him and obey his commands will be graciously remembered and recieve an abundant reward.

title: Numbers 27:3
text: As the cause of every death and of all our evils is sin, all our sufferings should lead us more and more to abhor and forsake it.

title: Numbers 27:5
text: In all cases of difficulty we should look to God, and seek that direction from him which we need.

title: Numbers 27:11
text: A statute of judgment; a permanent regulation.

title: Numbers 27:12
text: Abariam; a range of mountains on the east of Jordan; one of these was mount Nebo, a summit of which it is supposed was Pisgah, where Moses stood when he viewed the land of Canaan.   Numbers 21:20 Deuteronomy 3:27

title: Numbers 27:13
text: However much any one may be favored of God, however useful he may be, or however long he may live, the time will soon come when he must die, and leave all the concerns of this world to others.

title: Numbers 27:14
text: Ye rebelled;

title: Numbers 27:16
text:
Set a man over the congregation; to succeed Moses as their leader. 
 
A pious man earnestly desires the spiritual benefit of those who may survive him, and will be much in prayer that, after his decease, God will continue to bless them with all needed good.

title: Numbers 27:18
text:
The spirit; the Spirit of God. 
 
  Lay thy hand upon him; in token of his being appointed as leader of Israel, and endued with the Holy Spirit to fit him for his office.

title: Numbers 27:21
text: Rulers who seek the teaching of the Holy Spirit, who know their duties, and are faithful in the discharge of them, are great blessings to the people.

title: Numbers 27:23
