text: Gave him a charge; instructed him as to his duties, and exhorted him to the faithful discharge of them.

title: Numbers 28:2
text:
In their due season; according to the will of God, heretofore or hereafter made known. 
 
No engagements for this world should induce us to neglect the ordinances of religion, or to fail to observe, at the proper time, the divinely appointed means of grace.

title: Numbers 28:5
text: An ephah--a hin;  Exodus 29:1

title: Numbers 28:9
text: While it is our duty daily to read the Scriptures and pray, as individuals and families, we should on the Sabbath give special attention to these duties, and also worship God in public with the assembly of his people.

title: Numbers 28:10
text: Continual; daily.

title: Numbers 28:11
text:
Months; these began with each new moon. 
 
The Lord has appointed the sun and moon for seasons; and the beginning of every day, month, and year, should remind us of our obligations to him, and lead us to devote ourselves anew to his service.

title: Numbers 28:13
text: A several tenth-deal; one for each lamb.   Numbers 28:21 Numbers 28:29

title: Numbers 28:16
text: In all our religious exercises we should have reference to the atonement of Christ, and place our reliance on him and what he has done for acceptance with God.

title: Numbers 28:26
text: After your weeks; after seven weeks from the second day of the passover, when the feast of weeks, or Pentecost, was celebrated.

title: Numbers 29:1
text: The seventh month;  Leviticus 23:23-27:34

title: Numbers 29:11
text:
Beside the sin-offering of atonement; that is, besides the special sin-offerings appointed for this day, which was the great day of atonement.  See  Leviticus 16:3 , etc., compared with  Numbers 29:29-34 . 
 
The frequency with which the atonement of Christ is brought to view, in both the Old Testament and the New shows its importance in the system of mercy which God has devised for the salvation of men, and the necessity of relying upon it in order to obtain pardon and eternal life.

title: Numbers 29:39
text: True love to God will lead men not only to attend habitually and conscientiously on the appointed means of grace, but cheerfully to present to him freewill offerings of prayer, alms, thanksgiving, and praise.

title: Numbers 30:2
text:
He shall not break his word; provided the thing which he vowed or promised to do is practicable, and not morally wrong: but if the thing promised is wicked, he must repent of his sin in promising; for the sin in this case is in the promise, and not in breaking it.  Matthew 14:7-10 Acts 23:12  
 
A man may solemnly engage to do a wicked thing, but no engagement can lay him under any obligation to do it; and if he does it, it will be at the peril of his soul.  But if the thing which he has engaged to do is not wicked, and is practicable, he must not break his engagement, even if the fulfilment of it should injure himself.   Psalms 15:4

title: Numbers 30:4
text: Shall stand; be binding on her.

title: Numbers 30:5
text: The Lord shall forgive her; for not doing as she had promised.

title: Numbers 30:8
text: It is the will of God that there should be in all families conjugal and parental government and control; and relative duties are so important, that no vows or covenants into which any one can enter, can release him or her from obligations to perform them.  Those, therefore, who induce persons to shut themsleves up in nunneries, or to neglect relative duties, that they may control their persons or their money, are blind leaders of the blind--men who make void the commandment of God through their traditions.   Matthew 15:3-6

title: Numbers 30:9
text: Shall stand; because she had a right to bind herself, and no one had a right to forbid it.

title: Numbers 30:10
text: If she vowed; if the widow or divorced wife vowed before her separation from her husband.

title: Numbers 30:15
text:
Make them void; by hindering her from performing what he had previously allowed her to promise. 
 
  Bear her iniquity; be punished as the woman would have been if she had wilfully broken her promise. 
 
No conjugal, parental, ecclesiastical, or civil authority can in any case bind a person to commit sin; and if any attempt it, they rebel against the authority of God, and expose themselves to his just indignation.

title: Numbers 31:2
text:
Avenge--of the Midianites; punish them for tempting Israelites to sin, and thus causing their destruction.   Numbers 25:1-9 Numbers 25:17-18  
 
Vengeance belongeth unto God.  It is his prerogative to punish the guilty; and when he requires a magistrate to put the guilty to death, it is not the wrath of the magistrate which is manifested, but the wrath of God--designed for a terror to evil-doers, and a protection and encouragement to those who do well.

title: Numbers 31:3
text: Avenge the Lord; execute his just indignation.

title: Numbers 31:6
text: The holy instruments; what these were, aside from the trumpets, is uncertain.  Some propose to render, "with the holy instruments, even the trumpets."

title: Numbers 31:7
text:
Slew all the males; that is, all the adult males taken in war.  We cannot understand in this narrative a general extermination of the Midianites, since we find them afterwards warring against Israel.  The slaughter seems to have been confined to the five neighboring tribes that were involved in the sin of Baal-peor.  Other and distant tribes may have been left unmolested. 
 
It is as really righteous in God to destroy wicked men by the sword of the magistrate as by earthquake, pestilence, fever, or any other calamity.

title: Numbers 31:8
text: Balaam;  Numbers 22:1 Hebrews 1:1-13:25 He who tempts men, or induces others to tempt men to commit sin, must expect a most fearful retribution.   Revelation of John 2:14

title: Numbers 31:16
text: Through the counsel of Balaam;  Numbers 25:1-3 II Peter 2:1

title: Numbers 31:17
text: In putting men to death, magistrates may be obeying God; and not to do it when he commands, is rebellion against him.

title: Numbers 31:18
text: Keep alive for yourselves; to be their servants.

title: Numbers 31:19
text: Purify--yourselves;  Numbers 19:11-22:1

title: Numbers 31:23
text: The water of separation;  Numbers 8:1

title: Numbers 31:24
text: Our best services, even our most hearty obedience to God, are imperfect and polluted with sin; and we need in every thing the purifying influences of the Holy Ghost.

title: Numbers 31:28
text: We should ever acknowledge God as the giver of all our mercies, and a portion of all we obtain by following his directions should be devoted to his worship and service.

title: Numbers 31:47
text: God is the rightful owner of all things, and in taking, at his command, the possessions of their enemies, the Israelites were not guilty of robbery, but rightfully obtained from God that portion of his property which he was pleased in this way to give them.   Psalms 44:3

title: Numbers 31:50
text:
An oblation; an offering of gratitude for their preservation and success. 
 
  To make an atonement; this offering of the officers prefigured the atonement of Christ, and showed their need of his salvation. 
 
Special favors from God should be acknowledged with special thanksgiving, and with hearty reliance on the atonement of Christ as the meritorious cause of all our mercies.

title: Numbers 32:1
text: The land of Jazer, and--of Gilead; east of Jordan, between the rivers Arnon and Jabbok.

title: Numbers 32:4
text: In selecting a place of residence, men often regard land, cattle, merchandise, and other earthly treasures, more than religious privileges, the favor of God, and treasures in heaven.

title: Numbers 32:8
text: Thus did your fathers;  Numbers 13:2-20:1

title: Numbers 32:15
text: By discouraging men from pursuing the path of duty, persons may be the means of destroying not only themselves, but multitudes of their fellow men.

title: Numbers 32:18
text: Kind remonstrances and timely explanations remove misunderstandings, and prevent multitudes of evils.   Psalms 141:5 Proverbs 10:17 Proverbs 12:1 Proverbs 13:18   Proverbs 15:5 Proverbs 15:10 Proverbs 15:31 Proverbs 15:32 Proverbs 17:10

title: Numbers 32:19
text: Yonder side; the west side.

title: Numbers 32:22
text: Readiness to be satisfied with suitable explanations and with good reasons, is an indication of sound judgment, benevolent feeling, and an honest heart.

title: Numbers 32:23
text:
Your sin will find you out; it will bring punishment upon you. 
 
The idea that men may be selfish and continue in sin, and yet escape punishment, is vain.

title: Numbers 32:27
text: In promoting the cause of God and of human welfare, all should be disposed to bear their proportion of needful burdens, sacrifices, and labors.

title: Numbers 32:30
text: Among you; with the rest of the tribes on the west of Jordan.

title: Numbers 32:33
text:
Kingdom of Sihon; lying east of the Jordan near its mouth. 
 
  Kingdom of Og; a country north of Gilead, and east of the sea of Galilee. 
 
When God in his providence deprives one people of their possessions and gives them to another, he only does what he will with his own.  For all his dealings he has the wisest and best reasons, and he never afflicts individuals or nations beyond what their iniquities deserve.

title: Numbers 33:1
text:
The journeys of the children of Israel; the places mentioned from  Numbers 33:3-49 , are those through which the Israelites passed during their wanderings in the wilderness, and on their way from Egypt to Canaan. 
 
Human life is a journey from the cradle to the grave, and each day carries us one day nearer to our final, our eternal abode.

title: Numbers 33:2
text: It is often useful to look back on the various stages of our past life, to recount the goodness of God, and sometimes to write down portions of our history for the benefit of others.

title: Numbers 33:49
text: However long our journey, or whatever be our course through time, we shall soon come to its close and pass into eternity.

title: Numbers 33:52
text:
Pictures; sculptured figures used, as well as the "molten images" or idols, for idolatrous purposes. 
 
Occasions of sin, temptations to evil, and whatever tends to draw our hearts from God and unfit us for heaven, should be carefully avoided.

title: Numbers 33:55
text:
Pricks--and thorns; sources of vexation and distress. 
 
Our fleshly lusts and sinful habits of every kind are to our souls what the Canaanites were to the ancient Israelites.  If we spare them, or continue to indulge them, they will continue to torment us, and ultimately prove our ruin.

title: Numbers 33:56
text: Do unto you, as I thought to do unto them; expel you from your country and destroy you.

title: Numbers 34:2
text: God assigns to individuals and to nations the bounds of their habitation, and they possess no rights, privileges, or blessings, but what they receive from him.  They hold them by his permission, and subject at all times to his disposal.

title: Numbers 34:3
text:
From the wilderness of Zin--Edom; he begins with the south-eastern border where the wilderness of Zin lay. 
 
  The outmost coast of the salt sea; rather, "from the outmost coast of the Salt sea," that is, starting from the extreme southern bay of the Dead sea.

title: Numbers 34:4
text:
Ascent of Akrabbim; a line of cliffs six or seven miles south of the Dead sea. 
 
  Kadesh-barnea; about twenty-six miles a little west of south from the Dead sea.  From this point the border turned westward, reaching the Mediterranean at the river of Egypt, that is, the modern El-Arish and ancient Rhinocolura, south-west of Gaza.

title: Numbers 34:6
text: The western border; of Canaan, was the Mediterranean, from the river of Egypt, in latitude about thirty-one degrees, to a point a little above Zidon, in latitude between thirty-three and thirty-four degrees north.  Its average length was about one hundred and sixty miles.

title: Numbers 34:7
text:
vv 7-9. 
 
  Your north border; from the Mediterranean sea to mount Hor; supposed to be a summit or spur of mount Lebanon. 
 
  Hamath; a city and region of Syria on the Orontes, which was approached on the south by a pass in the mountain called the entering in of Hamath.   I Kings 8:65  
 
  Zedad--Ziphron--Hazar-enan; places further east.

title: Numbers 34:10
text:
vv 10-11. 
 
  East border--Riblah; on the Orontes, some distance south of Hamath. 
 
  Chinnereth; the lake of Gennesaret, or sea of Galilee, which, with the river Jordan and Dead sea, formed the eastern border.  The land of Canaan, upon an average, was about fifty miles wide.  It lay between thirty-four and thirty-seven degrees east longitude, and contained about eight thousand square miles.  A portion of the northern part, as here marked out, was never permanently possessed by the Israelites.

title: Numbers 35:2
text: Suburbs; the land around and near a city.

title: Numbers 35:4
text: A thousand cubits; about fifteen hundred feet.

title: Numbers 35:5
text: Two thousand cubits; this may be best understood of the extent of the sides of the suburb belonging to each city.

title: Numbers 35:6
text: Cities for the refuge; cities to which he who had killed a man might flee and be safe, till he could have a fair trial, and it be proved whether or not he intended to kill the man.  If he did, he was to be put to death,  Numbers 35:30-33 ; if he did not, he must stay in the city of refuge till the death of the high-priest, and after that he might go at large.   Numbers 35:11 Numbers 35:25-28

title: Numbers 35:7
text: A comfortable maintenance for the ministers of religion and their families is required by God in the Old Testament and in the New.  I Corinthians 9:14

title: Numbers 35:11
text: At unawares; without intending it.

title: Numbers 35:12
text:
The avenger; the nearest relative of him who was killed, and who, if he could find the manslayer out of the city of refuge would kill him. 
 
He who is charged with killing a man, or is supposed to have done it, should have a speedy and fair trial.  If he with malice intended to kill him, he is a murderer, and should himself be put to death.  If he did not, he should be acquitted.

title: Numbers 35:14
text:
This side; east side, where the Israelites then were. 
 
  In the land of Canaan; on the west side of the Jordan.

title: Numbers 35:24
text: The intention and the feelings with which an action is done give it its character.  Two men may sometimes perform the same outward act, and one be guilty and the other innocent.  Careful discrimination should therefore be made in such cases, and each treated according to the true character of his deeds.

title: Numbers 35:27
text: Not be guilty of blood; not be punished as a murderer.

title: Numbers 35:33
text: Murder is a great crime, not only against the person who is killed, but against the community and against God.  It pollutes the land, and exposes those who dwell in it to the judgments of God.  This exposure cannot be removed without the death of the murderer.  Hence, it becomes a public duty to put him to death.  Instead of being, as some contend, wrong, it is required by God and is essential in order to escape his judgments.  By protecting criminals we become partakers in their guilt and expose ourselves to share in their punishment.

title: Numbers 35:34
text: I the Lord dwell among the children of Israel; this he did in a peculiar manner, and especially by the visible manifestations of his presence and glory.

title: Numbers 36:2
text: Commanded by the Lord;  Numbers 27:1

title: Numbers 36:5
text: It is well to foresee evils to which we are exposed, and as far as practicable, by the use of proper means to provide against them.

title: Numbers 36:8
text: The regulations of the Jews, which were designed to make and keep them a peculiar peole, separate from other nations, are in the Christian dispensation done away.  All nations now are considered as one family; marriage and other connections may be formed with the inhabitants of different countries, the gospel should be preached to all, and individuals and nations do to others as they ought to wish that others should do to them.

title: Numbers 36:13
text:
The judgments; decisions of God concerning the duties, rights, and privileges of his people. 
 
  The plains of Moab; on the east side of Jordan, over against Jericho.  The Moabites had once possessed this country.  It was afterwards taken by the Amorites, and was now in the possession of the Israelites, yet it still retained its ancient name.   Numbers 22:1

title: Deuteronomy 1:1
text: In the plain over against the Red sea--Dizahab; "the plain" is the long narrow valley extending all the way from the sea of Galilee to the Red sea, in the lowest part of which the Dead sea lies.  The Israelites were in this plain opposite Jericho.  They are said to be "over against the Red sea," because they are in the northern part of the plain opposite to the Red sea, which lay at the other end of that plain. This plain is then further described as lying between Paran--the region about Kadesh--on the west, and Tophel on the east in the mountains of Moab.  Several places are then named which skirt the western border of this plain called the Arabah, or of the sea of Akabah, at which its southern extremity terminates.

title: Deuteronomy 1:3
text: Men who have spent their life in the service of God, as they draw near its close may often with great advantage recount the goodness of God, and repeat his commands to those around them.

title: Deuteronomy 1:4
text: Sihon--and Og;  Numbers 21:21-35:1

title: Deuteronomy 1:6
text: Horeb; the general name of the mountains of which Sinai was one.  Numbers 10:11-13

title: Deuteronomy 1:7
text:
The mount of the Amorites; the mountainous region of Canaan, which the Israelites, if obedient to God, would have entered from its southern part near Kadesh.   Numbers 13:17   The Amorites were properly the inhabitants of the mountains, but they are sometimes put in a general sense for all the Canaanitish tribes. 
 
  The plain; see note to  Deuteronomy 1:1 . 
 
  The hills; the mountainous part of Canaan. 
 
  The vale; the level region on the Mediterranean. 
 
  The south; the southern part of the land bordering on the desert. 
 
  The seaside; the coast of the Mediterranean. 
 
  Lebanon--Euphrates; the original grant extended thus far,  Genesis 15:18 ; but the northern and eastern part of this region was never permanently in the possession of the Israelites.

title: Deuteronomy 1:8
text: Unto your fathers;  Genesis 12:7 Genesis 13:14-15 Genesis 15:16

title: Deuteronomy 1:9
text:
vv 9-18. 
 
  Rulers over you;  Exodus 18:17-26:1

title: Deuteronomy 1:11
text: As good men draw near to heaven, they possess, and often manifest and unusual degree of the spirit of heaven, in earnest desires, fervent prayers, and benevolent efforts for the good of others.

title: Deuteronomy 1:17
text: Magistrates are God's ministers to execute that part of his government which concerns the temporal rights of men, and as such are bound to be candid and impartial; to decide and act in the fear nad love of God, and according to truth and duty.

title: Deuteronomy 1:19
text:
vv 19-21. 
 
  Kadesh-barnea;  Numbers 13:1

title: Deuteronomy 1:21
text: Great courage is needful in order to be willing, under all circumstances, to obey God.

title: Deuteronomy 1:22
text:
vv 22-45. 
 
  Ye would not go up;  Numbers 14:2-36:13

title: Deuteronomy 1:30
text: None will have courage enough to obey God, except those who put their trust in him.

title: Deuteronomy 1:34
text: God is angry with those who are afraid to obey him.

title: Deuteronomy 1:37
text: To please God, men must be careful not to boast of their own power; or take the glory of what they do to themselves.  As they have nothing good but what God gives them, the glory of their doing good all belongs to him.

title: Deuteronomy 1:39
text: Little children are objects of God's peculiar kindness and care; and though the sins of parents may occasion them great trouble, yet by loving and obeying their Father in heaven they may be delivered from all sorrow, and inherit pure and everlasting joy.

title: Deuteronomy 1:44
text: The Amorites; here a general name for the Canaanitish tribes.  In  Numbers 14:45 , they are called Amalekites and Canaanites.

title: Deuteronomy 1:45
text: Men often weep in view of the evils they have brought on themselves, when it is too late to escape them.  They must trust in and obey God, if they would avoid deep and unavailing sorrow.

title: Deuteronomy 1:46
text: In Kadesh many days;  Numbers 20:1-22:1

title: Deuteronomy 2:1
text:
We turned; from Kadesh-barnea. 
 
  Mount Seir; a range of mountains running from near the south of the Dead sea, towards the eastern branch of the Red sea.

title: Deuteronomy 2:3
text:
vv 3-8. 
 
  Turn you northward--passed by from our brethren--wilderness of Moab; at Kadesh-barnea, Moses requested of the king of Edom permission to pass through his country on the direct way to the plain of Jordan by Jericho.  This would have greatly shortened the route. Being denied his request, he marched south through "the plain," that is, the valley of the Arabah--see note to  Deuteronomy 1:1 --and passed around between mount Seir and the head of the eastern arm of the Red sea, on which Elath and Ezion-geber were situated.  Then he turned northward and skirted along the desert east of mount Seir, here called "the wilderness of Moab."

title: Deuteronomy 2:5
text: Nations, as well as individuals, are bound in all things to obey God; and rulers are to be governed, in public as well as private concerns, by his revealed will.

title: Deuteronomy 2:9
text:
Ar; the capital of Moab, about twenty-five miles south of the river Arnon.   Numbers 21:13-15  
 
The Lord claims, and in his providence exercises, the right of giving any and all portions of the earth to whomsoever he will.

title: Deuteronomy 2:10
text: Emim; the ancient inhabitants of the country which was afterwards possessed by the Moabites.

title: Deuteronomy 2:12
text: When the sins of one nation are full, and have ripened them for ruin, God in righteous judgment often suffers another nation to destroy them and take possession of their country; though none have a right to do this, except at the direction and under the guidance of God.

title: Deuteronomy 2:14
text: Zered; a brook which empties into the south-east part of the Dead sea.

title: Deuteronomy 2:19
text: The children of Ammon; on the east of Jordan, north of the Moabites.

title: Deuteronomy 2:23
text:
Hazerim; a country south and south-west of Gaza. 
 
  Azzah; Gaza. 
 
  Caphtorim; the Philistines. 
 
  Caphtor; supposed by some to be Crete, by others, Cappadocia. 
 
As with individuals so with nations, they rise and fall in succession, according to the wise and good purposes of God.  While the heart of man deviseth his way, the Lord directeth his steps; and though there be many human devices, the counsel of the Lord shall stand.   Proverbs 16:9 Proverbs 19:21

title: Deuteronomy 2:24
text:
The river Arnon; the northern boundary of the Moabites. 
 
  Heshbon; one of the cities of the Amorites.

title: Deuteronomy 2:26
text: The wilderness of Kedemoth; a wilderness north of the river Arnon.

title: Deuteronomy 2:30
text:
Hardened his spirit; by leaving him to follow his own wicked inclinations in fighting against the Israelites. 
 
If men continue to rebel against God, he will finally give them up, and suffer them to pursue their own chosen way of iniquity to their utter ruin.

title: Deuteronomy 2:32
text: Jahaz; a city near the northern frontier of the Moabites.

title: Deuteronomy 2:36
text:
Aroer; a city on the north side of the river Arnon. 
 
  Gilead; the country north of the Amorites.

title: Deuteronomy 2:37
text:
The land of the children of Ammon; east of the Amorites. 
 
  The river Jabbok; that empties from the east into the Jordan, about thirty miles below the sea of Galilee.

title: Deuteronomy 3:1
text:
Bashan; a country north-east of Gilead. 
 
  Edrei; a chief city of Bashan.

title: Deuteronomy 3:3
text: When men refuse to take warning from the destruction of others, and rush on in the same course of transgression, they may expect to come to the same dreadful end.

title: Deuteronomy 3:4
text: Argob; a district of Bashan.

title: Deuteronomy 3:8
text: Mount Hermon; mount Lebanon consists of two nearly parallel ranges, running over against the shore of the Mediterranean north of Palestine; the eastern of these ranges is called Anti-Lebanon.  Mount Hermon branches off from the south end of the Anti-Lebanon range, near the borders of Galilee.

title: Deuteronomy 3:11
text:
Of giants; of the rephaim or giants here spoken of. 
 
  Nine cubits; thirteen and a half feet. 
 
  Four cubits; six feet. 
 
  The cubit of a man; this expression seems to mean, the average fore-arm of a man from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger; for from this came the measure of the cubit. 
 
No human arm however strong, if employed against God, can ultimately succeed.  God may suffer his opposers to prosper for a time, while he waits to be gracious; but if his goodness does not lead them to repentance, they will perish.

title: Deuteronomy 3:12
text:
vv 12-20. 
 
  This land--gave I;  Numbers 32:1-33:1

title: Deuteronomy 3:18
text: However great the efforts of the people of God in obedience to his command, their successes are to be ascribed to him, not to their own wisdom, goodness, or power.

title: Deuteronomy 3:21
text: These two kings; Sihon and Og.

title: Deuteronomy 3:26
text:
The Lord was wroth;   
 
With such earthly good things as in the use of proper means God sees fit to bestow, we should be content, and pray that such evils as our sins here bring upon us, may wean us from the world, quicken us in duty, and prepare us for heaven.

title: Deuteronomy 3:27
text: Pisgah; the top of Nebo, one of the summits of mount Abarim.  Numbers 27:12-14

title: Deuteronomy 3:28
text: The good which we cannot do or enjoy, we should rejoice to have done and enjoyed by others; and we should be ready in all proper ways to aid them in doing and enjoying it.

title: Deuteronomy 3:29
text: Beth-peor; meaning, house of Peor; a place in Moab noted for the worship of Peor, or Baal.

title: Deuteronomy 4:1
text:
Statutes and--judgments; the laws which God gave the Israelites concerning his worship and their social and civil duties.  Deuteronomy 4:14  
 
Obedience to the laws of God is required by interest as well as by duty.

title: Deuteronomy 4:2
text: We should take the testimony of God in his word as he has given it, and not be disposed in any respect to alter it.

title: Deuteronomy 4:3
text: What the Lord did;

title: Deuteronomy 4:4
text: God often makes a difference in this world between the righteous and the wicked, and shows by his providence that godliness with contentment is great gain.   I Timothy 4:8 I Timothy 6:6

title: Deuteronomy 4:6
text:
This is your wisdom and your understanding; it would promote their reputation for wisdom and understanding among other nations. 
 
Obedience to God is the height of human wisdom, and all who neglect his commandments are guilty of the greatest folly.   Psalms 14:1

title: Deuteronomy 4:10
text:
vv 10-13. 
 
  In Horeb;  Exodus 20:1 
 
The object of God in the revelation of himself, is not only to lead the present generation to love and serve him, but also to communicate a knowledge of his will to their children and children's children, and thus perpetuate to all generations a people to his praise.

title: Deuteronomy 4:14
text: Statutes and judgments;  Exodus 23:1

title: Deuteronomy 4:16
text: Men are strongly inclined to corrupt themsleves by worshipping idols; serving the creature and neglecting the Creator.

title: Deuteronomy 4:19
text: God hath divided; he had given the benefit of the heavenly bodies to all nations, as well as to the Israelites.

title: Deuteronomy 4:20
text:
The iron furnace; the great oppression and hardship of their state of bondage. 
 
  A people of inheritance; his peculiar people, and heirs of his favor.

title: Deuteronomy 4:22
text:
This land;  Deuteronomy 4:1 
 
True benevolence will teach a man earnestly to desire and diligently to labor, that blessings of which he is deprived may, if consistent, be given to others.

title: Deuteronomy 4:23
text: The covenant;

title: Deuteronomy 4:24
text: Consuming fire--a jealous God; one who is greatly displeased with those who give to others what is due only to himself; and if they do not repent, will destroy them.  De 4.26

title: Deuteronomy 4:31
text: The covenant;  Leviticus 26:42-45 Genesis 15:14-21:1

title: Deuteronomy 4:34
text:
Assayed; attempted. 
 
  Temptations; trials; the mighty works of God, intended to prove the faith of his people.

title: Deuteronomy 4:36
text: His great fire;

title: Deuteronomy 4:41
text: Severed; set apart.

title: Deuteronomy 4:48
text: Sion; called also Sirion, which was another name for Hermon.  Deuteronomy 3:8-9

title: Deuteronomy 4:49
text: Sea of the plain; the Dead sea.  Deuteronomy 3:17

title: Deuteronomy 5:1
text: The great object of attending to and becoming acquianted with the laws of God should be, that we may obey them.

title: Deuteronomy 5:2
text: In Horeb;

title: Deuteronomy 5:3
text: Our fathers; Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

title: Deuteronomy 5:6
text: The Lord ever speaks to his people as if their deliverance from bondage was a great and precious blessing, and one which laid them under new and peculiar obligations to love and serve him.

title: Deuteronomy 5:8
text: Any graven image, or any likeness; to bow down to, adore, or worship.

title: Deuteronomy 5:11
text: In vain; see note to  Exodus 20:7 .

title: Deuteronomy 5:12
text: As the Lord--commanded;

title: Deuteronomy 5:14
text: Servants as well as masters have an inalienable right, and it is their indispensable duty, to rest from their labors on the Sabbath, and to keep it holy: masters are sacredly bound to grant servants liberty and opportunity for this.

title: Deuteronomy 5:15
text:
Therefore the Lord--commanded; this was to the Israelites a reason, in addition to that mentioned,  Exodus 20:11 , why they should keep the Sabbath; and especially why their servants should enjoy its rest and privileges. 
 
The giving of a new reason why men should perform a duty, is no evidence that the duty was not binding before that reason was given or even existed; or that there are not many other reasons for the performance of the duty.   Deuteronomy 24:17-18

title: Deuteronomy 5:16
text: Few duties are more intimately connected with or essential to the prosperity of children, than a kind, affectionate, hearty obedience to their parents.

title: Deuteronomy 5:21
text: It is wrong not only to take what we ought not to have, but even to desire it.

title: Deuteronomy 5:22
text: The obligations expressed in the ten commands, which were written by God on tables of stone, are moral: they arise from the nature of men, and their relations to God and their fellow men; and are binding upon all who know them, in all ages and in all countries.

title: Deuteronomy 5:33
text: Obedience to all the commands of God is conducive to the highest good of men, in this world as well as in the world to come.

title: Deuteronomy 6:1
text: Commandments--statutes--judgments; in this and some other places, commandments seem to mean the moral law, statutes the ceremonal, and judgments the judicial, or civil law.  In other cases they have a more general meaning, and comprehend the whole of God's commandments.

title: Deuteronomy 6:3
text: The commandments of God are all suited to promote industry, economy, temperance, and all those virtues which are conducive to health, long life, wealth, and happiness.

title: Deuteronomy 6:4
text: Though God is revealed as existing in three persons, yet is he one Jehovah.

title: Deuteronomy 6:8
text: Bind them for a sign--frontlets; figuratively spoken in the sense of, make yourselves familiar with them and remember them.

title: Deuteronomy 6:9
text: All are bound to become familiarly acquainted with the commands of God, in order that through divine aid they may habitually and heartily obey them.

title: Deuteronomy 6:12
text: Great prosperity, though it comes from God, is apt, through the wickedness of men, to lead them to forget and rebel against him.

title: Deuteronomy 6:13
text: Swear by his name; in taking an oath on any proper occasion, they were not to appeal to idols or false gods, but only to Jehovah.

title: Deuteronomy 6:14
text: The gods of the people; idols and imaginary deities.

title: Deuteronomy 6:16
text: As ye tempted him in Massah;

title: Deuteronomy 6:20
text: Testimonies; commandments.   Deuteronomy 6:1

title: Deuteronomy 6:21
text: Children are naturally inquisitive, and parents should delight to communicate to them the information they need; expecially with regard to the character, works, and ways of God, that they may understand and do his will.

title: Deuteronomy 6:23
text: The land of Canaan, of which the children of Israel at the command of God took possession, was his gift to them.  In taking it from the Canaanites and giving it to the Israelites, he only did what he saw to be best with his own.

title: Deuteronomy 6:25
text:
Our righteousness; by observing and doing with a proper spirit what God commanded, they would for Christ's sake be accepted and treated as righteous. 
 
The way for men to be treated for Christ's sake as righteous, is to obey God; and they can have no evidence that they are accepted of him, any further than they are disposed to keep his commandments.

title: Deuteronomy 7:2
text:
Thou shalt smite them, and utterly destroy them; the Israelites were the executioners of divine justice upon the Canaanites for their sins. 
 
In putting men to death according to God's directions, it is not needful or right to hate them, or have any unkind feelings towards them; and the idea that capital punishments spring from or imply any such feelings, is a great mistake.

title: Deuteronomy 7:4
text: Chosen and intimate connections with the openly wicked increase our danger of being drawn into sin, and should be carefully avoided.

title: Deuteronomy 7:5
text: Their groves; or, their images of Astarte.

title: Deuteronomy 7:7
text: Fewest of all; when God selected them and made promises to Abraham and his seed, they were very few; nor did they so greatly increase till near the time of their deliverance from Egypt.   Acts 7:17

title: Deuteronomy 7:9
text: The Lord will be faithful in fulfilling his promises to the righteous, and in executing his threatenings against the wicked.

title: Deuteronomy 7:10
text: Repay him to his face; promptly and openly punish him.

title: Deuteronomy 7:14
text: Obedience to God will procure the geatest blessings for this life and the life to come.

title: Deuteronomy 7:19
text: Temptations; trials; miracles by which God proved both Pharaoh and his own people.

title: Deuteronomy 7:23
text: Things which are done by God's direction, and which take place under his guiding and all-controlling providence, are in the Bible often spoken of as done by him.

title: Deuteronomy 7:24
text: The putting of criminals to death according to God's direction, is a proper expression of his just indignation against their sins; and when he commands, it cannot be neglected without disobeying him.

title: Deuteronomy 7:25
text: An abomination; having been used in idol-worship, the Israelites were to treat it with abhorrence, as a testimony against that sin.

title: Deuteronomy 8:2
text:
To know; make known to themselves and to others. 
 
One great object of God in all his dispensations, is to try men and lead them to see and to manifest their true character.

title: Deuteronomy 8:3
text:
By bread only; that is, food produced by natural means. 
 
  By every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Lord; by food miraculously produced by God's powerful word.  The meaning is, that God can supply the wants of his people without the use of natural means, by simply speaking the word.  He is therefore to be trusted for supplies in a desert, as well as in a fruitful land.  See  Matthew 4:4 .

title: Deuteronomy 8:5
text: The Lord never sends trials because he delights in them, but for the profit of his people; that they may be led to feel their dependence, and to exercise those feelings towards him which shall fit them for heaven.

title: Deuteronomy 8:9
text: Brass; or copper, of which brass is chiefly composed.

title: Deuteronomy 8:10
text: In seasons of great prosperity we should feel under special obligations to God, and acknowledge his goodness with special thanksgiving.

title: Deuteronomy 8:14
text:
Thy heart be lifted up; become proud and self-confident.  Deuteronomy 8:17  
 
Great prosperity is peculiarly apt to make men proud, and lead them so to trust in themselves and neglect God and his service, as to harden their hearts and increase their exposure to ruin.   Deuteronomy 8:17

title: Deuteronomy 8:18
text: Power to get wealth, and also liberty to keep and enjoy it, are from the Lord.  For this reason it should ever be viewed as his gift, and employed in promoting his cause.

title: Deuteronomy 8:20
text: However great the goodness of God, and however abundant his promises to any people, continued disobedience will bring upon them irretrievable ruin.

title: Deuteronomy 9:2
text: Anakim; descendants of Anak, son of Arba, and distinguished for their size and strength.   Numbers 13:22

title: Deuteronomy 9:3
text: In the discharge of duty, we should neither despise nor fear our enemies; but putting our trust in God, go forward in humble dependence on him, committing ourselves and all our concerns to his wise and gracious guidance and disposal.

title: Deuteronomy 9:6
text: Men do not receive blessings because of their own worthiness, but on account of the worthiness of Christ, and the abounding grace of God through him.

title: Deuteronomy 9:10
text: The words which the Lord spake;  Exodus 19:18 Exodus 20:1-17

title: Deuteronomy 9:14
text: Should men receive from God their just deserts as sinners, they would all be destroyed.

title: Deuteronomy 9:17
text: Brake them;  Exodus 32:1

title: Deuteronomy 9:19
text: Humble, believing, earnest, persevering prayer has great influence with God, and has often been the means of saving the wicked from destruction.

title: Deuteronomy 9:24
text: No mercies or trials will of themselves remove men's proneness to sin, or prevent their continued and persevering rebellion against God.  He must grant them the influences of his Spirit, or they will perish.

title: Deuteronomy 9:29
text: Prayers which spring from desires to have God honored, and reproaches against him prevented, are the fruit of his Spirit, and are peculiarly pleasing in his sight.

title: Deuteronomy 10:4
text:
The first writing;  Deuteronomy 9:10 Exodus 34:1 
 
The ten commandments express the will of God and the duty of men, and the effect of divine grace is to lead men heartily to love them and strive in all things perfectly to obey them.

title: Deuteronomy 10:6
text:
From Beeroth--Mosera; the Israelites twice marched northward along "the plain" of the Arabah to Kadesh, and thence southward from Kadesh towards the Red sea: 
 
first, in the second year of the exodus,  Numbers 12:1-13:33 . 
 
secondly, in the beginning of the fortieth year of the exodus,  Numbers 20:1-29 . 
 
It is probable that the record of encampments in  Numbers 33:31-33 , belongs to their journey in the second year; and that in the present passage, to their southern journey in the beginning of the fortieth year.  It is to be noticed that when the same route is twice gone over, the sacred writer, as a general rule, names only the more prominent stations.  Mosera, or Moseroth, being in the vicinity of mount Hor, probably at its foot, Aaron may well be said to have died there.

title: Deuteronomy 10:8
text:
At that time; while they were at Sinai.   Numbers 3:1-4:49  
 
It is the will of God that there should be an order of men set apart to minister for him, conduct his worship, proclaim his will, and set before men the motives which he has revealed to induce them to do it.

title: Deuteronomy 10:13
text: The fear and love of God which lead men cheerfully and heartily to obey him, promote not only his glory, but their highest good.

title: Deuteronomy 10:16
text: Circumcise--the foreskin of your heart; break off your sins, and engage heartily in doing the will of God.   Deuteronomy 10:20

title: Deuteronomy 10:17
text:
Regardeth not persons; does not regard men according to outward distinctions, or appearance merely, but according to their true character. 
 
vv 17-19 God is no respecter of persons.  He looks with tender compassion on the stranger, the widow, and the fatherless.  He delights to help them, and requires that all, in this, should imitate his example.

title: Deuteronomy 10:18
text: The judgment of the fatherless; God decides and acts rightly, kindly, and graciously concerning them.  He opens his hand and supplies their wants.

title: Deuteronomy 10:21
text: He is thy praise; the Giver of their mercies, whom they ought to praise.

title: Deuteronomy 11:1
text: Love to God and to men, a disposition to honor him and do good to them, is the essence of true religion.   Matthew 22:36-39

title: Deuteronomy 11:8
text: The dealings of God in past generations form a cogent reason why all men should obey him.

title: Deuteronomy 11:9
text: Floweth with milk and honey; is very fruitful.

title: Deuteronomy 11:10
text: Wateredst it with thy foot; drawing up water from the rivers and fountains by treadwheels, with great labor, to keep the land from drying up for want of rain.

title: Deuteronomy 11:12
text:
Careth for; by granting seasonable rains and rendering it fruitful.  Deuteronomy 11:14-15  
 
Temporal as well as spiritual blessings are the gift of God, and for them men are indebted to his unmerited favor.

title: Deuteronomy 11:17
text: Temporal as well as spiritual judgments are the fruit of sin, and should lead all to hate and forsake it, knowing that if they continue in it, it will prove their ruin.

title: Deuteronomy 11:18
text: Lay up these my words in your heart; remember and obey them.

title: Deuteronomy 11:20
text: Write them; to make them familiar not only to yourselves, but to your children.

title: Deuteronomy 11:21
text:
As the days of heaven upon the earth; that you may continue prosperous and happy to the end of time. 
 
Parents should take measures not only to become acquainted with the commands of God themselves, but to have them deeply impressed on the minds of their children.

title: Deuteronomy 11:23
text: Possess greater nations; the countries of those nations.

title: Deuteronomy 11:24
text:
The wilderness; of Zin, the south border of Canaan. 
 
  Lebanon; the north border. 
 
  Euphrates; the east border. 
 
  The uttermost sea; the Mediterranean, the west border of Canaan.  Numbers 34:1-12

title: Deuteronomy 11:28
text: Life and death are set before men, and the strongest motives presented to induce them to choose life.  If they do, and show this by taking the way that leads to it, they will live.  If they do not, they will die, and the blame will rest wholly on them.  Deuteronomy 30:19 Joshua 24:15 Ezekiel 33:10-16

title: Deuteronomy 11:29
text:
Put the blessing; cause it to be proclaimed.  Deuteronomy 27:12-13 Joshua 8:30-35  
 
  Gerizim--Ebal; these are two steep mountains lying near together. Between them was anciently the city Sychem, or Sichem, also called Sychar.   Genesis 33:18 John 4:5

title: Deuteronomy 11:30
text:
Champaign; "the plain" of the Arabah. 
 
  Gilgal; not the Gilgal where Joshua had his first encampment after crossing the Jordan, but another Gilgal further north, which is named in  Joshua 12:23 . 
 
  The plains of Moreh; or the oaks of Moreh.  See note  Genesis 12:6 .

title: Deuteronomy 12:3
text:
Their groves; or, images of Astarte. 
 
We should put away all things which tend to draw us from the worship and service of God, and encourage all which lead us to cleave to and obey him.

title: Deuteronomy 12:4
text: Not do so unto the Lord; not worship him as the heathen worship their gods, at their own discretion, on mountains and hills, and with images; but carry all your sacrifices and offerings to the one place which he shall choose.

title: Deuteronomy 12:5
text: His habitation; the place where he would dwell with his visible presence.

title: Deuteronomy 12:6
text: Your vows; that is, the offerings which they had vowed to Jehovah.

title: Deuteronomy 12:7
text:
There ye shall eat; according to the directions which God had before given them. 
 
To have our offerings accepted, we must bring them to God in the way of his appointment, in reliance on the atonement and intercession of Christ, and for the purpose of honoring him as well as benefiting ourselves and our fellow men.

title: Deuteronomy 12:8
text: Ye shall not do; as they had done while on their journey, when various things were neglected which they must attend to after they should be settled in the land of promise.

title: Deuteronomy 12:12
text: Sincere and hearty worship of Jehovah is not only highly pleasing to him, but a means of usefulness and happiness to those who present it, and to all connected with them.

title: Deuteronomy 12:15
text:
Kill and eat flesh; for their ordinary food. 
 
  Lusteth after; desireth, if not forbidden by the law of God. 
 
  The unclean and the clean may eat; they might satisfy their hunger on flesh, notwithstanding ceremonial uncleanness. 
 
  As of the roebuck, and--hart; these, though clean animals, were not offered in sacrifice.  The meaning is, that they were as free to kill and eat those animals which were offered in sacrifice, as those which were not offered.

title: Deuteronomy 12:16
text:
Not eat the blood; this was the means and emblem of life; it was offered in sacrifice to God to make atonement for the sins of men, and was not to be eaten, but to be regarded as sacred, in order to increase their conviction of the evil of sin, the justice of God, and their need of pardon. 
 
A deep conviction of the evil of sin, of the justice and mercy of God, and of the necessity and value of the atonement, and a holy regard for divine institutions, should ever be cultivated by all the children of men.

title: Deuteronomy 12:19
text:
Forsake not the Levite; by withholding what belonged to him. 
 
What belongs to God and his ministers should not be withheld or perverted to any other use.

title: Deuteronomy 12:25
text: Subjection of our desires to the revealed will of God, with habitual obedience to his commands, is the way to promote not only our own good, but that of all who come after us or may feel our influence.

title: Deuteronomy 12:32
text: We should not wish to add to or take from what God has said; but should take it as it is, and let it have its proper influence on our hearts and liver.

title: Deuteronomy 13:2
text: Wicked men who give themselves up to the service of the devil, may be suffered by God to do many strange and unaccountable things.  But no one should hearken to them, or in any way give them encouragement.

title: Deuteronomy 13:3
text:
Proveth you; by suffering the false prophets to do some strange and wonderful things, and thus to tempt them to forsake God and worship idols. 
 
God suffers many things to take place in this world to try men, and lead them to show whether they will serve him or not.

title: Deuteronomy 13:5
text: Turn you away from the Lord; as he was the King of the Jews, idolatry was treason, and punishable with death.

title: Deuteronomy 13:8
text: We must not suffer our nearest relatives or most intimate friends to lead us into sin, nor must we in any way connive at their transgressions.

title: Deuteronomy 13:9
text:
Kill him; when proved to be guilty by legal process according to divine directions. 
 
  Be first upon him; the accusers and witnesses were to cast the first stones.   Deuteronomy 17:7

title: Deuteronomy 13:11
text: One object of punishment is to express the wrath of God against crime, and thus restrain others from committing it.

title: Deuteronomy 13:16
text: Burn--every whit; this was to cut off all temptation to avarice, and to express the utmost abhorrence of the crime.

title: Deuteronomy 13:17
text: Men should show a deep abhorrence of crime by suitably punishing it, and in executing God's wrath against the guilty they should, both in reality and in appearance, be influenced only by holy and benevolent motives.

title: Deuteronomy 14:1
text: Not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness; as idolaters were accustomed to do in the worship of their gods.  Leviticus 19:28 I Kings 18:28

title: Deuteronomy 14:2
text: The people of God are called in a peculiar manner to be holy, and should carefully avoid sinful conformity to the world, and all those practices which tend to draw them away from the word and ordinances of Jehovah.

title: Deuteronomy 14:5
text:
Pygarg; a species of antelope or gazelle. 
 
  Wild ox; or, according to some, a species of antelope or mountain goat. 
 
  Chamois; a species of goat.

title: Deuteronomy 14:6
text: The Lord allows us freely to partake of all things which will not injure us, and which tend to our highest good.

title: Deuteronomy 14:13
text: Glede; a species of kite.

title: Deuteronomy 14:15
text: The owl; or, the ostrich.  Several of the names in this list of unclean birds, it is impossible to define with any degree of certainty.

title: Deuteronomy 14:22
text:
Truly tithe; the first tithe or tenth part was devoted to the worship of God and the support of the Levites.  There was a second tithe, a tenth of the nine remaining parts; and once in three years it was to be devoted to the entertainment of the Levites, the stranger, the widow, and the fatherless.   Deuteronomy 14:29  
 
We should endeavor to be truly honest and faithful in devoting to God whatever he requires, and in using all we possess according to his will, remembering that he is the owner, and that we are stewards of what he intrusts to our care.

title: Deuteronomy 14:26
text: Thy soul desireth; in accordance with the revealed will of God.

title: Deuteronomy 14:29
text: The ministers of religion, the stranger, the widow, the fatherless, and all who are destitute should be kindly remembered, and share in the blessings which God graciously gives us.

title: Deuteronomy 15:2
text: A debtor who without his fault is poor, and really not able to pay, should not be imprisoned, nor disabled from making efforts; nor should payment be enforced till he is, or by suitable means may be able to meet it.

title: Deuteronomy 15:3
text:
Thy brother; an Israelite. 
 
While we are bound, as we have opportunity and ability, to do good to all who are needy, we are under special obligations to do it to the friends of God.

title: Deuteronomy 15:9
text: Givest him naught; dost not lend to him what he needs.

title: Deuteronomy 15:10
text: The fact that a man is poor and may not be able to repay, is not to prevent us from lending to him, when it is necessary to relieve hs wants and our doing so will be for his benefit; but we are to love our neighbor as ourselves, and do what such love, under the guidance of sound wisdom, requires.
